data.title: Show HN: Terminal-Bench-RL: Training long-horizon terminal agents with RL
data.author: Danau5tin
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者成功构建了一个基于强化学习（RL）的可扩展基础设施，能够在32块H100 GPU上训练长时程的终端编码代理。该项目基于UC Berkeley Sky Lab的rLLM框架，扩展了自定义环境和基础设施，用于终端代理训练。作者的Qwen3-32B代理在Stanford的TerminalBench榜单上成为表现最好的Qwen3代理，超过了包括GPT-4.1在内的其他代理。然而，由于高昂的计算成本，作者未能进行充分训练，但项目展示了在多节点集群上训练的潜力。项目还包括详细的训练设置、数据集准备、以及未来改进方向，如课程学习和数据集扩展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于强化学习框架的效果、实现细节及其资源限制的讨论

不同观点：
• [tjungblut] 强调了实际强化学习实现的技术基础，指出该系统使用了verl，并推荐了相关论文《HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework》作为深入理解的资源。
• [anorwell] 澄清了对于该提交的一些误解，指出该项目并未涉及训练，仅通过自定义支架（系统提示和工具）利用Qwen3-32B模型在Terminal-Bench上取得了13.75%的成绩，并强调了支架对基准测试结果的重大影响。
• [OtherShrezzing] 对提交者在有限预算下击败GPT4.1的表现表示赞赏，认为这是对大型AI实验室垄断地位的挑战。
• [rboyd] 对项目表示赞赏，并提出了通过众筹方式资助模型训练的可能性，同时询问了关于部分评估和早期停止的技术细节，并寻求当前长时域强化学习的最优资源和论文。
• [lostmsu] 质疑了50k预算的必要性，建议可以使用LoRA进行调优以降低成本。
• [TarasBob] 表示愿意提供资金支持，并已通过邮件联系项目创建者。
• [enigma101] 建议通过Kickstarter克服GPU资源的不足，并认为筹集30至50的资金是可行的。
• [bravesoul2] 对个人独立完成如此规模的项目表示惊叹，强调了跨越多领域技能的难度和成就。
• [thomasfromcdnjs] 直接询问了项目的实际花费。
• [erdaltoprak] 对项目的成果表示难以置信和赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：目前没有明显的争议，但[anorwell]指出了对项目理解上的误区，强调了未涉及训练的事实。
• 资金问题：多个评论提到了项目预算和资金问题，包括对50k预算的必要性、LoRA调优的建议，以及通过众筹或Kickstarter获得资金支持的建议。
• 技术资源：[tjungblut]和[rboyd]提到了技术论文和资源，显示了对强化学习技术细节和最新进展的关注。

🤓 Terminal-Bench-RL: Training Long-Horizon Terminal Agents with Reinforcement Learning
TL;DR:
I successfully built stable RL training infrastructure that scales to 32x H100 GPUs across 4 bare metal nodes for training long-horizon terminal-based coding agents.
In doing so, I developed Terminal-Agent-Qwen3-32b to become the
highest scoring Qwen3 agent on
terminal-bench
. WITHOUT training! (currently under submission):
Unfortunately I am too GPU poor to train a SOTA coding agent 😅 (estimated £30k-£50k in compute required), but if anyone has the GPUs, this project should get you there!
This project builds upon the
rLLM framework
developed by UC Berkeley Sky Lab, extending it with custom environments and infrastructure specifically designed for terminal-based agent training.

💻💰 Training on $1M worth of compute
This image shows my training code running at full throttle on 32x H100's, distributed across a 4x bare metal node cluster, training Qwen3-32B. Thank you
Hyperbolic
for such a streamlined experience! This was fun!
Due to the extreme cost of this level of compute, I was not able to run it forever! So I made sure it worked and also ran the code on less extravagent hardware setups too.
Other training runs
I also ran Qwen3-32B training for longer on a 2x bare metal node cluster with 16x H100s:
Also 1 VM instance with 8x H100s:
My longest training run was using 2xA100s on a single VM instance, where I trained Qwen3-8B for over 60 steps:
Note: I did not expect the 8B to begin learning the complex behaviours required to solve the tasks in the dataset. However it was great to run the training through the dataset and ensure the code is stable.
🏆 Placing a spot on the Terminal Bench Leaderboard
Terminal bench
is a brilliant benchmark created by Stanford and
Laude Institute
to quantify agents' ability to complete complex tasks in the terminal.
Through prompt engineering & custom tool design, my Qwen3-32B agent outperformed Stanford's Terminus-Qwen3-235B-30A MoE agent, as well as Deepseek R1 & OpenAI's GPT-4.1 with Codex agent, to become the highest scoring Qwen3 agent on the leaderboard.
The results.json for the eval run can be found
here
.
I am sure that with the compute budget for training, my agent would climb the leaderboard significantly.
Agent details
My motivation behind this entire project was to place on the leaderboard of terminal bench by using RL to train a sophisticated LLM agent. In order to do so, I developed the tools (inspired by Claude Code) which a capable AI agent would use to help complete complex terminal/coding tasks, as well as a
system message
which encouraged the agent to use those tools and approach the task in a specific way.
These tools can be found
here
and include:
📝 Todo Management
: Planning and tracking task progress
📁 File Operations
: Read, write, and edit files
🔍 Search Tools
: Grep, glob, and ls for file exploration
⚡ Bash Execution
: Run terminal commands wit

data.title: Wikimedia Foundation Challenges UK Online Safety Act Regulations
data.author: Nurw
data.article_summary: 下周，2025年7月22日和23日，伦敦高等法院将审理维基媒体基金会针对《英国网络安全法》分类规定的法律挑战。维基媒体基金会运营着维基百科及其他维基媒体项目，认为该法规威胁到维基百科及全球志愿贡献者的隐私和安全。基金会的法律挑战聚焦于这些新分类规定，这些规定可能对维基百科施加最严格的义务（1类义务），包括验证贡献者身份等，这将增加负担并威胁贡献者的隐私和安全，可能导致数据泄露、骚扰甚至迫害。同时，这也会分散资源，影响维基百科的维护和改进。此案是首次对《网络安全法》分类规定的法律挑战，并有英国维基百科志愿者作为共同原告参与。维基媒体基金会呼吁法院保护维基百科及其贡献者的隐私和安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国《网络安全法》（Online Safety Act, OSA）的合法性、影响以及相关争议

不同观点：
• **对《网络安全法》的全面批评**：
  - 认为该法是政府对个人自由的过度干涉，尤其是对访问社交媒体、游戏聊天等基本服务的限制。
  - 举例：民众不需要为了与朋友交流而提供生物识别信息。
  - 担忧这是政府扩大权力的开始，未来可能进一步收紧。

• **对Wikimedia基金会法律挑战的讨论**：
  - 支持方：Wikimedia基金会的法律挑战是有道理的，因为新法规可能错误地将Wikipedia归类为Category 1，从而施加过于严格的义务。
  - 反对方：认为Wikimedia只是为了自己的利益申辩，其立场并不代表公众利益。同时，挑战的合法性不明，仅因为“不喜欢”该法律不足以构成法律挑战。

• **对具体实施方式的建议**：
  - 认为可以通过家长控制来管理未成年人访问受限内容，而非通过广泛的立法来限制所有用户。
  - 主张家长应承担管理孩子上网行为的责任，而不是依赖大科技公司。

• **对VPN和其他潜在限制的担忧**：
  - 提到英国工党正在考虑禁止VPN，进一步引发对网络自由的担忧。
  - 认为这些措施是逐步限制网络自由的开端。

补充讨论：
• **对法律细节和可行性的质疑**：
  - 有人指出《网络安全法》的条文过长且不清晰，难以理解具体责任。
  - 认为即使Wikimedia成功挑战次要法规，也不会影响主要立法内容，尤其是关于年龄验证的部分。

• **对集体抵制的设想**：
  - 建议若大多数网站集体屏蔽英国用户，可能会迫使政府撤销该法律。
  - 认为任何配合该法律的公司都是对自由互联网的背叛。

争议焦点：
• 《网络安全法》是否构成对个人隐私和网络自由的过度干涉。
• Wikimedia基金会的法律挑战是否基于合法理由，还是仅为了自身利益。
• 家长控制与立法限制之间的平衡点应如何把握。

总的来说，讨论围绕《网络安全法》的合法性、实施细节以及对网络自由的潜在影响展开，各方立场不一，争议较大。

44721403.article_content:
17 July 2025
— Next week, on 22 and 23 July 2025, the High Court of Justice in London will hear the Wikimedia Foundation’s
legal challenge
to the
Categorisation Regulations
of the United Kingdom (UK)’s Online Safety Act (OSA).
The Wikimedia Foundation, the non-profit that operates Wikipedia and other
Wikimedia projects
, announced its legal challenge earlier this year, arguing that the regulations endanger Wikipedia and the global community of volunteer contributors who create the information on the site.
“The Court has an opportunity in this case to set a global precedent for protecting public interest projects online,” said
Stephen LaPorte
, General Counsel at the Wikimedia Foundation. “Wikipedia is the backbone of knowledge on the internet. It’s the only top-ten website operated by a non-profit and one of the highest-quality datasets used in training Large Language Models (LLMs). We trust the Court will protect Wikipedia—a vital encyclopedic resource—from rules crafted for the internet’s riskiest commercial sites and, in doing so, safeguard the open internet for everyone”.
Information on Wikipedia is written and curated by a global community of nearly 260,000 volunteer contributors. These volunteers set and enforce policies to ensure that information on the platform is fact-based, neutral, and attributed to reliable sources. Over the last 25 years, this human-centered content moderation model has established Wikipedia as an unparalleled resource for reliable information in over 300 languages; its 65 million articles are viewed more than 15 billion times per month worldwide.
The Wikimedia Foundation shares the UK government’s commitment to promoting online environments where everyone can safely participate. The organization is not bringing a general challenge to the OSA as a whole, nor to the existence of the Category 1 duties themselves. Rather, the legal challenge focuses solely on the new Categorisation Regulations that risk imposing Category 1 duties (the OSA’s most stringent obligations) on Wikipedia.
If enforced on Wikipedia, Category 1 demands would undermine the privacy and safety of Wikipedia’s volunteer contributors, expose the encyclopedia to manipulation and vandalism, and divert essential resources from protecting people and improving Wikipedia, one of the world’s most trusted and widely used
digital public goods
.
For example, the Foundation would be required to verify the identity of many Wikipedia contributors, undermining the privacy that is central to keeping Wikipedia volunteers safe. In addition to being exceptionally burdensome, this requirement—which is just one of several Category 1 demands—could expose contributors to data breaches, stalking, lawsuits, or even imprisonment by authoritarian regimes. Additional details about the concerning impacts of the Category 1 duties on Wikipedia are available in this
blog post
.
The Wikimedia Foundation will be joined in the case by longtime UK-based volunteer Wikipedia contributor
User:Zzuuzz
as a joint claimant. Their voluntary participation highlights what is at stake in this case for the everyday people who read and contribute to Wikimedia projects. It presents the perspective of a Wikipedia volunteer on how the OSA Categorisation Regulations directly threaten the ability of contributors to participate in knowledge sharing on Wikipedia, as well as compromising their rights to privacy, safety, free speech, and association.
The legal challenge is the first to be issued against the OSA’s Categorisation Regulations, as well as the first with a volunteer Wikipedia editor participating as a joint claimant. It follows years of dialogue with regulators and policymakers, in which the Foundation expressed its concerns, as well as
warnings from the UK Parliament
and
civil society
.
“Our concerns on the looming threats to Wikipedia and its contributors remain unaddressed”, said Phil Bradley-Schmieg, Lead Counsel at the Wikimedia Foundation. “We are taking action now to protect Wikipedia’s volunteers, as well as the global accessibility and integrity of free knowledge. We call on the Court to defend the privacy and safety of Wikipedia’s volunteer contributors from flawed legislation”.
Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects are safe and important resources through which people across the UK—and the wider world—learn, share knowledge, collaborate, and gain media literacy. Thousands of volunteer Wikipedia contributors are based in the UK, and Wikipedia hosts content from cultural institutions such as the British Library and Wellcome Collection. Content on Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects was viewed 776 million times last month in the UK alone. Moreover, Wikipedia is used to preserve and promote cultural heritage in the UK, including Indigenous and minority languages such as Welsh. The
Welsh language version of Wikipedia
is the single most popular Welsh language website in the world and is an
official component of the curriculum
in Wales.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者通过制作电子萤火虫来学习基础电子知识的过程。作者从零开始，学习了无稳多谐振荡器电路，通过不断试错和借助AI与YouTube教程，逐步掌握了电阻、电容和晶体管等基础元件的使用。他解决了让LED灯只在夜间闪烁以及调整闪烁速度的问题，并通过使用电位器精细调节了延迟。作者还制作了基于网页的模拟器和电池寿命计算器工具来辅助设计。在过程中，作者遇到了一些问题，如跳线损坏、电路模拟器不兼容以及焊接烟雾影响呼吸等，但都通过各种方法解决了。最终，他成功制作出了模拟萤火虫的电路，并估算出电池可支持约8个月的使用时间。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：昆虫数量下降与电子电路设计和模拟

不同观点：
• 一些用户关注昆虫数量下降的问题，特别是萤火虫的消失。他们将其归因于光污染和杀虫剂的使用，并引用了相关研究支持这一观点。用户提到德国自然保护区中飞虫数量在25年内减少了四分之三，并讨论了全球昆虫生物量以每年2-10%的速度下降。

• 另一部分讨论围绕模拟电子电路设计的乐趣和挑战展开。有用户赞赏纯粹模拟设计的美学和动手操作的乐趣，认为这种设计比简单使用微控制器更有意义。也有用户分享了自己在学习模拟电路时的困难和领悟，尤其是对LRC电路和晶体管的理解。

• 一些用户则集中讨论电路模拟软件的问题，抱怨许多模拟工具对复杂电路的支持不足，并寻求更好的 hobby-grade 电路设计和仿真软件，尤其是在macOS平台上。

补充讨论：
• 有用户从文化角度出发，将萤火虫的消失与科幻作品中的情节联系起来，讨论人工照明对萤火虫繁殖和交流的影响。

• 关于萤火虫的互动性，有用户提出是否可以利用光敏电阻实现电子萤火虫之间的通信，甚至与真实萤火虫互动。

• 还有用户回忆了过去在电子学学习中的美好经历，并探讨是否可以通过DIY工具将电子萤火虫设计得非常小，接近真实萤火虫的大小。

• 最后，一些用户提到了对电子元件购买渠道的需求，特别是由于Radio Shack的消失，导致在本地购买电子元件变得困难。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于电路模拟软件的有效性，部分用户反映某些仿真软件在处理复杂电路时表现不佳，而其他用户则认为这可能与电路中的寄生参数有关。

44725757.article_content:
Learning Basic Electronics By Building FireFlies
Published:
Jul 28, 2025
|
at
12:00 AM
Disclaimer: this post is written in a raw, unstructured, real-time format and celebrates small wins, honest mistakes, and the messy process of learning and building. It’s not the ultimate guide - just what worked for me, shared as-is. If you like seeing how things break and get fixed, you’re in the right place!
I love fireflies. But in recent years, they stopped coming for reasons I don’t know. No tiny, glowing dots in the dark like they used to. I miss them more than I expected.
Few weeks ago, I decided to make my own fireflies. I discovered something called an
Astable Multivibrator
. It looked like magic to me TBH. A tiny circuit, with
minimal
components, that could automatically switch from ON to OFF and OFF to ON state (without an explicit “timer” component).
But there was one big problem: I didn’t know the first thing about electronics, not even the difference between voltage and current. Plus, now I needed to learn what a resistor, a capacitor, and a transistor is.
It was slow going, but step by step, I picked up the basics. I kept asking AI tools with my questions—sometimes embarrassingly simple ones and slowly, the fog began to lift 😇
Loaded with just enough theory (and a lot of YouTube and AI advice), I took my bike with a shopping list in my pocket and bought my first few components.
Back at home, I assembled my first blinking LED circuit. To my surprise, it worked on the first try!! (even softwares don’t do this, IYKYK 🤷🏼‍♂️).
But somethings still bugged me. One, it blinks all day. Two, the LED blinked too fast. Fireflies don’t blink this fast and they don’t blink all day. These were true deal breakers for me.
I wanted my firefly to only blink at night and slow down the blinking. The first part wud also cut the energy consumption by half. I asked my first question: “How can I make it blink only at night?” Perplexity introduced me to the LDR (Light Dependent Resistor). I was mind-blown. That’s exactly what I needed. I couldn’t believe it. It sounded like AI hallucination to me at that time TBH. Just to be sure, I checked if LDRs are real. They are! I jumped on my bike and rushed to the shop again. Got few. Soldered one into my circuit.
It did NOT work! I realized I connected it wrong (my bad, Perplexity’s bad, or maybe we both 🤷🏼‍♂️). Once I hooked it up correctly, it was like magic: the LED would stay ON only in the dark. Even better, I learned I could adjust the sensitivity by adding a resistor in series with the LDR.
To fine-tune the blink delay, I discovered I can tweak the capacitor and resistor values. But trying resistors one by one felt like a boring task. I discovered something called a Potentiometer that’s more like a dynamic resistor that has a knob you can twist to increase and decrease the resistance. Guess what? Took the bike, bought it, connected it, and found the sweet spot. I swapped out a 100kΩ resistor for the sweet spot 500kΩ and noticed the interval between blinks stretched from 1 to 5 seconds. I experimented with different capacitor values also and, after a lot of trial and error, even built my own little web-based simulator to predict blink delays ->
https://a64.in/tools/astable-delay-simulator.html
(I guess the software guy in me couldn’t rest!).
After that, I wanted to verify if my resistor and capacitor values were optimal. I learned how to measure power consumption with a multimeter and discovered that using a lower-value capacitor and higher resistance was best. I built another calculator ,
https://a64.in/tools/battery-life-calculator.html
, to estimate how long my “firefly” would glow before the battery died — it showed over ~8 months, by my math.
But the road was not always smooth 🥲
Incident#1:
My circuit stopped working. I tested all the components one by one — everything was working. Losing hope, I went to bed. The next morning, I thought: “What if it’s not the components—what if it’s the wires?” I tested each jumper wire and some of them were broken or had high resistance (I don’t think I’ll ever be able to trust jumper wires ever again :(). From then on, I began using “hookup wires”.
Incident#2:
I missed having a simulator, so I searched the web and found tinkercad.com has a circuit simulator where you can drag and drop all the components and see if and how it works. It worked for simple circuits, but for mine, the astable multivibrator, it didn’t for some reason. I tried
falstad.com/circuit
; the same thing happened. It also didn’t work. I searched the web for the reason, and I’ve noticed that sometimes these simulators don’t work well for complex circuits.
Incident#3:
The solder smoke. It was causing breathing issues (or at least I felt a difference in breathing after soldering). To help with that, I ripped out a cooler fan from an old CPU and connected it with a 12v spare adapter and used it as a fume extractor (or redirector? I don’t know what you call it).

data.title: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024: WebAssembly SDK
data.author: breve
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了WebAssembly（WASM）在Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024中的应用，特别是从DLL插件转向WASM模块的过程。为了兼容现有插件，Visual Studio引入了一个新的工具集，支持将C/C++项目直接编译为WASM，并提供调试功能。WASM模块在游戏中并非解释执行，而是提前转换为原生代码（如DLL）。文章还澄清了WASM模块在非网页环境下的运行误解，并提供了使用WASM创建仪表、系统、机场等的教程。

SDK提供了多个API头文件，如MSFS.h、MSFS_Core.h等，用于开发WASM模块。其中，Gauge API已成为遗留API，建议使用Vars API和Event API。Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024对WASM模块的运行进行了改进，模块可在不同线程上运行，提高了性能，但需要注意文件读取和SimConnect结构变化等问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软飞行模拟器2024（MSFS2024）的技术实现、性能问题及未来技术方向（如WebAssembly的应用）

不同观点：
• **对MSFS2024技术实现的负面评价**：
   - [shizcakes] 提到游戏经常崩溃，性能问题严重，玩家反馈非常负面。
   - [avazhi] 认为MSFS2024在流体动力学模拟方面表现不佳，且Asobo在拥有大预算的情况下表现不如预期，2024版尤其让人失望。

• **对错误处理机制的批评**：
   - [affenape] 指出MSFS2024的错误处理不一致，不同功能返回错误的方式不同，建议引入类似errno的标准错误处理机制。

• **对WebAssembly（WASM）应用的积极评价**：
   - [two_handfuls] 认为WASM的引入是个好消息，微软团队在这方面投入了很多努力，特别是为了不重写现有插件而设计的新工具集。
   - [diego_moita] 认为WASM作为模块化的解决方案非常有意义，可能成为多种现有技术（如嵌入式脚本语言和插件模块）的竞争者，甚至可能实现跨平台运行的目标。

• **对技术选择的质疑**：
   - [whatever1] 质疑为何不直接为单一平台（Windows）编译插件代码，推测可能是为了未来在其他平台上发布做准备。
   - [boffinAudio] 更倾向于使用Lua字节码作为执行目标，认为这样工具链会更简单高效，且与其他引擎的互操作性更强。

• **对行业趋势的批评**：
   - [naikrovek] 批评行业采用低效方式处理技术问题，尤其是将WASM模块重新编译为DLL的做法。推测这样做可能是为了安全考虑，但批评Nvidia的GPU许可政策阻碍了虚拟GPU技术的发展。

补充讨论：
• **对微软飞行模拟器历史地位的评价**：
   - [CSMastermind] 认为微软飞行模拟器是有史以来最具影响力的游戏之一，可以进入前100名。

• **技术细节的补充**：
   - [Stevvo] 提供了MSFS2024背后使用的技术链接，指出其使用了innative-sdk。

• **对技术讨论的幽默评论**：
   - [thescriptkiddie] 提到某个关于JavaScript作为通用ABI的博客文章其实是讽刺，并提供了一个相关演讲的链接。

争议焦点：
• MSFS2024的性能问题和技术实现上的负面反馈与WASM等新技术的潜在优势之间的矛盾。部分用户对WASM的引入持积极态度，而另一些用户则对其具体实现方式表示质疑和批评。

44695364.article_content:
WEBASSEMBLY (WASM)
In order to provide both security and portability, it was decided to move away from add-ons distributed as
DLL
s in favour of add-ons distributed as
WebAssembly modules
. In order to do so without requiring a full rewrite of existing add-ons, a new platform toolset was designed for Visual Studio with the following capabilities:
Direct compilation of C/C++ projects into WebAssembly (as
WASM
).
Debugging of WebAssembly modules by attaching to the game executable.
Full support for the standard C library.
Large support for the standard C++ library (see below).
GDI+
wrapper based on the NanoVG API to facilitate porting existing add-ons.
â
While WebAssembly itself is
well documented
, there seems to be some confusion as to how WebAssembly modules can be run outside of a web environment. To clear a few misconceptions:
The add-ons developed in WebAssembly for
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
are not interpreted but rather converted to native code ahead of time (as DLLs).
WebAssembly itself doesn't offer API "X", "Y" or "Z" - it is up to its implementation to grant access to these APIs.
â
You can also find a complete tutorial to get you started using WASM for your gauges on the following pages (including information on
Debugging
):
Creating A WASM Project
Creating WASM Gauges
Creating WASM Systems
Creating WASM Airports
Debugging WASM Gauges
â
â
SDK APIs
The API's supplied with the SDK for use in Visual Studio are as follows:
â
MSFS.h
and
MSFS_Core.h
- These are the "base" files that should be included in all projects that are creating WASM gauges. You can find more information here:
Core And Helpers
MSFS_AirportContext.h
- This is the "base" file that should be included in all projects that are wanting to support WebAssembly modules in airports.
MSFS_CommBus.h
- This file corresponds to the
Communication API
.
MSFS_Event.h
- This file corresponds to the
Event API
.
MSFS_GaugeContext.h
- This is the "base" file that should be included in all projects that are creating WASM gauges using the
MSFS 2024
callbacks.
MSFS_IO.h
- This file corresponds to the
IO API
.
MSFS_MapView.h
- This corresponds to the
MapView API
.
MSFS_Network.h
- This corresponds to the
Network API
.
MSFS_PlannedRoute.h
- This corresponds to the
Planned Route API
.
MSFS_Render.h
- This corresponds to the
NanoVG API
.
MSFS_Utils.h
- This is a small library of functions used by several API.
MSFS_Vars.h
- This file corresponds to the
Vars API
.
MSFS_Vector.h
- This is a small library of helper functions for vector maths.
MSFS_Vfx.h
- This corresponds to the
VFX API
.
MSFS_WindowsTypes.h
- This is a library of type definitions for that defines some types used by windows/rendering with their equivalent in WASM.
Legacy/gauges.h
and
Legacy/gps_info.h
- These files are the main gauge API and they have multiple functions related to getting and setting data, rendering, etc... You can find full details here:
Gauge API
.
IMPORTANT!
This API is now considered a
legacy
API and you should be using the
Vars API
for
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
instead.
ââ
â
Upgrade a WebAssembly module from
MSFS 2020
to
MSFS 2024
Unlike
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020
where all WebAssembly modules were run on the main thread,
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
runs WebAssembly modules on different threads (however, each module is still single threaded). Thanks to that improvement, the entire frame can be used to run updates, callbacks... which increases overall performance. Standalone modules will automatically benefit from this improvement, but gauge modules will
not
benefit from the entire feature without changes (see
Creating WASM Gauges
for information). Things to note about the updated WASM modules are as follows:
â
New
WebAssembly Modules Usage
are designed to be used the entire frame.
â
The Gauge API has been deprecated and is now considered a
legacy API
, mainly because its architecture is not compatible with the
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
simulation architecture anymore. However the features provided by this API are still available through the
Vars API
and
Event API
.
â
Standalone modules now have an update callback to avoid having a SimConnect connection used only for this purpose.
â
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
streams a lot of content, including WebAssembly packages of all types. Because of this, dependency files (data, assets...) might not have been downloaded yet when referenced. If a WebAssembly module tries to read a file which has not been downloaded yet (using synchronous
libc
functions to read the file), the module will be "paused" for few frames until the file is ready to be used that in way. To avoid this behavior, we strongly advise you to use the new
IO API
for read purposes.
â

Towards a Periodic Table of System Design Principles
System design is often taught through domain-specific solutions specific to particular domains, such as databases, operating systems, or computer architecture, each with its own methods and vocabulary. While this diversity is a strength, it can obscure cross-cutting principles that recur across domains. This paper proposes a preliminary “periodic table” of system design principles distilled from several domains in computer systems. The goal is a shared, concise vocabulary that helps students, researchers, and practitioners reason about structure and trade-offs, compare designs across domains, and communicate choices more clearly.
1. INTRODUCTION
One of the rewards of working in computer systems is the field’s sheer diversity, spanning operating systems, databases, computer architecture, distributed systems, programming languages, networking, and more, each with a rich history. For newcomers, it can be challenging to spot connections across different domains due to the diversity of traditions and vocabularies: the same design principle may appear in different guises across domains.
For example, consider the classic paper on database isolation levels by Jim Gray et al. [17]. It offers a careful account of concurrency-control mechanisms and the trade-offs between correctness and performance. Yet without prior exposure to similar issues in operating systems or computer architecture, the ideas can appear narrowly “about databases.” In reality, the same design principle, "relaxation of consistency," reappears across systems in different guises, from weakly ordered memory hierarchies to eventual-consistency protocols. When each community uses its own terms and exemplars, newcomers may find it difficult to recognize the underlying design principles. This fragmentation increases cognitive overhead, as the same trade-off must be relearned in each context.
This is a broader pattern: systems research is rich in practical insight but lighter on shared conceptual scaffolding. Across domains, similar challenges recur—managing concurrency, ensuring consistency, and adapting to change—while the framing and vocabulary often differ. As a result, deep connections between seemingly disparate domains can remain relatively obscure.
This article is a small step toward bridging those gaps. Borrowing Mendeleev’s metaphor, we present a "periodic table" of recurring system design principles. The goal is not a rigid taxonomy but a working vocabulary: a concise way to annotate papers, lectures, and design documents with the fundamental principles they employ. The aim is to surface structure that already exists in computer systems, so that students can form a more coherent mental map, researchers can situate contributions with precision, and practitioners can discuss design choices across domains with greater clarity.
2. METHODOLOGY
We identified principles by going over 100+ influential papers across operating systems, computer architecture, databases, networking, programming languages, security, and other domains in computer systems. These papers were chosen for historical significance and ongoing relevance, such as classic papers on concurrency control [17] and consensus [25], and more recent work on using machine learning inside systems [22] and designing systems for the cloud [6].
For each paper we asked: what is the underlying high-level design principle? Across domains, independent systems often converged not on mechanisms but on shared design principles: for example, relaxing consistency to improve performance or lifting abstractions to enhance usability.
To qualify as a system design principle, it must satisfy two conditions:
Abstract
– The principle must be independent of specific technologies or implementations.
Generality
– The principle must show up across different domains (e.g., database systems, operating systems, programming languages).
This analysis does not aim to catalogue every principle, but to surface many of those with lasting, general-purpose value.
3. THE DESIGN PRINCIPLE TABLE
We have curated a structured set of 40+ general-purpose design principles distilled from the systems literature. As shown in Table 1, they are organised into thematic groups that mirror familiar axes of system design.
Each principle is tagged with a short symbol (e.g.,
Co
for composability,
Op
for optimistic design) for quick reference. We emphasi

data.title: Structuring large Clojure codebases with Biff
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: Jacob O'Bryant分享了重写Yakread应用的进展，并探讨如何通过改进Biff（一个Clojure web框架）来更好地管理大型代码库。Yakread原版存在查询缓慢的问题，新方法通过在XTDB上实现物化视图（存储在RocksDB中）来解决，避免了手动去规范化数据模型。每个物化视图由纯函数（denormalizer）定义，Biff自动处理相关操作。测试方面，使用Fugato生成测试数据，并通过“oracle”函数验证物化视图的正确性。此外，所有应用逻辑都是纯函数，通过状态机模式将副作用处理与应用逻辑分离，确保单元测试不依赖副作用，提高了代码的可测试性和可维护性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用Datomic/XTDB数据库时数据去规范化（denormalization）和查询性能的讨论。

不同观点：
• [codemonkey-zeta] 认为，使用Datomic或XTDB的初衷是避免去规范化。他对于原文中提到的查询性能问题表示惊讶，并建议可以通过一个复杂的查询语句来获取所有需要的数据，而不需要对每条订阅单独查询。他提供了一个示例查询，通过逻辑连接（join）操作在一次查询中获取所有订阅的相关信息。

• [4b11b4] 对去规范化提出质疑，似乎在询问是否应该在视图（views）中保持去规范化的数据。这表明他可能在考虑一种混合方法，即在数据库中保持规范化结构，但在视图层进行去规范化处理。

• [tiffanyh] 转移了话题，赞赏网站的网页设计，提到其简洁、信息密集、对比度好。这属于对设计美学的非技术性评价，与主要讨论点无关。

• [aboardRat4] 提到了Biff框架和Comsat，但没有详细阐述自己的观点，可能在暗示是否可以在不使用Comsat的情况下用Biff来解决类似问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该完全避免去规范化。codemonkey-zeta主张通过复杂查询避免去规范化，而4b11b4则似乎在探索视图中去规范化的可能性。
• 另外，tiffanyh的评论表明讨论中存在一些与技术无关的设计审美评价。
• aboardRat4的评论较为模糊，但可能暗示了在技术实现上可以有其他选择。

总结来看，讨论的核心在于数据库查询性能与数据去规范化之间的权衡，以及可能的解决方案（如复杂查询或视图层处理）。

Structuring large Clojure codebases with Biff
Jacob O'Bryant
| 28 Jan 2025
I've been making some progress on rewriting
Yakread
(a
fancy reading app) from ~scratch and open-sourcing it in the process. Along the
way I'm experimenting with potential new features for
Biff
, my Clojure web framework, which Yakread is built
with. In particular I'm working on approaches for keeping Biff apps more
manageable as the codebase grows: the original Yakread codebase was about 10k
lines and was already getting pretty crufty. I've also learned some things from
contributing to our ~85k-line Clojure codebase at work.
I thought it'd be worth going over the main new architectural approaches in
Yakread for anyone interested in poking around the code/as a preview of what to
expect in Biff later on. The
open-source
repo
has only a sliver of the
production app's functionality so far, but it has examples of all the
approaches described below.
Materialized views
"Old Yakread" has a lot of slow queries. For example, loading the subscriptions
page on my account takes more than 10 seconds: for each of my hundreds of
subscriptions, it has to run a query to figure out how many unread posts there
are and when the most recent post was published. This is currently done the dumb
way, i.e. Yakread queries for every single post and then computes the aggregate
data.
The traditional way to solve this would be to denormalize the data model (add
fields for “# unread items” and “last published at” to the subscription model)
and keep it up to date manually (update those fields whenever a new post is
published, whenever the user reads a post, etc). However,
this approach can get
out of
hand
.
I’ve addressed this in a cleaner way by
implementing materialized
views
for XTDB. I store them in a dedicated RocksDB instance. For each piece of
denormalized data you need,
you define a pure "denormalizer"
function
*
which takes in an item from XTDB’s transaction log along with the current
RocksDB state and returns a map of key-value pairs that will be written back to
RocksDB. Biff handles everything else: setting up RocksDB, running your
denormalizer functions whenever there’s a new XTDB transaction, and providing a
RocksDB snapshot for querying that’s consistent with your current XTDB snapshot
(we retain XTDB's database-as-a-value semantics).
*Still deciding on the name... the codebase calls them "indexer" functions
currently, but I decided "materialized views" are a clearer/more accurate term
than "indexes."
This is a lower-level approach than something like
Materialize
, which lets you write regular SQL
queries instead of defining these denormalizer functions (i.e. you’re defining a
function of
current DB state -> materialized view
instead of
new transaction, current materialized view -> new materialized view
). However,
when I experimented with Materialize several years ago I found that its memory
overhead made it untenable for my use case. I’m sure it’s much better for, say,
aggregating metrics from large real-time systems, even if it sadly didn’t work
out for the simplify-random-guy’s-RSS-reader use case. (I’d also like to look
into other things in this space like
Rama
and
Feldera
).
Writing the
incremental view
maintenance
logic
by hand is somewhat tedious, but the testing approach I'm using makes it really
not bad. I’ve
written
code
with
Fugato
that can take the
database schema for your app and generate test data for use with test.check
(Clojure’s property-based testing library). All you have to do is write an
“oracle” function that takes a database snapshot and computes what the
materialized view should look like for that snapshot. e.g. for the “subscription
last published at” materialized view,
the oracle
function
simply gets all the posts for each subscription and then finds the one with the
latest published-at date. Then the testing code ensures that the materialized
view computed by your denormalizer function matches.
Separating application logic from effects
100% of the application code in "New Yakread" is pure. The unit tests never have
to set up mocks or check the results of side effects. Every unit test has the
form “pass some data to this pure function and make sure the output matches this
constant.”
I accomplish this by turning each function with application logic into
a little
state
machine
,
where each state is either a unit of pure computation (app logic) or an effect
handler. Whenever the pure app logic needs to do something effectful, like run
an HTTP request or save something to the database, it returns
some
data
describing the effect, which causes the machine to transition to an effectful
state.
These effectful
states
perform the effects and then transition back to your pure application logic.
They're centralized in one spot in your app, and they’re kept as dumb as
possible: take some input data, do the effect, return the output.
For testing, each pure app logic state can be called individually without
running th

data.title: Linux 6.16: faster file systems, improved confidential memory, more Rust support
data.author: CrankyBear
data.article_summary: Linux 6.16引入了几项重要更新，包括更深入的Rust语言支持，使添加Rust硬件驱动更容易，并提升图形性能和安全性。Rust集成扩展到驱动核心、PCI设备子系统及DRM，减少漏洞并优化GPU性能，使游戏玩家和AI/ML开发者受益。文件系统方面，XFS支持大型原子写操作，提升数据完整性；Ext4通过多项改进，使顺序I/O性能提升达37%。安全方面，支持Intel TXT和TDX及AMD SEV-SNP，增强云环境中的内存加密。此外，新内核支持Intel APX，增加x86寄存器数量，提升性能，并改进对Nvidia Blackwell GPU的支持。网络方面，TCP/IP与DMABUF的改动加速了GPU和AI加速器的网络速度。总体而言，Linux 6.16在性能、安全和Rust支持上均有显著提升。

主要讨论点：Linux内核新特性和技术细节

不同观点：
• arp242对Linux笔记本作为音乐播放器的新功能（在系统休眠时通过USB传输音频）表示困惑，质疑是否仍需要一个程序来播放音乐，并提到缺乏相关细节和资料。
• bpbp-mango对Ext4文件系统的改进表示赞赏，特别是其在顺序I/O工作负载上的速度提升。
• jauntywundrkind对零拷贝网络传输、文件系统Folio工作、IO_Uring和AMDGPU用户队列等新特性表示高度赞赏，并详细列举了各项改进的技术细节和潜在应用。
• remexre质疑Linux支持Intel Advanced Performance Extensions（APX）的说法，认为APX尚未发布。
• tombert对Linus允许Rust进入内核表示惊讶，并期待新版本在NixOS Unstable上的发布。

Linux 6.16 brings faster file systems, improved confidential memory support, and more Rust support
Linux continues to grow bigger and better. Here's what's new and notable in the 6.16 release, plus what you need to know about 6.17.
Written by
Steven Vaughan-Nichols,
Senior Contributing Editor
Senior Contributing Editor
July 29, 2025 at 1:40 a.m. PT
herraez/Getty Images
The changes in the latest Linux kernel,
Linux 6.16
, may be small, but they include some significant ones. Linus Torvalds himself summed up
this release as looking fine, small, and calm
, but not "really not all that interesting (in all the best ways!)."
Here's my list of what's new and improved.
First, the
Rust language
is continuing to become more well-integrated into the kernel. At the top of my list is that the kernel now boasts Rust bindings for the driver core and PCI device subsystem. This approach will make it easier to add new Rust-based hardware drivers to Linux.
Also:
My 5 favorite Linux distros for home office desktops - and I've tried them all
Additionally, new Rust abstractions have been integrated into the Direct Rendering Manager (DRM), particularly for ioctl handling, file/GEM memory management, and driver/device infrastructure for major GPU vendors, such as AMD, Nvidia, and Intel. These changes should reduce vulnerabilities and optimize graphics performance. This will make gamers and
AI/ML developers
happier.
Linux 6.16 also brings general improvements to Rust crate support. Crate is Rust's packaging format. This will make it easier to build, maintain, and integrate Rust kernel modules into the kernel.
For those of you
who still love C
, don't worry. The vast majority of kernel code remains in C, and Rust is unlikely to replace C soon. In a decade, we may be telling another story.
Beyond Rust, this latest release also comes with several major file system improvements. For starters, the
XFS filesystem
now supports large atomic writes. This capability means that large multi-block write operations are "atomic," meaning all blocks are updated or none. This enhances data integrity and prevents data write errors. This move is significant for companies that use XFS for databases and large-scale storage.
Perhaps the most popular Linux file system,
Ext4
,
is also getting many improvements. These boosts include faster commit paths, large folio support, and atomic multi-fsblock writes for bigalloc filesystems. What these improvements mean, if you're not a file-system nerd, is that we should see speedups of up to 37% for sequential I/O workloads.
Also:
I'm a Linux pro - here are my top 5 command line backup tools for desktops and servers
If your
Linux laptop
doubles as a music player, another nice new feature is that you can now stream your audio over USB even while the rest of your system is asleep. That capability's been available in Android for a while, but now it's part of mainline Linux.
If security is a top priority for you, the 6.16 kernel now supports Intel Trusted Execution Technology (TXT) and
Intel Trusted Domain Extensions (TDX)
. This addition, along with Linux's improved support for
AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization and Secure Memory Encryption (SEV-SNP
), enables you to encrypt your software's memory in what's known as
confidential computing
. This feature improves cloud security by encrypting a user's
virtual machine
memory, meaning someone who cracks a cloud can't access your data.
There are several other Linux chip improvements in this release. For starters, Linux now supports
Intel Advanced Performance Extensions (APX)
. With APX, Linux can now use 32 general-purpose x86 registers. That's double older chips' 16 registers. This improvement means you'll see increased performance from next-generation Intel CPUs, such as the Lunar Lake processors and the Granite Rapids Xeon processors.
You'll also be able to access this improved processor performance via the new
CONFIG_X86_NATIVE_CPU option
. This option enables users to build kernels optimized specifically for their processor. While some people view this move as a way for Linux hobbyists to get the most power from their laptops and desktops, I also see it as a means for business developers to create optimized Linux kernels for their servers.
Also:
8 things you can do with Linux that you can't do with MacOS or Windows
Linux 6.16 brings improved support for
Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs
. The
Blackwell chips, used mostly for AI, are already being deployed in high-end Linux desktops
.
On the network front, changes to how TCP/IP works with
DMABUF
will enable devices, including GPUs and AI accelerators, to speed up their networks while not burdening the CPU. While an average user may not notice this change, high-performance networkers will see the acceleration.
And chances are that average users will see the benefits if they use
OpenVPN
. OpenVPN's native networking protocol still won't run as fast as
WireGuard
, but it will, at least, g
44726551.article_summary: Linux 6.16引入了几项重要更新，包括更深入的Rust语言支持，使添加Rust硬件驱动更容易，并提升图形性能和安全性。Rust集成扩展到驱动核心、PCI设备子系统及DRM，减少漏洞并优化GPU性能，使游戏玩家和AI/ML开发者受益。文件系统方面，XFS支持大型原子写操作，提升数据完整性；Ext4通过多项改进，使顺序I/O性能提升达37%。安全方面，支持Intel TXT和TDX及AMD SEV-SNP，增强云环境中的内存加密。此外，新内核支持Intel APX，增加x86寄存器数量，提升性能，并改进对Nvidia Blackwell GPU的支持。网络方面，TCP/IP与DMABUF的改动加速了GPU和AI加速器的网络速度。总体而言，Linux 6.16在性能、安全和Rust支持上均有显著提升。

data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文简要列出了与YouTube及其相关服务有关的各类信息和资源。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻、版权说明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者条款、隐私政策、安全政策、YouTube的使用方式、新功能测试、NFL Sunday Ticket等服务，以及版权归属为2025年的Google LLC。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FoundationDB的背景、技术特点、应用情况及社区反馈

不同观点：
• [正面评价] **jauntywundrkind** 认为FoundationDB将数据库职责分解为多个部分是非常合理的，有助于每个部分的扩展。他还赞扬了其制作价值和测试方法的先进性，提供了相关链接供参考。
• [技术演示影响] **romanhn** 提到2014年的一场开发者大会演示让他对FoundationDB印象深刻，特别是其在机器故障时的数据再平衡能力，相比当时分布式Cassandra的挑战，FoundationDB的表现非常突出。
• [收购后的疑虑] **gregoriol** 表示对FoundationDB被Apple收购后的维护状况感到担忧，认为被Apple收购的项目通常缺乏长期维护或发生巨大变化，这对打算使用该技术的开发者来说是一个警示。
• [技术发展] **pjmlp** 提到FoundationDB正在被重写为Swift，并提供了相关演讲链接，讨论了Swift作为C++继任者在FoundationDB中的应用。

补充讨论：
• [对测试改进的赞赏] **vlovich123** 对FoundationDB在发现关键缺陷后仍坚持改进测试表示赞赏，并提到虽然未能被Snowflake保留，但催生了Antithesis服务，算是有积极的结果。
• [应用规模和场景] **msy** 询问FoundationDB在Apple内部的使用情况，特别是与Cassandra集群的区别；**Nican** 则好奇FoundationDB的规模限制，比如是否能存储所有Discord消息，并提到Discord转向Scylla和ElasticSearch。
• [市场表现和评价] **piokoch** 认为FoundationDB在市场上没有像MongoDB那样获得巨大关注，质疑这是否是由于炒作或其实际表现不如宣传。
• [实际应用案例] **philosopher1234** 希望了解使用FoundationDB构建的实际项目案例。
• [视频中人物关系] **majestik** 注意到视频中两个人的互动有些紧张，猜测他们之间是否存在某种背景故事。

争议焦点：
• FoundationDB被Apple收购后的长期维护和变化不确定性是社区关注的焦点，部分用户对此持怀疑态度。

data.title: A month using XMPP (using Snikket) for every call and chat (2023)
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 作者在一个月内使用XMPP（通过Snikket）与妻子进行所有通话和聊天。之前他们使用Matrix，但因音视频通话不稳定和加密问题，转向了XMPP。最初使用Prosody时，消息功能良好，但iPhone上的实时通知和来电通知不理想。安装Snikket后，音视频通话和消息功能都非常可靠，仅两次因网络问题用了手机通话。Sandra作为典型用户，对技术细节不感兴趣，但XMPP使用体验顺畅。作者尚未与其他服务器或用户测试XMPP，但很满意自家通信的加密性。他还提到希望Snikket支持多域名。

不同观点：
• danieldk认为XMPP在2010年左右代表了一种“未来”的聊天方式，能够在不同平台上通过多种客户端使用，如Google Talk和iChat，尤其是在Linux和macOS上表现出色。
• rckt表示自己虽然维持了一个XMPP账号五年，但实际使用中仅与一人聊天，最终放弃了，认为XMPP在现实中非常小众。
• nadof分享了在iPhone和Android上使用XMPP的不同体验，指出在Android上结合"conversations"应用可以实现实时通知和高质量的音视频通话，但在iPhone上通知功能不佳，且通话通知存在问题。
• daneel_w表示自己使用XMPP超过十年，习惯称之为Jabber，使用Prosody作为服务器，Profanity作为桌面终端客户端，Monal作为移动客户端。
• wahern回应了nadof的评论，指出Monal在iPhone上的通知问题，尽管Monal的网站和提交日志显示通知功能应该可用，但实际使用中存在问题，而在macOS上的Monal则工作正常。

• ColinWright引用了一个两年前的XMPP使用案例，显示XMPP的长期使用情况。

• rlpbb表示自己一直是XMPP的粉丝，但对其未能达到专有解决方案的功能对等感到失望，例如Conversations.im不支持实时位置分享。
• haunter疑惑是否评论中提到的用户仅与一人通过XMPP聊天。

• XMPP在隐私保护和自主托管方面的优势，特别是在家庭使用场景中。
• XMPP潜在功能的扩展性，如与OsmAnd的集成以实现更多功能。
• 对XMPP未能达到专有解决方案功能对等的失望，以及对其未来发展的期望。

争议焦点：
• XMPP在现实使用中的小众性与其潜在功能的广泛性之间的矛盾。
• iPhone上XMPP通知功能的实际表现与预期不符。
• XMPP与专有解决方案的功能差距及其是否能被广泛接受。

44726731.article_content:
For the last month, I’ve been using XMPP (using Snikket) for every call and chat between me and my wife Sandra, at least.
Sandra and I switched from using Matrix to using XMPP a while back. Matrix was pretty good for messaging, although quite a few encryption-related issues, but it - or my installation of it, possibly - was unreliable for audio and video. Sometimes it would work, sometimes it would not.
Moving to XMPP - using prosody - worked really well for messaging, but the lack of real-time notifications on Sandra’s iPhone was sub-optimal, and the lack of any notifications for incoming XMPP calls on her phone was
really
undesirable.
I
installed Snikket, a self-contained XMPP distribution
just over a month ago and, since then, we’ve tried to use that for every call and message.
And we have very nearly succeeded - I can think of only two times where I fell back on using a cellular call instead of an XMPP call:
One was where Sandra was somewhere with very poor cellular data coverage (as in, cannot load a basic web page of check email), so fair enough.
Another was when I was in Westminster, so there really shouldn’t have been a coverage problem, but there was an annoying latency on the connection of a few seconds, which made me think that perhaps the cell was congested, or something like that. Enough for a monologue or to get an important message across, but too poor for a meaningful conversation.
But other than those two occasions, voice and video have been incredibly reliable. We’ve had quite long calls using it, moving between cells, and switching between Wi-Fi and cellular connections, and it has been great. I haven’t experimented yet too much with calls from my computer; that’s still to come.
Messaging, including photo sharing, has worked flawlessly throughout.
Sandra is, with no disrepect meant, a pretty typical end user. She puts up with me installing different apps on her phone, or asking her to use Service X or Y for something, but she doesn’t have a particular interest in how it all works, or what it is, as long as it does the job. So it is very pleasing that XMPP has been so painless in
that
regard too.
I haven’t tried using it with anyone else though, or across different servers, as there’s no-one else with whom I want to talk who also uses XMPP. I could set up my parents on it, and use XMPP instead of Signal, and this is kind of where I wish Snikket supported multiple domain names rather than needing different instances (I know, I know, there’s prosody for that…).
I rather like the fact that’s an Intel NUC, sitting in the rack at home, carrying all our communications, and that they are encrypted. That all appeals to me.

• rlpbb表示自己一直是XMPP的粉丝，但对其未能达到专有解决方案的功能对等感到失望，例如Conversations.im不支持实时位置分享。
• haunter疑惑是否评论中提到的用户仅与一人通过XMPP聊天。
• rdm_blackhole提到在做笔记，以防欧盟议会通过Chat Control法案。

补充讨论：
• XMPP在不同操作系统和设备上的表现差异，尤其是iPhone上的通知问题。
• XMPP在隐私保护和自主托管方面的优势，特别是在家庭使用场景中。
• XMPP潜在功能的扩展性，如与OsmAnd的集成以实现更多功能。
• 对XMPP未能达到专有解决方案功能对等的失望，以及对其未来发展的期望。

争议焦点：
• XMPP在现实使用中的小众性与其潜在功能的广泛性之间的矛盾。
• iPhone上XMPP通知功能的实际表现与预期不符。
• XMPP与专有解决方案的功能差距及其是否能被广泛接受。

data.title: More honey bees dying, even as antibiotic use halves
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 尽管加拿大限制了养蜂业中抗生素的使用，蜜蜂的死亡率仍在上升。一项由圭尔夫大学研究人员主导的研究发现，随着抗生素使用减半，蜜蜂的越冬死亡率反而从不到20%上升到超过40%。研究表明，抗生素的减少可能导致蜜蜂对致病微生物的抵御能力下降，因为它们的微生物群受到破坏。此外，二氧化氮（NO2）污染也被发现是蜜蜂死亡率上升的一个意外因素，因为它干扰了蜜蜂的觅食能力。研究人员呼吁采用“同一健康”方法，综合考虑人类、动物和环境健康，寻找替代抗生素的解决方案，如益生菌。目前，加拿大正在开展一个全国性项目，研究蜜蜂的微生物群以应对这一问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：蜜蜂和传粉者的保护及其面临的威胁

不同观点：
• JumpCrisscross认为，蜜蜂并非北美本土物种，它们的引入对本地传粉者如大黄蜂构成威胁，导致生物多样性下降。此外，工业化农业依赖蜜蜂传粉，而个人在后院放置蜂箱可能会无意中破坏本地蝴蝶和大黄蜂的种群。
• mushroomba指出，现代养蜂实践类似于工厂化养殖，并提到Tim Rowe的"The Rose Hive Method"利用进化来改善蜜蜂的活力。然而，由于对蜂蛰过敏，他无法实践这些方法，并认为商业养蜂的当前实践无法持续。
• miellaby批评某些文章将问题归因于抗生素，而不是广泛认可的新烟碱类农药，指责农业行业的误导性声明。
• imzadi认为，停止使用抗生素可能会导致蜜蜂健康状况下降，因为之前的抗生素使用可能已经杀死了健康的细菌。
• alionski强调，工业和政府应 equally 关注野生蜂的衰退，指出“拯救蜜蜂”实际上是指野生蜂，而非蜜蜂。
• ceedan引用研究指出，蜂群崩溃症可能是由于瓦螨传播的病毒和/或杀虫剂引起的。
• endo_bunker认为，抗生素与蜂巢死亡的关联可能是因为抗生素通常用于不健康的蜂巢。
• horacemorace提到，过去夏天每周都需要清理挡风玻璃上的虫渍，而现在不再需要，暗示昆虫数量的减少对生态系统有巨大影响。
• westurner引用研究指出，病毒和瓦螨是导致蜜蜂 colony collapse 的主要原因。
• giantg2认为，细菌问题对养蜂人来说并不是主要问题，除了可以治疗的欧洲 foulbrood 外，只有美国 foulbrood 是无法治疗的，并提到一些关于生物群研究的有趣内容。
• thebees对非洲化蜜蜂在某些地区成为主要的蜂蜜生产者的现象感到有趣。
• animitronix和7734128认为，问题主要是杀虫剂而非抗生素。
• moomoo11建议购买和支持有机产品，认为自然生长的产品会更好。
• more_corn简洁指出，问题在于杀虫剂。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于蜜蜂健康问题的主要原因：抗生素、病毒、瓦螨还是杀虫剂。
- 不同观点中，有人关注蜜蜂的工业化利用对本地物种的影响，有人讨论现代养蜂实践的可持续性，还有人关注具体病害和农药的影响。
- 支持有机农业和减少化学药剂使用的建议也被提出作为解决方案。

Top Stories
More Honey Bees Dying, Even as Antibiotic Use Halves
More Honey Bees Dying, Even as Antibiotic Use Halves
Despite tighter restrictions on antibiotics used in Canadian beekeeping, honey bee death rates are still rising.
A new study led by University of Guelph researchers, published in
Nature Sustainability
, is the first large-scale project to assess antibiotic usage trends and their impact on honey bee health in Canada.
The withdrawal of antibiotics, following recent regulation changes, was one of the top predictors of honey bee overwintering mortality — a result that surprised lead author Dr.
Brendan Daisley
.
Dr. Brendan Daisley
“You’d assume the lessening of antibiotics might be associated with improved health outcomes, especially since antibiotics are so overused,” says Daisley, a postdoctoral researcher in the
College of Biological Science
. “But without effective alternatives, it seems the bees have developed a dependency on them.”
Using national survey data, researchers investigated more than 700,000 honey bee colonies per year between 2015 and 2023. Colony losses varied by province, but overwintering mortality rose from an average of less than 20 to over 40%, even as antibiotic usage halved, decreasing from approximately 50 to 25% nationally.
During the period studied, a new framework in 2018 put forth by the World Health Organization (WHO) and adopted by U.S. and Canadian agencies decreased over-the-counter access for certain beekeeping antibiotics.
This was done to address antimicrobial resistance (AMR) — the rising resistance to antibiotics that makes infectious diseases more difficult to treat. AMR is one of top 10 public threats facing humanity, according to WHO.
“We didn’t know the repercussions of these global changes in antimicrobial stewardship,” he says. “But it shows one of the most important drivers of honey bee mortality rates is likely infectious disease, and the imbalance between ‘bad’ and ‘good’ microbes.”
‘Microbial apocalypse’ could explain global colony loss, rising food costs
Daisley is one of few scientists who study honey bees’ entire bacterial community, known as their microbiome, as a way to assess their health.
“It’s a catch-22 — we know antibiotics are very useful for controlling disease outcomes, but they also disrupt the microbiome and do not distinguish between harmful and beneficial bacteria,” says Daisley. “We could be experiencing a microbial apocalypse in front of our eyes.”
The findings are a major breakthrough in microbiome research, he says, and may help explain record losses of the world’s bee colonies.
Millions of colonies lost in the U.S. alone are already leading to the rising costs of honey and pollination services, Daisley says, as beekeepers are forced to increase imports of bees to compensate.
This further translates to rising food costs, decreased crop yields and the disruption of global food security.
‘All interconnected’: One Health approach needed for alternatives
In addition to antibiotic usage, researchers identified another unexpected predictor of honey bee mortality: nitrogen dioxide (NO2), a common air pollutant from diesel exhaust.
NO2 degrades floral odours and disrupts the bees’ ability to forage, researchers say, which could be contributing to colony loss.
“It’s all interconnected, and in my opinion, all links back to microbial ecology and the microbial homeostasis of pollinators,” Daisley says.
Given the complex relationships between bees’ microbiomes, their health and their environment, researchers call for a
One Health
approach, a systems-level view that assesses
human, animal and environmental health more holistically
.
“Honey bees epitomize the principles of One Health by serving as a tangible example of the interconnectedness of human, animal and environmental well-being — particularly through their microbiome, which reflects and mediates the impacts of ecological stressors, agricultural practices and disease transmission across systems,” Daisley says.
Solutions to stop colony loss will require the One Health approach, as factors like NO2 must be considered alongside antibiotic alternatives like probiotics.
Daisley co-leads the Canadian Bee Gut project to investigate the microbes of bees
In this emerging field, bee probiotics are still in development and far from widespread adoption. Daisley leads research to characterize several different probiotics’ mechanisms of action within the bees’ intestinal tracts.
“But we need more funding to support the study of alternatives,” Daisley says. “The next aim is also to comprehensively characterize the microbiome of bees, to develop a baseline understanding so we have something to compare it to.”
To accomplish that, Daisley and Dr.
Emma Allen-Vercoe
(
Department of Molecular and Cellular Biology
) lead
the Canadian Bee Gut project
at U of G, a nationwide crowdsourcing initiative that began in 2022. The project collects samples from about 1,000 beehives each year from every

data.title: Playing with Open Source LLMs
data.author: zer0tonin
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者探索使用大型语言模型（LLM）在终端中进行代码编写的过程。作者首先提到当前流行的工具Claude Code，虽然功能全面，但作者担心被绑定到不盈利公司的工具上。因此，他转而寻找开源替代方案。经过尝试，作者选择了Qwen3:8b模型，该模型由阿里巴巴开发，支持现代AI工具，并且在本地运行良好。作者使用Ollama搭建本地API来运行LLM，并通过Aider实现与模型的配对编程。Aider允许用户通过命令行与模型交互，指导其修改代码、运行检查工具并提交更改。尽管模型并不完全自主，需要用户引导，但整体体验较为高效。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放大语言模型的使用、内部机制探索、硬件需求以及开源与免费软件的区别。

不同观点：
• roadside_picnic认为开放模型的真正价值在于其内部并非“黑箱”，用户可以探索和修改模型的内部结构，如通过实现推测解码、约束解码等方式深入理解模型运作。他强调探索模型内部比单纯运行模型更有意义。

• simonw指出，尽管在理论上使用LLM进行编码看起来很成功，但在实际操作中，调整提示、等待AI运行以及修复小问题所花费的时间远远超过手动编辑文件的时间。他还提到，实验中使用的模型（如deepseek-r1:8b, mistral:7b, qwen3:8b）较小，能生成可用的代码已经是个奇迹。

• v3ss0n认为许多人对模型的理解有误，建议使用qwen3 8b-14b而不是deepseek-r1 8b，因为前者性能更好。

• channel_t表示，这种探索过程具有教育价值，但最终可能还是会转向使用由“不盈利公司”拥有的大模型。

• ikejix关注运行这些模型所需的硬件条件。

• runningmike对使用自由和开源ML工具的更新表示感谢，认为这节省了大量时间。

• BoorishBears澄清deepseek-r1 8B并不以其著名性而闻名，且指出其与Deepseek的混淆，类似于他自己微调Llama并不意味着他创造了Llama。

• 44za12以讽刺的语气表示，使用顶级“开源LLM”后发现它们表现不佳，从而认为自己的工作很安全。

• lrvick强调开源与免费软件的区别，指出如果某些东西无法从在OSI许可下分发的源代码中重现，那么它们就不是开源的，并提供了相关定义和链接。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及模型的性能、大小及其对实际任务的适用性。
• 对“开源”和“免费软件”的定义存在争议，lrvick提供了明确的定义和区分标准。
• 对具体模型（如deepseek-r1 8b和qwen3 8b）的性能和来源存在不同看法。
• 讨论还涉及到实际应用中的时间和效率问题，特别是与手动操作相比的优劣。

44726838.article_content:
Every 6 months or so, I decide to leave my cave and check out what the cool kids are doing with AI.
Apparently the latest trend is to use fancy command line tools to write code using LLMs.
This is a very nice change, since it suddenly makes AI compatible with my allergy to getting out of the terminal.
Me, browsing HN from my cave (by Stable Diffusion)
The most popular of these tools seems to be Claude Code.
It promises to be able to build in total autonomy, being able to use search code, write code, run tests, lint, and commit the changes.
While this sounds great on paper, I’m not keen on getting locked into vendor tools from an unprofitable company.
At some point, they will either need to raise their prices, enshittify their product, or most likely do both.
So I went looking for what the free and open source alternatives are.
Picking a model
There’s a large amount of open source large language models on the market, with new ones getting released all the time.
However, they are not all ready to be used locally in coding tasks, so I had to try a bunch of them before settling on one.
deepseek-r1:8b
Deepseek is the most popular open source model right now.
It was created by the eponymous Chinese company.
It made the news by beating numerous benchmarks while being trained on a budget that is probably lower than the compensation of some OpenAI workers.
The 8b variant only weights 5.2 GB and runs decently on limited hardware, like my three years old Mac.
This model is famous for forgetting about world events from 1989, but also seems to have a few issues when faced with concrete coding tasks.
It is a reasoning model, meaning it “thinks” before acting, which should lead to improved accuracy.
In practice, it regularly gets stuck indefinitely searching where it should start and jumping from one problem to the other in a loop.
This can happen even on simple problems, and made it unusable for me.
mistral:7b
Mistral is the French alternative to American and Chinese models.
I have already talked about their 7b model
on this blog
.
It is worth noting that they have kept updating their models, and it should now be much more accurate than two years ago.
Mistral is not a reasoning model, so it will jump straight to answering.
This is very good if you’re working with tasks where speed and low compute use are a priority.
Sadly, the accuracy doesn’t seem good enough for coding.
Even on simple tasks, it will hallucinate functions or randomly delete parts of the code I didn’t want to touch.
qwen3:8b
Another model from China, qwen3 was created by the folks at Alibaba.
It also claims impressive benchmark results, and can work as both a reasoning or non-thinking model.
It was made with modern AI tooling in mind, by supporting MCPs and a
framework for agentic development
.
This model actually seems to work as expected, providing somewhat accurate code output while not hanging in the reasoning part.
Since it runs decently on my local setup, I decided to stick to that model for now.
Setting up a local API with Ollama
Ollama is now the default way to download and run local LLMs.
It can be simply installed by downloading it from
their website
.
Once installed, it works like Docker for models, by giving us access to commands like
pull
,
run
, or
rm
.
Ollama will expose an API on
localhost
which can be used by other programs.
For example, you can use it from your Python programs through
ollama-python
.
My new pet (by Stable Diffusion)
Pair programming with aider
The next piece of software I installed is
aider
.
I assume it’s pronounced like the French word, but I could not confirm that.
Aider describes itself as a “pair programming” application.
Its main job is to pass context to the model, let it write the output to files, run linters, and commit the changes.
Getting started
It can be installed using
the official Python package
or via
Homebrew
if you use Mac.
Once it is installed, just navigate to your code repository and launch it:
export
OLLAMA_API_BASE
=
http://127.0.0.1:11434
aider
--model
ollama_chat/qwen3:8b
The CLI should automatically create some configuration files and add them to the repo’s
.gitignore
.
Usage
Aider isn’t meant to be left alone in complete autonomy.
You’ll have to guide the AI through the process of making changes to your repository.
To start, use the
/add
command to add files you want to focus on.
Those files will be passed entirely to the model’s context and the model will be able to write in them.
You can then ask questions using the
/ask
command.
If you want to generate code, a good strategy can be to starting by requesting a plan of actions.
When you want it to actually write to the files, you can prompt it using the
/code
command.
This is also the default mode.
There’s no absolute guarantee that it will follow a plan if you agreed on one previously, but it is still a good idea to have one.
The
/architect
command seems to automatically ask for a plan, accept it, and write the code.
The specificity of this c

data.title: Supervised fine tuning on curated data is reinforcement learning
data.author: GabrielBianconi
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了监督微调（SFT）在精选数据上的应用，并将其与强化学习（RL）的理论和实践联系起来。作者指出，SFT可以被视为在稀疏奖励设置下最大化RL目标的下界，从而解释了其良好表现的原因。基于此观点，作者提出了一种重要性加权监督微调（iw-SFT）方法，该方法优化了更紧的下界，并可能提升性能。实验表明，iw-SFT在多个大型语言模型和连续控制任务中，表现可与更先进的RL算法相媲美，例如在AIME 2024数据集上达到了66.7%的成绩。文章提供了相关代码和详细信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过精调小型模型并降低推理成本，是否可以超越大型模型的性能，以及对相关技术方法的争议和讨论。

不同观点：
• [anndvision] 认为，通过在大型模型自动筛选的高质量输出上精调小型模型，可以在降低推理成本和推理时间的情况下，超越大型模型的性能。他们通过在多个任务上进行实验，证明了这一点。
• [iandanforth] 质疑将任何优化问题框定为强化学习（RL）问题的类比是否恰当。他指出，RL的核心是 sequential decision making（序列决策过程），如果不涉及代理在环境中多次决策，就不应称之为RL。
• [markisus] 对特定的数学方程（方程5）表示怀疑，认为其中的期望计算可能存在问题，特别是由于指示函数导致的中项期望值可能接近于零。
• [mandevil] 对两个独立研究人员同时研究这一主题表示好奇，询问是否为副项目或其他背景。
• [henriquegodoy] 支持通过将AI视为模块化组件而非代理，从而解决某些问题（如沟通、合规等）的观点。他认为可以从超智能模型开始，然后提炼为小型模型，以降低成本。
• [stolencode] 以讽刺的口吻批评学术界发表论文多于实际工作的现象，暗示在某些数据集上取得成绩需要耗费大量资源。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于对精调小型模型以超越大型模型的可行性和方法的认可与质疑。
• 对RL应用范围和定义的讨论，反映了在技术方法论上的分歧。
• 对特定数学方程和计算结果的怀疑，显示出对技术细节的关注和严谨性。
• 对研究背景和动机的兴趣，可能涉及对学术和商业研究透明度和合作性的期望。
• 对学术与实际工作投入不平衡的批评，反映了学术界与产业界在资源使用和成果展示上的张力。

Title:
Supervised Fine Tuning on Curated Data is Reinforcement Learning (and can be improved)
Authors:
Chongli Qin
,
Jost Tobias Springenberg
View a PDF of the paper titled Supervised Fine Tuning on Curated Data is Reinforcement Learning (and can be improved), by Chongli Qin and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Behavior Cloning (BC) on curated (or filtered) data is the predominant paradigm for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of large language models; as well as for imitation learning of control policies. Here, we draw on a connection between this successful strategy and the theory and practice of finding optimal policies via Reinforcement Learning (RL). Building on existing literature, we clarify that SFT can be understood as maximizing a lower bound on the RL objective in a sparse reward setting. Giving support to its often observed good performance. From this viewpoint, we realize that a small modification to SFT leads to an importance weighted variant that behaves closer to training with RL as it: i) optimizes a tighter bound to the RL objective and, ii) can improve performance compared to SFT on curated data. We refer to this variant as importance weighted supervised fine-tuning (iw-SFT). We show that it is easy to implement and can be further generalized to training with quality scored data. The resulting SFT variants are competitive with more advanced RL algorithms for large language models and for training policies in continuous control tasks. For example achieving 66.7% on the AIME 2024 dataset.

补充讨论：
• 项目的时间和成本效益是讨论的重要方面，尤其是coterm项目带来的优势。
• 项目课程的公开性和在线资源的历史也是一个关注点。
• 对MS&E学位在实际工作中的价值存在争议，特别是在不同专业背景下的适用性。
• 项目的录取率和学生特质引发了一些评论者的批评和怀疑。

data.title: 2D to 3D model and 3D print it
data.author: Jimmy6929
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对2D到3D技术平台"Amodeling"的使用体验、功能评价及付费模式的争议

不同观点：
• [对2D到3D技术的评价]  
  - specproc认为2D到3D技术目前仍处于概念阶段，生成模型的质量参差不齐。虽然有些优秀作品（如PiperMakes等），但大多数模型缺乏原创性。他表示宁愿支持人类艺术家，因为AI模型在质量上还无法与人类设计师相比。
  
• [对平台内容和版权的关注]  
  - hnlmorg指出平台上一些模型与现有版权作品（如索尼的Astro Bot）过于相似，存在潜在的版权问题。同时，他认可平台的创意，但对月度订阅模式不满，更倾向于按需付费（PAYG）模式。他还提出了对模型生成质量的担忧，质疑如果生成的模型质量不佳，用户是否有多种选择或退款机制。

• [对平台技术问题的反馈]  
  - Jimmy6929分享了自己在使用Amodeling进行3D建模和打印过程中遇到的困难，虽然解决了大部分问题，但下载功能仍存在一些问题。
  
• [对平台设计细节的质疑]  
  - overgard提出一个元问题，质疑为什么AI应用程序的按钮设计普遍采用粉蓝渐变，这种设计选择似乎很普遍。

• [技术错误的反馈]  
  - marcodiego报告了遇到应用程序错误，客户端在加载过程中出现问题，并提示查看浏览器控制台以获取更多信息。

• [设备兼容性问题]  
  - ed_mercer表示在iPhone 12 mini上使用时应用崩溃，怀疑是内存溢出（OOM）问题。

补充讨论：
• 平台的付费模式引起了用户的不满和讨论，特别是对于不频繁使用者来说，月度订阅模式并不理想，PAYG模式更受欢迎。
• 用户对生成模型的质量和版权问题表示关注，质疑平台是否能提供足够多的选择和保障机制。
• 技术问题和设备兼容性也是用户反馈中的重要部分，显示出平台在技术稳定性和兼容性方面仍有待改进。

Frequently Asked Questions
Everything you need to know about Monochromate greyscale browser extension.
What is Monochromate and how does it work?
Monochromate is a free browser extension that applies a greyscale filter to
websites, removing colors to reduce visual distractions and doomscrolling. It works
by modifying the CSS of web pages in real-time, making them appear in black and
white while preserving functionality.
Does Monochromate really reduce screen time?
Yes! Research shows that colorful interfaces trigger dopamine responses that make
websites more addictive. By removing colors, Monochromate makes websites less
visually stimulating, naturally reducing the time you spend browsing and scrolling.
Is Monochromate free and safe to use?
Absolutely! Monochromate is completely free and open-source. We don't collect any
personal data, track your browsing, or display ads. All settings are stored locally
on your device for maximum privacy and security.
Can I exclude specific websites from greyscale mode?
Yes! Monochromate includes smart site exclusion features. You can easily add
websites to your blacklist where colors should remain enabled - perfect for photo
galleries, design work, or work-critical applications that require color accuracy.
Which browsers support Monochromate?
Monochromate is available for both Chrome and Firefox with identical features. It's
built using the WXT framework, ensuring consistent performance and functionality
across both browsers. You can download it from the Chrome Web Store or Firefox
Add-ons.
How do I install and use Monochromate?
Installation is simple: visit the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons, click "Add to
Browser," and you're ready! Once installed, click the Monochromate icon in your
toolbar to toggle greyscale mode on/off. You can adjust intensity and manage site
exclusions from the popup interface.
I found a bug in Monochromate. How can I report it?

Ned O'Leary提出了几种改进多因素身份验证（MFA）用户体验的方法：

1. **大盲法**：用户从52张扑克牌中选择5张，作为二次认证因素，易于记忆且难以猜测。
2. **魔方法**：用户打乱一个数字魔方，再次登录时重复相同操作，魔方有约4.3 x 10^19种可能配置。
3. **香农数法**：使用象棋对局作为认证因素，有约10^120种可能对局，提升安全性和趣味性。
4. **打字模式**：利用用户独特的打字速度作为认证因素。
5. **无硬件指纹**：展示指纹图片让用户确认，无需专用硬件。
6. **离线TOTP**：将TOTP密码打印在纸上通过邮寄传递，避免SMS漏洞。
7. **隐私优先**：利用自拍肖像进行身份验证，结合外观和技巧两个验证维度。
8. **歌唱认证**：用户通过唱歌进行认证，必须完整唱完一首歌以防欺诈。
9. **亲友协助**：系统随机选择亲属发送验证码，如叔叔帮助访问旧邮箱。

这些方法旨在提高MFA的用户友好性和安全性。

主要讨论点：多因素认证（MFA）及其各种实现方式的优缺点

不同观点：
• **BlackFly的观点**：认为多因素认证被过度使用，尤其在不需要高安全性的场景下。他指出，高强度密码已经足够安全，TOTP（基于时间的一次性密码）只是增加了网站的安全性而非用户自身的安全性。他还提到，很多人将TOTP密钥存储在登录设备上，导致单点漏洞。

• **seplox的观点**：表达了对非TOTP多因素认证方法的不满，尤其是某些强制使用的、不够完善的认证方式。他主张至少应提供TOTP作为选项，因为用户更喜欢使用认证器应用。

• **jerjerjer的观点**：提出使用扑克牌局作为密码的创意，认为这既容易记住又难以被攻击者猜测。不过，这种方法可能导致用户选择常见牌局，降低其安全性。

• **averageRoyalty的观点**：幽默地指出自画像签名方法类似于过去几十年接受的签名方式，认为这种方法在特定场景下是有效的。

• **FuriouslyAdrift的观点**：在工作中发现指纹锁的NFC Yubikey受到各年龄层用户的欢迎，但普遍讨厌passkey，因为其经常无法正常工作。

• **thcipriani的观点**：认为扑克牌局可用于快速识别的编码，例如密钥指纹，提供了一种有趣的编码方式。

• **smokel的观点**：质疑大多数2FA应用限制仅当前验证码有效的设计，认为允许前一个验证码短暂有效可以提高可用性而不显著损害安全性。

• **marc_abonce的观点**：提到Facebook曾使用类似强制MFA的方法应对可疑登录，并指出这种方法可被用于训练Facebook的面部识别器。此外，这种方法对熟人或 stalker 攻击无效。

• **Liftyee的观点**：对某些方法是否真正构成第二因素认证表示怀疑，认为它们可能都属于“你知道的东西”这一类别，而非不同的认证因素。

• **pmontra的观点**：仅在银行等强制要求时使用2FA，对其他服务的2FA选项通常跳过。特别不喜欢基于SMS的2FA，因为国际旅行时接收短信不便。

• **PeterStuer的观点**：希望使用自己选择的认证器应用扫描QR码，不想要其他复杂的认证方式。

• **1970-01-01的观点**：认为这些创意很糟糕，甚至可能已经在GitHub上有了。

• **anteloper的观点**：质疑为什么在认证因素中追求高熵，未展开具体论述。

补充讨论：
- 各种2FA方法的用户体验和安全性之间的权衡。
- 不同认证方法在不同场景下的适用性和有效性。
- 用户对多因素认证的接受度和实际使用中的困扰。
- 对特定认证方法（如SMS、TOTP、passkey）的安全性和便利性的争议。

44716280.article_content:
I designed some more user-friendly methods for multi-factor authentication.
Ned O'Leary
Cofounder and CEO, Tesseral
When I tell people I work on authentication software, I nearly always hear some version of the same story:
I hate multifactor authentication
. No, really. People hate this stuff.
So I spend a lot of time thinking about how we can make MFA a better user experience. We don't always need MFA to be airtight, after all. Sometimes, the Google
match-a-number
MFA flow is good enough.
I thought I'd share here my best ideas for the future of multi-factor authentication. Here they are.
The big blind
We like
entropy
in auth factors, so it's intuitive to start with a familiar example of randomness: playing cards. For example,
Wikipedia says
there are about 2.5 million unique poker hands.
That makes poker hands a compelling secondary authentication factor. Here's what a simple version of the UI could look like: challenge the user to pick exactly five cards from a set of 52.
It's incredibly easy to remember your hand. Just ask any of your friends that play poker -- they can surely remember a bad beat. And it's pretty much impossible for an attacker to guess.
Cubes
This one's a bit tougher than poker, but it's much less risky. (I'm not sure how comfortable I am with just 2.5M possibilities). Instead of having the user pick 5 cards from a deck of 52, we have the user scramble a digital Rubik's cube.
Then, when the user logs back in, they just have to scramble the cube in exactly the same way. Easy. Here's what it'd look like:
We can rest easy knowing that there are roughly
4.3 x 10^19 possible configurations
of the cube.
The Shannon number
If we're looking for even
more
entropy in our auth factors, we could use chess games as an option. It's
been estimated
that there are 10^120 possible chess matches. That's a nice big number.
Imagine this: when you set up your account, you play out a chess match. When you log back in, you play out the exact same chess match. It's like a second password! There's no chance anyone would ever guess your chess match correctly.
It's clean and intuitive. Hard to beat. Plus it'll boost your chess skill.
Mavis Beacon teaches auth
Everyone types a little differently. We can exploit our unique typing tendencies as an auth factor. There's a simple version of this that relies solely on approximate words-per-minute (WPM), as shown below.
If you want access to your account, all you have to do is reliably reproduce the same typing speed!
Fingerprints without the hardware
Biometric factors like fingerprints are perfect -- except for the fact that they generally require fancy hardware. How does a normal web app take a fingerprint as an input?
Well, I just don't think it's necessary. You can simply
present the user with a fingerprint
and ask whether it's a match!
All the benefit, none of the fuss.
Airgapped TOTPs
Everyone still seems to use SMS-based MFA, but we all know by now that SMS opens vulnerability to
SIM-swapping attacks
.
How do we retain the user-friendly experience of SMS MFA while protecting ourselves from its vulnerabilities? I think I have a solution. We never put our passcodes over the air. Instead, we print them onto sheets of 8.5" x 11" paper and route them through a trusted Postal Service.
Maximum security.
Privacy first
Many of us would like to use photographs as an auth factor. We often require photographs as
part of onboarding
for certain sensitive applications (e.g., banking, ridesharing).
But users really don't like submitting photographs. It can feel a bit invasive. Plus, privacy considerations aside, it's just inconvenient and puts an annoying speedbump between the user and successful use of the software.
Good news: we don't need to grab a
photo
of the user. With today's multi-modal AI, we can simply infer identities from self-portrait.
With self-portraits, we get two distinct vectors of comparison: first, we can evaluate the portrait for its similarity to the user's real appearance; second, we can evaluate the portrait for the user's skill level.
That stuff is hard to fake!
Of me I sing
Biometric auth based on users' voices used to be reliable, but now it's too
easy to spoof
with AI tools. But AI still has a tough time singing as poorly as normal people do -- that's why Karaoke Auth is the future.
The user just has to pick a song and belt it out. For anyone thinking of implementing karaoke-based auth, I will caution you: it is
critical
to require the user to finish the entire song. Song fragments do not generate sufficient samples to protect against fraud.
Phone a friend
We can borrow an innovation from the Web3 crowd. Instead of sending a code to
your
email (predictable, boring, lame), the system sends a code to a randomly-selected relative. Like an uncle!
The user just has to help their uncle access a 22-year-old Hotmail account before the passcode expires (upon expiry, the system will select a different relative at random).

data.title: How the brain increases blood flow on demand
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了哈佛医学院的一项新研究，该研究揭示了大脑如何快速有效地将血液输送到需要更多氧气和营养的活跃区域。研究发现，大脑依赖于血管内皮细胞间紧密交织的通道进行通讯，这些通道通过所谓的缝隙连接迅速传递信号，从而调节血流量。该研究发表在《Cell》杂志上，有助于更好地理解神经退行性疾病以及脑成像（如功能性磁共振成像，fMRI）的解读。如果这些发现能在动物和人类中得到进一步验证，可能会为治疗认知问题提供新思路。这项研究还强调了联邦资助对科学研究的重要性。

主要讨论点：围绕血压控制机制及相关药物影响的讨论

不同观点：
• **[evanjrowley]** 分享了个人使用血管紧张素II受体阻滞剂（一种降压药）的经历。他提到最初身体难以在持续用力时升高血压，但之后有所适应，且尚未遇到明显的副作用。不过，他提到其他人报告过如“脑雾”等不良反应，并质疑该药物与研究中的血压控制机制之间的潜在交互。

• **[Insanity]** 对人类大脑如何运作的研究表示兴趣，简单表达了对研究的欣赏，但没有深入探讨具体科学内容。

• **[bozhark]** 以一种调侃的方式提出“大脑是否会变硬”的问题，属于非严肃的评论，没有提供实质性的科学讨论或论据。

• **[searine]** 提到资助该研究的多个机构（如国家科学基金会、哈佛医学院等）面临资金削减的问题，暗示科研资金问题可能影响研究的进展，但未对研究本身提出质疑。

• **[HardCodedBias]** 对大脑血流灌注的机制提出疑问，具体讨论了血流是否根据计算/代谢需求（通过内皮细胞经由缝隙连接进行通信）调整，还是大脑直接向内皮细胞发出信号。这表明对研究中涉及的生理机制有更深入的兴趣，并指出可能需要更多研究来解答这些疑问。

补充讨论：
• 评论中存在一定的科学讨论，尤其是关于药物副作用和血压控制的具体机制，但也有一些调侃和非正式的评论（如[bozhark]）。
• **争议的焦点** 主要在于降压药物的潜在副作用，以及药物与大脑血流控制机制之间的可能交互。这些尚未有明确的答案，表明需要更多的研究来澄清。

44727191.article_content:
How the Brain Increases Blood Flow on Demand
New findings could improve understanding of neurodegeneration, interpretation of brain scans
By CATHERINE CARUSO
July 16, 2025
Research
3 min read
Blood vessels in the brain. Image: mr.suphachai praserdumrongchai/iStock/Getty Images Plus
At a glance:
A new study in mice describes how the brain rapidly and efficiently increases blood flow to active areas where oxygen and nutrients are needed most.
The work shows that the brain relies on a communication highway of tightly interlaced cells lining its blood vessels.
The insights could advance understanding of neurodegenerative diseases and improve interpretation of brain imaging.
Work described in this story was made possible in part by federal funding supported by taxpayers. At Harvard Medical School, the future of efforts like this — done in service to humanity — now hangs in the balance due to the government’s decision to terminate large numbers of federally funded grants and contracts across Harvard University.
All day long, our brains carry out complicated and energy-intensive tasks such as remembering, solving problems, and making decisions.
To supply the energy these tasks require while conserving this precious fuel, the brain has evolved a system that allows it to quickly and efficiently send blood only to the areas that need it most in any given moment. This system is essential to brain function and overall health, yet how it works has remained somewhat of a mystery.
Get more HMS news
Now, a team led by researchers at Harvard Medical School has uncovered new details of how the brain moves blood to active areas in real time. Their
findings are published July 16 in
Cell
.
In experiments in mice, the team discovered that the brain uses specialized channels in the lining of its blood vessels to communicate where blood is needed.
“This work helps us understand how you can get that super-important blood supply to the correct areas of the brain on a time scale that is useful,” said co-lead author
Luke Kaplan
, a research fellow in neurobiology in the Blavatnik Institute at HMS.
If confirmed in additional studies in animals and humans, the findings could be used to better understand findings on brain imaging tests such as functional MRI (fMRI). The insights may also advance understanding of neurodegenerative diseases, in which this communication system often breaks down, leading to cognitive problems.
A long-standing mechanistic puzzle
In the late 1800s, Italian physician Angelo Mosso observed something intriguing in a patient with a skull defect that left an area of his brain exposed: When the patient got angry, parts of the exposed area instantly swelled with blood — hinting at a connection between brain activity and blood flow.
A century later, this connection became the basis of fMRI, a type of brain scan that measures blood flow to different regions as a proxy for neural activity while individuals perform various tasks.
The brain is one of the body’s most energy-demanding organs, accounting for 2 percent of the body’s weight but consuming 20 percent of its total energy. To stay within budget, the brain must be highly efficient: It rapidly directs blood flow to the regions that need it the most, explained senior author
Chenghua Gu
, professor of neurobiology at HMS.
While the brain’s proportion of energy consumption varies across species depending on the organ’s complexity, Gu said, the brain is an energy-hungry organ in all mammals.
“There’s this an elegant evolutionary mechanism that’s distributing blood flow on demand throughout the brain, but we don’t understand how it works,” said co-lead author
Trevor Krolak
, a doctoral student in the Gu lab.
This blood-allocation process deteriorates in neurodegeneration, Kaplan noted, and understanding its inner workings could lead to new insights.
“If we don’t know how this system operates on a biological level, we won’t know how to fix it when it goes wrong,” he said.
A cellular signaling highway revealed
To understand what happens on a molecular level as different brain regions become active, the researchers performed a series of experiments in mice. Their analysis showed the brain rapidly communicates the need for more blood in a particular area via endothelial cells that line blood vessels in the brain. Furthermore, the researchers observed, the endothelial cells communicated so quickly and efficiently via so-called gap junctions — tiny channels that physically connect neighboring cells. The team also identified two genes pivotal to the function of this communication pathway.
A blood vessel in the brain. The left shows outlines of individual endothelial cells lining the vessel. The center shows smooth muscle cells that wrap around the vessel and produce the physical force needed to move blood through it. The right shows gap junctions that tightly connect neighboring endothelial cells, allowing them to rapidly transmit signals. Image: Gu Lab

• **争议的焦点** 主要在于降压药物的潜在副作用，以及药物与大脑血流控制机制之间的可能交互。这些尚未有明确的答案，表明需要更多的研究来澄清。
