44725966.article_content:
Open Access Publication & ACM
ACM's Transition to Full Open Access: A New Era for Computing Research
For more than seven decades, ACM has played a pivotal role in advancing computing research, fostering collaboration, and disseminating knowledge through its world-class Digital Library, influential publications, and premier conferences.
In a significant step to broadening access to computing research, ACM is transitioning to a fully Open Access (OA) publishing model by the end of 2025. This bold move marks a pivotal moment in making all ACM research content freely available and removing barriers to discovery and innovation.
ACM's journey towards Open Access has been a carefully considered, phased approach, ensuring the long-term sustainability of its publications program and the various educational, diversity, public policy, and community recognition initiatives it supports.
The move to Open Access is not just a change in policy, but a reflection of ACM's commitment to its community, where the goal is to remove barriers to publishing and accessing vital research, and accelerating the pace of discovery and innovation.
ACM’s approach to Open Access is centered on 2 key elements:
1. ACM Open – A Sustainable Open Access Framework for Institutions
ACM Open is a unique and innovative take on the Read & Publish model, offering institutions a seamless way to support Open Access publishing. For academic or research institutions, pricing is based on an institution’s publishing output, averaged over the previous three years, and remains fixed for the duration of the agreement. This approach ensures predictability in budgeting while providing unlimited Open Access publishing and full read access to ACM content.
Key Benefits of ACM Open:
Unlimited Open Access Publishing
Corresponding authors from participating institutions can publish an unlimited number of Open Access articles without Article Processing Charges (APCs).
Fair and Predictable Pricing
ACM Open’s fixed term annual price, based on an academic or research institution’s historical publishing activity, ensures transparency and budget stability. This pricing model helps institutions manage costs effectively while supporting Open Access publishing. For corporate pricing,
please refer here
. For government pricing,
please refer here
.
Premium Digital Library Access
Institutions subscribing to ACM Open receive full access to the Premium version of the ACM Digital Library, providing their users with unrestricted access to over 800,000 ACM published research articles, the ACM Guide to Computing Literature (which indexes more than 6,500 3rd party publishers with direct links to the content), advanced tools, and exclusive features.
2. ACM Digital Library – A Tailored Approach to Access and Engagement
ACM is introducing
Premium and Basic
access options for the ACM Digital Library in
January 2026
, supporting a sustainable approach to Open Access. Institutions that subscribe to ACM Open will automatically receive full Premium access. A stand-alone Digital Library Premium subscription will also be available, providing continued access to critical resources and tools that support world-class computing research.
The Premium ACM Digital Library Experience
Premium
access enables institutions to fully leverage ACM content, providing deeper insights, seamless workflows, and richer collaboration opportunities for their users.
Premium
features include:
Access to the ACM Guide to Computing Literature,
expanding research beyond ACM content for a broader view of computing research.
Advanced research tools,
including AI-assisted search, bulk downloads, and citation management, to streamline discovery and workflow.
Comprehensive research insights,
including article usage metrics, citation trends, and Altmetric tracking to measure research impact.

data.title: RIP Shunsaku Tamiya, the man who made plastic model kits a global obsession
data.author: fidotron
data.article_summary: 日本知名模型制造公司田宫（Tamiya）的前社长及董事长田宫俊作于7月18日去世，享年90岁。他带领田宫从运输和木材业务转型为高精度塑料模型和遥控车制造商，尤其以迷你四驱车闻名。田宫俊作推动公司从木质模型转向塑料模型，并创造了田宫的标志性品牌形象和高质量声誉，包括著名的“双星”logo和“白盒”包装设计。他为确保模型精度，曾购买保时捷911并拆解以完善模型细节。2018年，他获得日本媒体艺术节的终身成就奖。他的贡献对模型爱好者和汽车 enthusiasts 产生了深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：模型制作爱好及其变迁

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun认为，模型组装本身虽然有趣，但更重要的是后期 painting 和 lighting，这与现代 YouTuber 们的观点一致。他还提到模型制作培养了他的空间思维和设计心态，但遗憾这个爱好逐渐失去流行，类似于 R/C 飞机和火箭模型。
• louthy分享了自己在80年代玩Tamiya遥控车的经历，强调了那种动手改造（如增加电池包）带来的短暂刺激和乐趣，即使结果是破坏性的。
• firefax指出，模型制作是一项需要技能的艺术形式，但对某些人（如自闭症谱系的人）来说可能存在障碍。他还表达了对模型套件简化和品牌化趋势的担忧，认为这可能反映了社会过度依赖网络的现象。
• spankibalt提到在东德时期对模型制作不感兴趣，但通过铁路模型店培养了对设计和插图的热爱，强调了模型盒艺术的吸引力。
• kkylin对RC汽车技术发展缓慢表示惊讶，质疑是否因为新一代孩子对这种动手体验不感兴趣，导致技术停滞。

补充讨论：
• radpanda通过Tamiya-san的故事，幽默地质疑其购买保时捷以确保模型准确性的动机，可能与税务问题有关。
• toomuchtodo简单提到了Tamiya主席逝世的新闻链接，未深入讨论。
• mirkodrummer和esafak分享了与家人一起组装模型和玩具的怀旧记忆，强调了这种活动对动手能力和专注力的培养。
• kawsper指出Tamiya的影响已延伸至其他爱好，如airsoft和无人机领域。
• billforsternz对模型制造行业的长寿和多样性表示赞赏，并好奇是否存在如“明星工匠”这样的角色。
• burnt-resistor怀念Tamiya模型出色的图示说明书，认为其优于IKEA说明书。
• Aeolun提到在Tamiya店铺中提供的工具、空间和赛道体验，认为这是吸引人的部分，且价格合理。

争议焦点：
• 模型制作的现代趋势，尤其是简化和品牌化套件是否削弱了传统模型的魅力和挑战性。

44728188.article_content:
Shunsaku Tamiya, former president and chairman of Tamiya, Inc., passed away on July 18. His death was announced on July 21, with funeral services attended by close family and friends. Mr Tamiya led the transformation of Tamiya into a world-renowned manufacturer of high-precision plastic model kits, radio control vehicles, and motorized Mini 4WD racers.
He joined the company founded by his father originally as a transport firm, and switched to supplying lumber after the war. That brought about an expansion into wooden models, primarily of ships and planes. After a fire destroyed the company’s lumber supply, it focused primarily on the models.
Not long after, plastic technology improved and began taking over the model kit market. Shunsuke Tamiya spearheaded the shift to
puramo
(a portmanteau of “plastic” and “model”) and in the process changed the industry. He helped fuel enthusiasm for cars, as well as other types of transportation, for generations of children and adults alike.
Shunsaku Tamiya was responsible for creating Tamiya’s signature branding and reputation for quality. He invited his brother Masao to create the “twin stars” logo and hired illustrators to create the “white box” look that made Tamiya stand out in sharp contrast to the box art of other model makers.
Most of all, he was the driving force in the unmatched precision Tamiya kits have come to be celebrated for. Famously, while creating the model kit for the 1976 Porsche 934 Turbo RSR, Tamiya-san sent his designers to Porsche’s Zuffenhausen factory several times to get the measurements and details just right. However, despite repeated trips there were still doubts about the kit’s accuracy. So Tamiya bought a Porsche 911 and completely disassembled it to get every detail correct. Eventually, the car was put back together, and Shunsaku Tamiya personally ferried Jody Scheckter and his wife to the 1976 Japan Grand Prix in it.
In 2018 Shunsaku Tamiya was given a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Japan Media Arts Festival for his contributions to the hobby industry. His contributions to the imaginations of petrolheads, however, will live on for many more years to come. Shunsaku Tamiya was 90 years old.

data.title: URL-Driven State in HTMX
data.author: lorenstewart
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了如何在HTMX中通过URL管理应用状态，避免复杂的客户端状态处理。核心思想是将状态存储在URL参数中，使页面状态可书签化和共享。文章通过一个示例演示了这一模式的实现步骤：

1. **服务器读取URL状态**：服务器端点读取URL参数并渲染初始视图。
2. **使用表单和隐藏字段保持状态**：通过HTML表单和隐藏字段在不同交互中保持状态一致。
3. **自动更新浏览器URL**：利用`hx-push-url`自动更新URL，确保状态同步。

这种方法依赖于URL作为单一状态来源，通过服务器端渲染和简单的HTML机制实现状态管理，避免了复杂的JavaScript操作。CSS类和隐藏字段帮助保持和反映当前状态。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：URL参数作为状态管理在现代和传统Web开发中的应用及争议

不同观点：
• **支持URL作为单一状态来源**：[podgorniy]认为PHP可能会在Node.js基础上被重新发明，表明对URL参数用于状态管理的信心。[Twey]提出通过使用唯一ID或时间戳实现可书签化的URL，以解决动态内容变化的问题。

• **质疑URL作为单一状态来源**：[btown]强烈反对将URL参数作为单一状态来源，指出UI状态管理中的多个层次，强调不同状态（进行中、已提交、已加载）的复杂性，并提出了一系列实际开发中的问题，如请求顺序、参数可视化等。

• **URL参数使用的历史与回归**：[junto]和[PaulHoule]认为当前JavaScript开发者重新发明了20年前就存在的模式，并指出这些模式在没有HTMX的情况下也能很好地工作。

• **对现代开发工具的批评与建议**：[DimmieMan]对现代JS框架在URL参数处理上的不足表示不满，建议学习Tanstack router等工具，提供更好的URL处理支持。[ac130kz]指出URL长度限制带来的扩展性问题。

• **实践经验分享**：[TimTheTinker]分享了使用jQuery和ExtJS时通过URL hash管理状态的经验，并描述了复杂状态保存的方法。[tomtomistaken]分享了在libmap.org上实验状态保存的经验。[vyrotek]提到了与ASP.NET ViewState相似的状态管理方式。[aitchnyu]介绍了在HTMX项目中使用Rison处理嵌套对象的经验。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于URL作为状态管理的适用性，特别是在复杂状态和多请求场景下的处理。[btown]的评论引发了对URL参数状态管理的广泛讨论，涉及到状态的层次、请求管理及可视化等问题。

• 历史与现代开发模式的对比也是一个重要讨论点，反映了开发者对简化开发和遵循Web标准的不同看法。

• 实践中，开发者通过各种编码和压缩技术解决URL长度限制问题，并通过具体工具和库实现URL参数的状态管理。

Bookmarkable by Design: URL-Driven State in HTMX
When you move from React to HTMX, you trade complex state management for server-side simplicity. But you still need to handle filters, sorting, pagination, and search. Where does that state live now?
The answer is surprisingly elegant: in the URL itself. By treating URL parameters as your single source of truth, you get bookmarkable, shareable application state without needing to install another dependency.
The Pattern in Action
A URL like
/?status=active&sortField=price&sortDir=desc&page=2
tells you everything about the current view. It’s not just an address: it’s a complete state representation that users can bookmark, share, or refresh without losing context.
Quick Start: Three Essential Steps
The entire pattern revolves around three synchronized steps:
Server reads URL parameters
and renders the appropriate view
Forms and hx-include preserve all state
when making HTMX requests
Browser URL updates automatically
with hx-push-url
Let’s build this step by step.

44728833.article_summary:
文章介绍了如何在HTMX中通过URL管理应用状态，避免复杂的客户端状态处理。核心思想是将状态存储在URL参数中，使页面状态可书签化和共享。文章通过一个示例演示了这一模式的实现步骤：

1. **服务器读取URL状态**：服务器端点读取URL参数并渲染初始视图。
2. **使用表单和隐藏字段保持状态**：通过HTML表单和隐藏字段在不同交互中保持状态一致。
3. **自动更新浏览器URL**：利用`hx-push-url`自动更新URL，确保状态同步。

这种方法依赖于URL作为单一状态来源，通过服务器端渲染和简单的HTML机制实现状态管理，避免了复杂的JavaScript操作。CSS类和隐藏字段帮助保持和反映当前状态。

data.author: mooreds

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件工程中的任务变异性、度量问题、架构责任以及开发者角色

不同观点：
• **thisoneisreal**：认为软件工程中的任务具有高度变异性，不能像流水线或销售工作那样简单量化。强行的量化反而会增加摩擦，使问题更严重。引用了《The Principles of Product Development Flow》来支持这一观点。

• **foxbarrington**：强调计划本身可能没有太大价值，但规划的过程非常重要。估计的价值不在于结果，而在于通过观察估计如何随时间变化，理解背后的原因，从而获得洞见。

• **bee_rider**：指出讨论应明确针对软件工程，而非一般工程。认为博客标题应更清楚地说明讨论对象，以免引起误解。

• **jongjong**：认为软件工程师实际上同时扮演架构师、工程师和建造者的角色，且工作基于他人成果，具有动态变化的特点。批评许多公司试图将软件工程师变为可替换的齿轮，而不是赋予他们管理和所有权责任，导致开发者流失和项目复杂性增加。强调软件架构的重要性，认为10x开发者的核心能力在于优秀的架构技能。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：软件工程师是否应被视为可替换的齿轮。jongjong认为这种做法导致了不负责任的开发文化和高复杂性的项目，而其他观点未直接回应此争议，但thisoneisreal和foxbarrington的观点可以间接支持这一批评，即简单的量化管理和忽视规划过程可能加剧问题。

• **readthenotes1**：质疑对土木工程师的泛化评论，暗示不同工程学科之间可能存在误解或不恰当比较，但未展开具体讨论。

• **例子**：jongjong提供了个人经历，描述了一个复杂且 poorly architected 的10年老项目，展示了复杂性和架构问题对开发工作的影响。这一例子支持了其关于架构和开发者角色的论点。

整体来看，讨论围绕软件工程的特殊性、度量与估计的价值、开发者角色和架构责任等主题展开，其中jongjong的观点较为全面，提供了具体案例和批评。

data.title: JavaScript decided my day starts at 9am
data.author: SenHeng
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了JavaScript中使用`new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')`创建日期对象时，默认时间为UTC凌晨，而非本地时间。例如在日本（UTC+9），`new Date('2000-01-01')`实际为`2000-01-01T09:00:00+09:00`。这导致作者的管理仪表板在日期过滤时，遗漏了早上9点前的数据。

**问题原因**：`new Date()`将日期字符串解释为UTC时间。

**解决方案**：明确设置时间为本地时区的午夜，并设定最大日期范围到当天最后一毫秒：
```javascript
const minDate = new Date(`${minInputDate}T00:00:00`);
const maxDate = new Date(`${maxInputDate}T23:59:59.999`);
```

**经验教训**：处理跨时区数据时，需注意日期字符串的解释方式，建议显式设置时间或使用本地时间构造日期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：处理日期和时间时，尤其是跨时区场景下的最佳实践和常见问题

不同观点：
• **日本程序员的时区处理习惯**：koito17指出，由于日本只有一个时区，许多日本程序员在处理日期时缺乏时区相关逻辑，经常使用OffsetDateTime而不是UTC，导致一些细微的错误。例如，后端返回UTC+9的时间戳，而前端根据用户本地时间格式化，从而产生不一致。他提到，很多日本服务不考虑海外用户，因此这些问题不会被修复。

• **时区作为时间参考系的问题**：sgentle认为，时间问题源于没有明确的时间参考系。如果日期和时间没有明确其相对的时区，传递给不同时区的用户时会导致混乱。因此，设计时需要明确时间的参考系，避免隐式时区引发的复杂性。

• **使用UTC作为内部表示**：AdieuToLogic和hatthew建议，所有日期计算应使用UTC作为内部表示，只在展示给用户时转换为本地时间，以避免歧义。

• **JavaScript的Date类问题**：多个评论（如gnabgib, svachalek, tobyhinloopen）提到JavaScript内置的Date类处理日期和时间时存在很多问题，建议使用第三方库如Joda或新的Temporal API来简化处理。

• **具体实现建议**：
  ◦ sangeeth96提供了从HTML输入元素获取日期并设置时间为午夜的代码示例，并指出没有"date-local"输入类型可能导致的陷阱。
  ◦ xyzzy9563建议将日期存储为Unix秒，并在浏览器端根据本地时间显示，以避免歧义。

补充讨论：
• **全球化产品的日期处理焦虑**：CuriousRose提到在开发全球化SaaS产品时，对如何正确存储和展示日期感到焦虑，目前使用Postgres的timestampz和Luxon库，但希望找到更多最佳实践来确保正确性。

• **幽默与历史背景**：
  ◦ kayodelycaon引用MDN文档说明JavaScript日期处理的特性，并幽默地提到JavaScript的历史问题。
  ◦ jedimastert通过Tom Scott的视频幽默地表达了处理时间问题的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于是否应使用UTC统一处理日期和时间，以及如何在设计中明确时间参考系，避免隐式时区问题。日本程序员的习惯做法在国际化场景中暴露出问题，而全球化产品则需要更严谨的时区处理策略。

总结：讨论围绕日期和时间处理的最佳实践展开，重点是如何在跨时区场景中避免错误和混乱，提出了使用UTC、第三方库、明确时间参考系等多种策略。

TL;DR:
new Date('2000-01-01') creates a date at midnight UTC, not local time.
In Japan (UTC+9), that means 2000-01-01T09:00:00, so our dashboard filters missed all data created before 9AM.
The Bug
We noticed something strange while fetching data for an admin dashboard:
records created before 9AM were missing!
Our date filters were simple:
<input type="date" />
Which outputs a simple string like
const minDateString = '2000-01-01';
So we wrapped it in a Date constructor and compared it in our filter
new Date(minDate) < item.date && item.date < new Date(maxDate);
How hard can it be, right? Well...
Why It Happened
I knew that
new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')
sets the time to midnight. What I didn’t know was that it sets it to midnight in UTC.
For Japan (UTC+9), that means the Date actually becomes
2000-01-01T09:00:00+09:00
.
So when we said “greater than January 1st”, we really meant “greater than 9AM on January 1st”. Hence, anything created from midnight to 8:59:59 was excluded.
The Fix
Instead of letting new Date() assume UTC, explicitly set it to midnight. (And while we're at it, set the max date range to 1ms before the next day.)
const minDate = new Date(`${minInputDate}T00:00:00`);
const maxDate = new Date(`${maxInputDate}T23:59:59.999`);
Lessons Learned
new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')
→ midnight UTC
Always check how date strings are interpreted when time zones matter.
For filters, prefer constructing with year/month/day explicitly or append a local time.

文章主要讨论了JavaScript中使用`new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')`创建日期对象时，默认时间为UTC凌晨，而非本地时间。例如在日本（UTC+9），`new Date('2000-01-01')`实际为`2000-01-01T09:00:00+09:00`。这导致作者的管理仪表板在日期过滤时，遗漏了早上9点前的数据。

**问题原因**：`new Date()`将日期字符串解释为UTC时间。

```javascript
const minDate = new Date(`${minInputDate}T00:00:00`);
const maxDate = new Date(`${maxInputDate}T23:59:59.999`);
```

**经验教训**：处理跨时区数据时，需注意日期字符串的解释方式，建议显式设置时间或使用本地时间构造日期。

主要讨论点：处理日期和时间时，尤其是跨时区场景下的最佳实践和常见问题

不同观点：
• **日本程序员的时区处理习惯**：koito17指出，由于日本只有一个时区，许多日本程序员在处理日期时缺乏时区相关逻辑，经常使用OffsetDateTime而不是UTC，导致一些细微的错误。例如，后端返回UTC+9的时间戳，而前端根据用户本地时间格式化，从而产生不一致。他提到，很多日本服务不考虑海外用户，因此这些问题不会被修复。

• **时区作为时间参考系的问题**：sgentle认为，时间问题源于没有明确的时间参考系。如果日期和时间没有明确其相对的时区，传递给不同时区的用户时会导致混乱。因此，设计时需要明确时间的参考系，避免隐式时区引发的复杂性。

• **使用UTC作为内部表示**：AdieuToLogic和hatthew建议，所有日期计算应使用UTC作为内部表示，只在展示给用户时转换为本地时间，以避免歧义。

• **JavaScript的Date类问题**：多个评论（如gnabgib, svachalek, tobyhinloopen）提到JavaScript内置的Date类处理日期和时间时存在很多问题，建议使用第三方库如Joda或新的Temporal API来简化处理。

• **具体实现建议**：
  ◦ sangeeth96提供了从HTML输入元素获取日期并设置时间为午夜的代码示例，并指出没有"date-local"输入类型可能导致的陷阱。
  ◦ xyzzy9563建议将日期存储为Unix秒，并在浏览器端根据本地时间显示，以避免歧义。

补充讨论：

• **幽默与历史背景**：
  ◦ kayodelycaon引用MDN文档说明JavaScript日期处理的特性，并幽默地提到JavaScript的历史问题。

• 主要争议在于是否应使用UTC统一处理日期和时间，以及如何在设计中明确时间参考系，避免隐式时区问题。日本程序员的习惯做法在国际化场景中暴露出问题，而全球化产品则需要更严谨的时区处理策略。

data.title: Two Birds with One Tone: I/Q Signals and Fourier Transform
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要讨论了信号处理中的I/Q信号及其在无线通信中的重要性。I/Q信号常被视为进入信号处理领域的“门槛”，因为其概念较为复杂，令许多人望而却步。文章首先比较了音频信号和无线电信号，指出虽然两者都是实数波形，但I/Q处理在无线通信中尤为关键。

文章详细解释了电磁波作为信息载体的作用，描述了正弦波的参数（振幅、角频率、相位移）如何用于编码信息。I/Q信号的复杂性主要源于“相位”概念，包括相位移和相位角的区别。

为了在不干扰的情况下传递更多信息，文章引入了正交性的概念，解释了如何利用正交载波实现多路复用。正交性在数学上类似于线性代数中的垂直关系，是解决波形干扰问题的关键。

文章分为两部分，第一部分探讨I/Q处理在无线系统中的意义，第二部分将其与傅里叶变换这一信号处理的核心工具联系起来。通过这些解释，文章旨在揭开I/Q信号的神秘面纱。

44729302.article_content:
When a new member arrives at the Signal Processing Club, this is what they find at the club gate: I/Q signals. Perhaps a secret plot to keep most people out of the party?
Some return from here to try another area (e.g., machine learning, which pays more and is easier to understand but less interesting than signal processing). Others persist enough to push the gate open for implementation purposes (even a little understanding is sufficient for this task) but never fully grasp the main idea. So what exactly makes this topic so mysterious?
To investigate the answer, we start with an example audio signal drawn in the figure below that displays amplitude versus time for some spoken words.
For a comparison, a radio signal with digital modulation is plotted below.
Clearly, both audio and radio signals are simple real waveforms plotted with time. Why then I/Q processing is not common in traditional audio applications but an integral part of radio communications? For this purpose,
Part 1 delves into the significance of I/Q processing in wireless systems, and
Part 2 broadens the scope, linking the I/Q signals (also known as quadrature signals) to Fourier Transform, the most important tool in all signal processing applications.
Let us start with the nature of an electromagnetic wave.
An Electromagnetic Messenger
Wireless systems employ an electromagnetic wave acting as a carrier of information hidden in the variations of its parameters.
The Sinusoidal Wave
This electromagnetic wave is produced by an oscillator through acceleration and deceleration of charges in the forward and reverse directions. Since the charges primarily oscillate back and forth, the wave exhibits a sinusoidal form.
A reverse process occurs on the receive side. The impinging EM wave influences the electrons in the antenna through its electric and magnetic fields. The acceleration and deceleration of these electrons under the influence of these fields creates a tiny sinusoidal electrical signal.
In signal processing, a pure sinusoidal signal is also known as a
tone
. The title of this article refers to this tone, as we will now see how this simple signal alone leads us towards a deep understanding of I/Q signals now and Fourier Transform later.
The Message
This sinusoidal wave can be written as
\[
x(t) = A \cos (\omega t + \phi)
\]
where
$A$ is the amplitude,
$\omega$ is the angular frequency, and
$\phi$ is the phase shift.
I/Q Signals: Mystery # 1
Much of the confusion behind I/Q signals is hidden underneath the idea of phase. Therefore, instead of simply using the term phase, I will differentiate between the following expressions.
Phase shift: This occurs when the waveform is displaced to the right or left from the zero time reference (not aligned with how the waveform is defined, e.g., with peak of a cosine or zero of a sine).
Phase angle: This is the angle of a complex number in the plane formed by real and imaginary parts (more on this later). A good example of phase angle is the
carrier phase offset
between the Tx and Rx local oscillators.
Are these different versions of phase related to each other? The answer depends on the context and I will use the term phase shift or phase angle in the article for clarity.
Any of the above three parameters of a sinusoid can be altered with time to encode a message. The information in this message can be
user-generated (e.g.,
wireless communications
),
arising from the laws of nature (e.g.,
radar
, astronomy, remote sensing, biomedical), or
both (e.g., navigation and positioning systems,
beamforming
).
To people familiar with signal processing, the logical route from here is to show that the phase shift of the sinusoid can only be measured in two dimensions, not one. But this approach will require the reader to understand orthogonality, which is where we go next.
Are There More Carriers?
In bygone times, messages were delivered either by homing pigeons traveling long distances or by spies arriving on horseback at the gates of a walled city. For obvious reasons, having more messengers was essential for surveillance and governance. Therefore, kingdoms used to rely on flocks of pigeons and networks of spies.
Similarly, the question is how to get more carriers in the case of a sinusoidal wave to deliver more messages. To achieve this goal, there should be no interference among the carriers as a fundamental requirement. However, as shown in the figure below, when two carriers with different amplitudes (or phase shifts or frequencies) combine, they create a wave with an amplitude (or phase shift or frequency) that differs from both of the original carriers. Clearly, two waves cannot coexist without meddling with each other.
To solve this problem, we need to learn about orthogonality.
A Numerical Prism
In mathematics, orthogonality is a concept that generalizes the geometric idea of perpendicularity to linear algebra.

data.title: USB-C for Lightning iPhones
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款适用于多种iPhone型号的USB-C保护壳——iPh0n3保护壳。该产品售价为49.90瑞士法郎，目前所有型号均已售罄。用户可以登记邮箱以获取到货通知，需求量大的型号将优先补货。该保护壳支持通过USB-C进行充电和数据传输，兼容无线和MagSafe充电，且增强了磁吸效果。不过，某些需要从手机取电的配件（如有线音频设备、外部存储或显示器）需取下保护壳使用Lightning接口。该产品由瑞士制造，采用坚固的深灰色尼龙12塑料。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一款iPhone保护壳及其相关技术特性的评价和讨论

不同观点：
• 一些用户对保护壳的设计表示赞赏，例如其质感和按钮设计（traspler），但也提到了一些舒适度和耐用性问题，比如连接角会刺痛手掌以及扣具可能容易损坏。
• 另一部分用户关注USB-C和Lightning接口的过渡问题。Brajewar建议购买USB-C到Lightning的适配器以解决过渡问题，而ubermonkey则提到家中仍有大量Lightning和Micro-USB设备，完全过渡到USB-C还需要时间。
• 部分用户对USB-C接口的实际传输速度提出了关注，p_ing指出该保护壳仅支持USB 2.0速度，而tamimio则表示如果Lightning接口能提供USB 3.0速度会更好。
• 一些评论提到了对其他功能的需求，例如rahulbisht建议将USB-C接口移到保护壳底部以提高使用舒适性，而DrNosferatu认为增加3.5mm耳机 jack会是一个 killer feature。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户表达了对该项目工程成就的赞赏，但对其必要性提出质疑（rckt）。同时，也有用户表示非常希望购买此类产品（OrvalWintermute）。
• 讨论中还涉及了对技术设备的个人需求和偏好，例如chromatin提到他更希望USB-C设备上有Lightning接口，而saagarjha则提及了与该产品无关的另一条推特内容。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于用户对接口类型的偏好以及对USB-C和Lightning接口过渡的适应程度。部分用户认为Lightning接口仍足够使用，而另一部分用户则渴望更快过渡到USB-C以获得更好的兼容性和速度。

data.title: Dropbox Passwords discontinuation
data.author: h1fra
data.article_summary: Dropbox Passwords sera supprimé le 28 octobre 2025, dans le cadre de la concentration de Dropbox sur d'autres fonctionnalités. 44727653.article_content:
Interruption de Dropbox Passwords
Mis à jour Jul 29, 2025
person icon
Les informations contenues dans cet article concernent tous les utilisateurs de Dropbox Passwords, sauf indication contraire.
Pourquoi Dropbox Passwords ne sera bientôt plus disponible ?
Dans le cadre de nos efforts pour nous concentrer sur l’amélioration d’autres fonctionnalités de notre produit de base, Dropbox Passwords sera supprimé le 28 octobre 2025.
Nous vous recommandons de transférer vos mots de passe vers une autre application de gestion de mots de passe telle que
1Password
, un gestionnaire de mots de passe hautement fiable et sécurisé.
Quand Dropbox Passwords sera supprimé ?
Dropbox Passwords sera entièrement supprimé le 28 octobre 2025. Les modifications apportées au produit se feront de manière progressive. Les dates clés sont les suivantes :
28/08/25 : Dropbox Passwords sera disponible en lecture seule dans l’application mobile et l’extension de navigateur
. Vous pourrez toujours consulter vos noms d’utilisateur, mots de passe et informations de paiement enregistrés, mais vous ne pourrez plus en ajouter de nouveaux. Par ailleurs, la fonctionnalité de saisie automatique sera désactivée.
11/09/25 : l’application mobile Dropbox Passwords cessera de fonctionner
. Cependant, vous pourrez toujours accéder à vos informations de mots de passe via l’extension de navigateur.
28/10/25 : Dropbox Passwords sera entièrement supprimé
. Vous ne pourrez plus accéder aux noms d’utilisateur, mots de passe et informations de paiement enregistrés, ni en ajouter de nouveaux. Ces informations seront supprimées de manière permanente et sécurisée de nos serveurs. La fonctionnalité de surveillance du dark web sera supprimée.
Comment exporter mes données Dropbox Passwords ?
Il existe plusieurs façons d’exporter les mots de passe stockés dans Dropbox Passwords vers d’autres gestionnaires de mots de passe. Nous vous recommandons d’utiliser
1Password
pour importer facilement vos informations de mot de passe et protéger vos comptes à l’avenir.
warning icon
Assurez-vous d’exporter vos mots de passe avant le 28 octobre 2025, sinon vous perdrez l’accès à vos données Dropbox Passwords.
Vous pouvez exporter tous les identifiants de connexion et cartes de paiement de votre compte depuis Dropbox Passwords sous forme de fichier CSV. Pour une expérience optimale, nous vous recommandons d’utiliser l’extension de navigateur. Pour créer votre fichier CSV, suivez les étapes suivantes :
Ouvrez l’extension de navigateur Dropbox Passwords.
Cliquez sur votre avatar (votre photo de profil ou vos initiales) dans l’angle inférieur gauche.
Cliquez sur
Préférences
.
Cliquez sur l’onglet
Compte
.
Cliquez sur
Exporter
.
Cliquez sur
Exporter
pour confirmer.
Ouvrez l’application mobile Dropbox Passwords.
Appuyez sur
(paramètres).
Appuyez sur
Exporter
.
Appuyez sur
Exporter
pour confirmer.
highlighter icon
Administrateurs
: chaque membre de l’équipe devra effectuer l’action ci-dessus pour exporter ses données de mot de passe. Pour voir quels membres de votre équipe utilisent Dropbox Passwords, accédez à la
page Passwords
dans l’interface d’administration. Si un membre de l’équipe a un score de mot de passe, cela indique qu’il utilise Dropbox Passwords. Si le statut indique Inactif, cela signifie que l’utilisateur n’utilise pas Dropbox Passwords.
Que se passe-t-il si je ne respecte pas la date limite d’exportation ?
Malheureusement, une fois la date de fermeture définitive passée, le 28 octobre 2025, nous ne pourrons plus récupérer vos données. Nous vous encourageons à exporter vos mots de passe dès que possible.
Si vous ou votre équipe avez des questions ou si vous avez besoin d’aide, veuillez contacter votre responsable relation clients (le cas échéant),
l’assistance Dropbox
ou consulter notre
centre d’assistance
.
Que vont devenir les mots de passe stockés ?
Après le 28 octobre 2025, toutes les données Dropbox Passwords seront supprimées de manière permanente et sécurisée.
highlighter icon
Remarque :
Dropbox n’a jamais accès à vos mots de passe en texte brut.
Quels autres gestionnaires de mots de passe recommandez-vous ?
Nous vous recommandons de passer à
1Password
, un gestionnaire de mots de passe hautement fiable et sécurisé.
Comment importer mes données dans 1Password ?
Pour savoir comment importer facilement vos données Dropbox Passwords dans 1Password, consultez le lien suivant :
https://support.1password.com/import-dropbox/
Comment importer mes données vers un autre fournisseur ?
D’autres fournisseurs peuvent avoir besoin d’informations différentes pour importer vos données Dropbox Passwords. Contactez-les après avoir exporté vos données Dropbox Passwords dans un fichier CSV en suivant les
étapes ci-dessus
.
Mes données sont-elles toujours sécurisées pendant la transition ?
Oui. Nous continuerons à respecter les mêmes normes élevées de chiffrement et de sécurité pour protéger vos données pendant cette transition.

data.title: Someone made a 128k line PR to OpenCut
data.author: agtestdvn
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要描述了OpenCut项目的一次代码合并请求和相关更新。贡献者donghaozhang试图将480个提交合并到主分支，并列举了所做的多项改进和新增功能，包括视频导出、文本到图像转换、图像编辑、媒体面板导出按钮、AI视频生成、项目卡片组织、Electron构建支持等。此外，还进行了全面的测试套件和文档更新，涵盖视频处理、AI工作流和UI测试等方面。代码改动包括增强`.gitignore`以覆盖更多构建输出和环境文件，以及改进FAL.ai API的错误处理，提供更友好的用户提示信息。项目团队对贡献表示感谢，并提到需要手动审查部分代码以确认其对项目的实用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对AI生成代码提交（PR）及其对开源社区的影响的讨论

不同观点：
• **反对和批评观点**：
  - [fn-mote] 认为此类AI生成的PR显然是垃圾提交，不值得浪费时间阅读，应直接拒绝。
  - [delecti] 表示项目维护者没有立即拒绝这种提交，表明他们比一般人更有耐心，暗指这种PR本应立即被拒。
  - [Ancalagon] 质疑生成此类PR的成本和价值，认为其没有实质性贡献。

• **警示和忧虑观点**：
  - [soraminazuki] 警告AI生成代码将导致大量低质量PR，增加维护者的负担，可能加速维护者倦怠，目前没有好的解决方案。
  - [a2128] 提到自己项目中遇到类似情况，认为AI工具让非程序员可以定制开源软件，但缺乏指导可能导致严重问题。

• **理解和支持观点**：
  - [bee_rider] 认为这种PR可能是出于好意，虽然方法不对，但至少表现出贡献的意愿。
  - [maxbond] 强调不应苛责那些寻求帮助的人，认为他们只是需要指导，而不是嘲讽。

• **技术细节讨论**：
  - [RGBCube] 分享了使用Claude Code的体验，指出其生成过多代码且难以理解小改动的需求。
  - [5pl1n73r] 提出疑问，AI工具能够生成的有效代码规模有多大。

补充讨论：
• **对标题和点击诱饵的讨论**：
  - [cadamsdotcom] 建议修改标题，去掉“Someone”一词，认为其过于点击诱饵。

• **对未来趋势的预测**：
  - [pengaru] 幽默地表示期待垃圾贡献者入侵自由软件项目的一天。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于AI生成代码的低质量和大量提交对开源项目维护的影响，以及如何处理这些提交。一部分人认为应直接拒绝，另一部分人认为应给予指导和理解。

data.title: Online Ruler – Measuring in inches/centimeters
data.author: artiomyak
data.article_summary:
这款在线尺子适用于任何桌面或移动设备屏幕，自动检测设备并按实际尺寸缩放显示厘米和英寸刻度，无需安装。主要功能包括：

1. **自动设备检测**：自动识别100多种设备，应用正确的PPI，准确显示刻度，设置保存后可跨访问使用。
2. **手动设置屏幕对角线**：若自动检测失败，可手动输入屏幕对角线尺寸或使用信用卡校准，确保精度。
3. **信用卡校准**：通过调整滑块使尺子与信用卡宽度（85.60毫米）匹配，达到精确校准。

支持设备和浏览器广泛，包括苹果、三星、谷歌等品牌。使用时建议将浏览器缩放设为100%，切换设备或显示器时重新校准，并确保JavaScript已启用。

• [tzs] 建议校准时将信用卡的一角固定，以便更容易调整其他三个角的位置，从而简化校准过程。
• [brainwad] 指出96dpi作为移动设备的默认值不合适，移动设备通常使用接近160dpi的设置，因为手持设备通常离眼睛较近。
• [LukeShu] 讨论了因X11配置错误导致的DPI问题，以及不同配置下校准结果的差异，并提到许多X11用户的DPI配置错误问题。
• [kasbah] 建议使用`window.devicePixelRatio`代替手动校准，以提高精度和简化操作。
• [gus_massa] 使用信用卡方法进行校准，并建议增加裁切线以便更容易比较，同时建议使用透明规则进行校准。
• [willtemperley] 认为实际尺寸选项对文档编辑器很有用，并提到不同文档编辑器对A4宽度的解释不同。
• [turtlebits] 指出校准模态框在暗模式下不可读，影响用户体验。
• [mkl] 认为对带圆角的屏幕，对角线测量不准确，建议增加宽度和高度校准方法，并使用多点触控进行调整。
• [HPsquared] 质疑设备/浏览器是否报告显示PPI，认为这是Web标准中的一个缺陷。
• [tiffanyh] 提到iPhone 14 Pro被错误识别为iPhone 11，尽管屏幕尺寸相同，但型号识别错误可能导致混淆。
• [wojtek1942] 提到自己的iPhone 15 Pro被误识别为iPhone 16。

补充讨论：
• [gnarlouse] 开玩笑地建议将1英尺改为光在1纳秒内传播的距离，与主要讨论点无直接关系。
• [netfortius] 提供了一个YouTube视频链接，内容可能与讨论主题相关。
• [rahulbisht] 提到在使用27" QHD显示器时，不同缩放比例下校准结果不一致的问题，认为实际尺寸应保持不变。

争议焦点：
• 校准准确性问题：多位用户报告手动测量与网站显示尺寸不一致，表明校准过程存在改进空间。
• 默认DPI设置是否合理：[brainwad] 和 [LukeShu] 都提到默认DPI设置对移动设备和不同配置下的影响，指出标准可能不适合所有设备。
• 设备识别错误：[tiffanyh] 和 [wojtek1942] 提到设备型号识别错误，尽管不影响实际使用，但可能导致用户混淆。

这些讨论反映了用户在使用校准工具时遇到的实际问题，以及对改进校准方法和设备识别精度的需求。

data.title: Show HN: Building a Production Finance Model for Open Source
data.author: positron26
data.article_summary: Positron is developing PrizeForge, an open-source production finance model using Elastic Fund Matching. This model empowers users, allowing programmers to focus on coding rather than fundraising. Funds are matched weekly, creating recurring revenue streams with dynamic thresholds. The process involves enrolling funds, matching them in power-of-two fragments, and triggering payouts when lower levels reach their thresholds. This approach ensures large contributions are supported by matching smaller ones, maintaining equity. PrizeForge aims to fund specific goals like Linux Desktop Environments or Rust language improvements. Initially, funds will improve the platform and support community features. For now, communication relies on third-party platforms like Reddit. The team seeks community involvement and plans to expand beyond software, reinvesting all profits into the company.

Elastic Fund Matching
Loading
Positron
is building PrizeForge, a production
finance model for Open Source.  We're shipping our two-dimensinoal fund-matching prototype
to bootstrap our development and begin iterating & gathering a community.  Check out our
vision
to learn where we're headed.
Sign up now
to take part in the
bootstrapping
PrizeForge Self-Funding Stream!
How PrizeForge Will Work
Unlike existing social finace, we
keep the power with the users.
Programmers
who build our stuff can
focus on coding
not "selling".  Delegates can create
accountability
and
clear communication
so you don't have to log in
every week or have a PhD in Wayland Compositor programming.  Elastic Fund Matching
produces recurring streams with dynamic thresholds.  Week after week, matched funds will
go to the right places without having to raise funds over and
over.
Matching Recurs Weekly
00
:
00
Every midnight on Sunday (GMT -12:00, latest timezone, the middle of the Pacific) all streams begin
matching again.  A weekly cycle enables
responsive
rewarding of those doing
good work while also being friendly to the human-scale rhythm of building things, either
during the week or primarily on weekends.  Ongoing enrollments will
automatically
start matching again, setting new thresholds and recruting new
contributors.
How We Match Funds
enrolled ➛ matching ➛ matched
Enrolling funds sets a
maximum
of what can be matched and paid out each week.
We break up each enrollment into power-of-two fragments, like the binary representation
of a number.
One by one, each fragment begins matching, waiting for other users' fragments to appear.
Higher levels only become available when the level below has enough matched and
matching funds, so large fragments may require waiting on several rounds of matching
to fully match.
Each level accumulates fragments until one of them triggers.
When a level triggers, all matching funds in
all
levels become matched.
Each level's new threshold is set to double its matched funds (as long as levels
below will allow).
Read the
full terms
of Elastic Fund Matching 1.0.0 for a
more detailed breakdown.  Our
general terms
contain more
generic definitions that should vary less between versions of Elastic Fund Matching.
Never
Leaves You Hanging
Large enrollments won't fully match until there is at least as much matched in the level
directly below.
Participation from those doing almost as much is a requirement before
large enrollments can become fully matched.
Nobody wants to do a lot unless other
people do almost as much.  Nobody wants to do more unless a lot of people do more.  It's
just one way we will protect the value proposition of the cooperative side of financing
larger projects.  Protecting the value proposition of large-budget contributors enables them
to equitably participate.
Make PrizeForge Happen
PrizeForge is about building things that need to happen.  PrizeForge needs to happen.
We're using our Elastic Fund Matching to raise revenue to make it happen.
PrizeForge Self-Funding Stream
Enrolled

Make It Happen!
Use of Funds
We are first focusing on features that can deliver value to user communities immediately
while improving on what we have with Elastic Fund Matching.  We can do a lot of good while
completing our vision.
Streams -
Raise funds for explicit goals.  Streams can be broad, like Linux Desktop Environments
or very specific, such as critical features in PipeWire.  A stream for Linux Gaming can
support improvements to VkD3D.  Language ecosystems like Rust and individual programs
like Emacs and Blender can have streams.
Delegated Payout Authority -
While we have big plans for new social decision models, the first step is to delegate
authority so that not every contributor has to evaluate every single git repository.  We
will start with simple systems and build up.
Expanding Elasticity -
We are moving to quickly support cents and to add an at-least
half rule that has cost-averaging behavior when higher levels become too small relative to
lower levels.  Another feature, Elastic Momentum, is in the design phase.
We believe our solutions can expand well beyond software and that we can build a business
with massive impact.  All of
the founding team will remain deeply incentivized to put
every available dollar back into the company.
Get Involved!
Until we develop our on-platform communication features, we are relying on 3rd party
platforms like Reddit and will continue using it later as an out-of-band relief valve.
Subscribe to the
sub-reddit
to keep up
with development and give feedback on new features and plans.  We post short updates on
BlueSky
@positron26
.
Links to our YouTube and others can be found on our
company site
where we also plan to have a blog
with an RSS feed to discuss our tech and perspectives on unfolding trends.
Can you tackle work in our
job
listings
?  Meet up with the team in Busan, South Korea, while we navigate out of the
garage phase.
Generous equity and career

data.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了1929年华尔街股市大崩盘（"黑色星期二"）及其带来的深远影响。1929年10月29日，股市暴跌，道琼斯工业平均指数从381点的高峰跌至230点，交易量创纪录达到1600多万股。这场崩盘前，投机热潮和高杠杆交易盛行，尽管有一些警告声音，但大多数人，包括政客，都对经济前景持乐观态度。崩盘导致美国经济陷入长达十多年的大萧条，投资者总损失超过740亿美元。许多人在崩盘后因财务困境选择自杀，股市一片惨淡。文章指出，崩盘不仅是市场问题，更是经济深层次问题的表现。

44698216.article_content:
TIME
October 29, 1979 12:00 AM EST
Fifty years later: 1929 and all that remembered
Without hearing a word of what is being said or shouted, any experienced trader on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange can listen to the hum of voices around him and tell what is happening. An up market has a different pitch from a down market. But old Wall Street hands vividly remember an exception to that rule. One day 50 years ago next week, recalls David Granger, 76, a senior partner at Granger & Co., a Wall Street brokerage house, “there was a hush over the floor that I’ve never heard since. It was funereal.” Indeed, it was Oct. 29, 1929 —Black Tuesday, the most cataclysmic day of the Great Crash. It was the day prosperity died and the U.S. economy began the decline that culminated in more than ten years of Depression and national anguish.
The panic selling had actually started the previous Thursday, Oct. 24. That was when the Dow Jones industrial average, having already slipped in seven weeks from its record high of 381, dropped by six points on spectacularly high volume to 299. The plunge continued on Friday, on a half-day session Saturday, and on Monday as well. But Tuesday is nonetheless remembered as the truly black day: as frightened shareholders across the country rushed to sell, trading volume soared to an unprecedented 16,410,030 shares,— the Dow tumbled another 31 points, to 230, and it was clear to almost everyone that something catastrophic had taken place. The Dow was down 151 points, or about 60%, from its September peak. When its wild plummet finally stopped in July 1932, the index was at 41, and the stocks it represented were worth around 12% of what they had been valued at in September 1929. All told, in three years investors lost more than $74 billion, which in terms of today’s inflated dollars would be nearly $300 billion.
Signs of impending disaster had appeared all through 1928 and 1929. The speculative fever of the Roaring Twenties had infected rich and poor alike, and vast numbers of people were dangerously overextended. Credit was absurdly easy to obtain, and most brokerages required only 10% cash for stocks bought on “margin.”
That is, one could buy $10,000 worth of stock with just $1,000. Many thousands did, lured into the market by boosters like John J. Raskob, the stenographer turned entrepreneur who built the Empire State Building. “Everyone ought to be rich,” he wrote in an exuberant Ladies’ Home Journal article; anyone who could invest $15 a month, he declared, could eventually reap a profit of $80,000. A Harvard behavioral psychologist named John Watson even found therapeutic value in speculation. “Sex has become so free and abundant,” he theorized, “that it no longer provides the thrill it once did.” Gambling on Wall Street is about the only thrill we have left.”
The politicians seemed to endorse such ebullience. In his last message to Congress in December 1928, outgoing
President Calvin Coolidge assured the country that it could “regard the present with satisfaction and anticipate the future with optimism.” His successor, Herbert Hoover, said that the U.S. would soon see the end of poverty. Only a few public figures raised doubts. One of them was Financier Paul Warburg, who warned in March 1929 that unless the Federal Reserve acted to curb speculation, there would be a collapse and “a general depression involving the entire country.”
Such concerns began to seem more immediate during the summer of ’29, as the economy began to falter. After the market reached its high on Sept. 3, there was a gentle decline, with ups as well as downs, for several weeks. “We tend to blame the market,” says Kidder Peabody Chairman Albert Gordon, 78, who then worked in corporate finance for Goldman, Sachs. “But the market was just a symptom. We were in a bad economic situation whether or not the stock market crashed.”
The decline turned into a rout on Oct. 24, five days before Black Tuesday, and in the days and weeks that followed Wall Street was like a city under siege. Broker Jonas Ottens, 78, then an odd-lot order clerk with Salomon Bros., recalls being pressed into service to telephone customers to tell them that their margined stocks were to be sold off unless they put up more money. “The first call was routine,” he remembers. “But the second man acted so upset that I thought he was going to go out and kill himself. I just refused to make any more calls.”
Leonard Jarvis, 75, now a senior vice president with Shearson Hay den Stone, remembers Black Tuesday as “a bloodbath. It was horrible.” In the days after the crash, he says, several of his friends committed suicide, one by jumping off the Daily News Building, another by leaping from his commuter train. One man asked a friend of Jarvis how someone could kill himself without pain; a drug was mentioned and the next morning the questioner was dead. data.title: Pkgbase Removes FreeBSD Base System Feature
data.author: vermaden
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了FreeBSD系统中引入PKGBASE后引发的一个严重问题。作者对使用"pkg delete -af"命令在传统FreeBSD系统和PKGBASE FreeBSD系统上的不同效果表示担忧。在传统系统上，该命令仅删除所有第三方软件包，不影响Base System。然而，在PKGBASE系统上，该命令会删除几乎整个Base System，仅保留FreeBSD-clibs和FreeBSD-runtime两个包，甚至包括基本的vi编辑器和/rescue工具也被删除。作者质疑这种变化违反了FreeBSD一贯遵循的POLA（Principle of Least Astonishment）原则，使系统行为变得不可预测和危险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FreeBSD系统中使用包管理器删除所有包是否破坏基础系统，以及将基础系统转换为通过包管理安装的机制是否合理。

不同观点：
• messe认为，使用`pkg delete -af`命令删除所有包时，会破坏FreeBSD的基础系统，违背了"最小惊讶原则"（POLA）。他认为，基础系统和普通软件包应有明确的区分，否则用户会误删核心系统组件。
• o11c指出，相关更改是实验性的，并提供了一个链接（https://wiki.freebsd.org/PkgBase）供参考，强调实验阶段出现问题是正常的。
• BSDobelix建议将系统包管理程序和普通包管理程序分开，提出创建`pkgs`命令用于管理系统包，并强调这种分离可以避免端口包的错误影响系统稳定性。他还提到其他操作系统（如Windows、Android、MACOS）也有类似的分离机制。
• altairprime询问原评论者（OP）是否提交了相关补丁但被忽略，并要求了解该问题对原评论者的重要性。
• JdeBP引用Graham Perrin的回复，指出FreeBSD的pkgbase实验中存在多个未解决的bug，强调该机制尚未完成。
• yjftsjthsd-h认为，FreeBSD的目的是消除基础系统和普通包的区别，像其他包管理器（apt/dnf/zypper/apk）一样，通过标记核心包并要求强制删除来保护系统。
• jmclnx回顾了FreeBSD 8.x时代关于将基础系统通过包管理安装的讨论，并询问当前是否正在实施这一改变。

补充讨论：
• 实验性质的机制：多个评论者提到FreeBSD的pkgbase机制仍处于实验阶段，出现问题在预期之内。
• 系统与普通软件包的分离：BSDobelix和messe强调系统包与普通包分离的必要性，以保护系统稳定性和避免误操作。
• 最小惊讶原则：messe认为当前机制违背了这一原则，导致用户误操作后系统被破坏。
• 历史背景：jmclnx提到FreeBSD历史上关于将基础系统通过包管理安装的讨论，提供了一个历史视角。

44730021.article_content:
From:
vermaden  <vermaden_at_interia.pl>
Date:
Wed, 30 Jul 2025 00:28:35 UTC
Hi,
after short discussion here:
- https://github.com/freebsd/pkg/issues/2485
I got REALLY concerned.
One of THE features and selling points of a FreeBSD UNIX system is the 'untouchable' Base System.
Without PKGBASE all the features are preserved.
But when You convert to PKGBASE its ... GONE!
Consider this command:
# pkg delete -af
What it does?
It removes all third party packages on 'classic' FreeBSD system without touching the FreeBSD Base System.
What the same "pkg delete -af" command does on a PKGBASE FreeBSD system?
It kills/destroys almost all of the FreeBSD Base System and leaves only two PKGBASE packages called:
- FreeBSD-clibs
- FreeBSD-runtime
All the rest of Base System is GONE. Destroyed.
You do not even have vi(1) editor ad /rescue is separate not protected FreeBSD-rescue package and its also removed.
WTF?!
POLA is the principle that made FreeBSD such predictable system. Where is the POLA now?
Why the same *pkg delete -af* command on 'classic' FreeBSD system without PKGBASE only removes all third party packages and the same *pkg delete -af* literally destroys most of the FreeBSD PKGBASE Base System?
Its crazy ...
Regards,
vermaden

data.title: Why Metaflow?
data.author: savin-goyal
data.article_summary: Metaflow是一个帮助数据科学家和机器学习工程师高效构建和部署数据科学及ML应用的工具。它提供了一个通用、人性化的基础，解决了数据访问与处理、计算性能、多步骤工作流编排、项目版本管理等问题。Metaflow支持弹性计算资源，集成主流云平台和Kubernetes，并允许使用各种ML库和自定义方法。它简化了底层基础设施的管理，使团队能够专注于建模等核心任务，已被Netflix、CNN、SAP等数百家公司采用。通过Metaflow，用户可以快速迭代想法并自信地部署应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Metaflow框架的优缺点及其实用性

不同观点：
• 反对观点（sito42）：认为Metaflow框架不够灵活，无法实例化或绕过`FlowSpec`进行编程，且类型安全性差。具体指出在跨步骤持久化数据时，需要随意地分配给`self`，这显得不够严谨。此外，认为`step`类似于功能增强的Jupyter单元，限制了利用近年来在ML操作方面的创新。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Metaflow的类型安全性和灵活性是争议的核心。反对者认为其设计限制了开发者利用其他现代ML创新工具的能力。
• 重要论据：反对者提到无法有效实例化或绕过`FlowSpec`，以及跨步骤数据持久化的随意性，都是具体的技术性批评。
• 隐含观点：可能存在其他在ML操作方面更具创新性和灵活性的框架或工具，这些工具可能比Metaflow更受欢迎或更适合特定需求。

44730042.article_content:
On this page
Why Metaflow
1. Modern businesses are eager to utilize data science and ML
​
In the past, data scientists and ML engineers had to rely on a medley of point solutions
and custom systems to build ML and data science applications.
2. What is common in DS/ML applications?
​
Applications can be built quicker and more robustly if they stand on a common,
human-friendly foundation. But what should the foundation cover?
3. All DS/ML applications use data
​
Data
may come in different shapes and sizes and may be loaded from various data
stores. However, no matter what data is used, accessing and processing it shouldn't be
too cumbersome.
4. DS/ML applications need to perform computation
​
Some applications require a tremendous amount of compute power - think computer vision -
while some do with less. Regardless of the scale, all applications need to perform
computation
reliably. Thanks to cloud computing, data scientists and ML engineers
should be able to utilize elastic compute resources without friction.
5. DS/ML applications consists of multiple interconnected parts
​
Consider an application that loads data, transforms it, trains a bunch of models,
chooses the best performing one, runs inference, and writes the results to a database.
Multi-steps workflows like this are a norm in ML.
A workflow orchestrator
is needed
to make sure all steps get executed in order, on time.
6. DS/ML applications evolve over time incrementally
​
Rarely a real-world application is built and deployed only once. Instead, a typical
application is built gradually, through contributions by many people. The project needs
to be tracked, organized, and
versioned
, which enables systematic and continuous
improvement over time.
7. DS/ML applications produce business value in various ways
​
To produce real business value, DS/ML applications can't live in a walled garden. They
must be integrated with the surrounding systems seamlessly: Some applications enhance
data in a database, some power internal dashboards or microservices, whereas some power
user-facing products. There are many such ways to
deploy
ML in production. The more
valuable the application, the more carefully it needs to be operated and monitored as
well.
8. DS/ML applications should leverage the best tools available
​
For many data scientists and ML engineers, the most rewarding part of the project is
modeling
. Using their domain knowledge and expertise, the modeler should be able to
choose the best tool for the job amongst off-the-shelf libraries, such as PyTorch,
XGBoost, Scikit Learn, and many others. Or, if necessary, they should be able to use a
wholly custom approach.
9. Metaflow covers the full stack of DS/ML infrastructure
​
Metaflow was originally created at Netflix, motivated by the realization that data
scientists and ML engineers need help with all these concerns: Any gaps or friction in
the stack can slow down the project drastically. Thanks to a common foundation provided
by Metaflow, data scientists can iterate on ideas quickly and deploy them confidently by
relying on a well-defined architecture and best practices, shared by everyone in the
team.
10. Metaflow takes care of the plumbing, so you can focus on the fun parts
​
Metaflow provides a robust and user-friendly foundation for a wide spectrum of
data-intensive applications, including most data science and ML use cases. Data
scientists and ML engineers who know the basics of Python can build their own
applications, models, and policies on top of it, while Metaflow takes care of the
low-level infrastructure: data, compute, orchestration, and versioning.
11. Metaflow relies on systems that engineers know and trust
​
Metaflow was designed at Netflix to serve the needs of business-critical ML/DS
applications. It relies on proven and scalable infrastructure which works for small and
large organizations alike. Metaflow integrates with all the top clouds as well as with
Kubernetes and systems around them in a responsible manner. It respects the security and
other policies of your company, making engineering teams happy too.
12. Metaflow is used by hundreds of innovative companies
​
Today, Metaflow powers thousands of ML/DS applications at innovative companies such as
Netflix
,
CNN
,
SAP
,
23andMe
,
Realtor.com
,
REA
,
Coveo
,
Latana
,
and hundreds of others across industries. Commercial support for Metaflow is provided by
Outerbounds
. To hear first-hand experiences from these
companies and many others,
join the Metaflow Slack
.

data.author: frizlab
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在使用不同浏览器访问如Yelp等网站时遇到的"使用Google登录"提示问题。在Safari或Firefox中，这些横幅经常出现，但Google Chrome中不会显示。通过在Safari中伪装成Chrome的User-Agent，可以避免看到这些横幅。然而，Chrome虽然不显示横幅，但会在用户已登录Google账户时弹出一个One Tap对话框，这是Chrome原生界面的一部分，无法通过像StopTheMadness Pro这样的扩展隐藏。用户可以在Chrome设置中通过访问"chrome://settings/content/federatedIdentityApi"来禁用此对话框。作者指出，这是Google为其浏览器Chrome提供的优势，可能涉及不公平竞争。

44715166.article_content:
Sign in with Google in Chrome
July 28, 2025
By Jeff Johnson of
Underpass App Company
Many websites such as Yelp show an annoying âSign in with Googleâ banner when you visit.
This is what Google calls
the One Tap user experience
. Fortunately, my web browser extension
StopTheMadness Pro
hides âSign in with Googleâ banners.
What you may not realize if you use Safari or Firefox is that the banners are never displayed in Google Chrome! You can see this in macOS Safari by spoofing the Chrome User-Agent header. In Safari Advanced Settings, enable âShow features for web developers.â This setting adds a Develop menu to Safariâs main menu bar. The Develop menu includes a User Agent submenu with a list of several web browsers. When you select Google Chrome from the list and then load Yelp, the âSign in with Googleâ banners no longer appear in Safari.
Although Chrome avoids the âSign in with Googleâ banners, Googleâs browser still has its own custom annoyance. If youâre already signed in to your Google account when you visit a participating website such as Yelp, Chrome will display a One Tap dialog.
This dialog differs from the âSign in with Googleâ banners you see in Safari and Firefox in a couple of important ways. First, the Chrome dialog is
not
an element in the web page but rather a part of the Chrome native app user interface. Thus, StopTheMadness Pro cannot hide the dialog. Indeed, while Chrome is displaying the dialog, it blocks
all
Chrome extension popup windows from appearing. Selecting an extension in the Extensions toolbar widget does nothing. (In other words, itâs not a bug in StopTheMadness Pro.)
The second difference is that the Chrome dialog can be disabled in Chromeâs Settings. Enter
chrome://settings/content/federatedIdentityApi
in the address bar to access the setting directly.
Select âBlock sign-in prompts from identity servicesâ to stop the dialogs from appearing in Chrome.
If the courts and antitrust regulators are reading—they probably wonât read my blog, but one can dream—this is yet another example of Google advantaging its own browser Chrome over other web browsers.

data.title: Unleashing the Editing Superpower of Emacs
data.author: kickingvegas
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了Emacs在文本编辑中的强大功能，重点介绍了其在处理文本结构（如字符、单词、句子、段落等）方面的独特优势。Emacs提供了丰富的命令来简化编辑操作，如标记、复制、剪切、转换大小写、导航等，共计至少50种命令。尽管这些功能极大提升了编辑效率，但记忆和查找这些命令较为困难，导致许多用户未能充分利用。为解决这一问题，作者开发了Casual界面和EditKit菜单，帮助用户更轻松地访问这些命令。Emacs的扩展性和多年积累的功能使其成为文本编辑的强大工具，使用户能更专注于思考而非机械操作。最终，掌握这些命令可以让写作者更高效地工作。

44728310.article_content:
notes from /dev/null
by Charles Choi ìµë¯¼ì
Unleashing the Editing Superpower of Emacs
29 Jul 2025  Charles Choi
This is a contribution to the
Emacs Carnival 2025-07: Writing Experience
collection of posts on Greg Newmanâs blog.
Emacs boosters often extol its virtues in editing text. But what does that really mean? In this post Iâll scrutinize that assertion. Hopefully by the end of this post, youâll understand why long-time Emacs users so celebrate editing in it.
Any text editor worth its salt will let you type text into a file, save it, and subsequently edit it. The table stakes are to reliably transcribe thought into characters, typically one at a time. If that is all one wants, there really is no distinction in using Emacs over another editor.
Thoughts however
do
have organization and context. Editors like Emacs take advantage of this by providing features that exploit structure. The benefit for doing this is letting users work
less
in transcribing their thoughts to digital form.
For example, in prose, characters are grouped as words, words grouped as sentences, sentences as paragraphs. Emacs offers dedicated commands to manipulate such text structures. Implicit is the notion that Emacs is able to identify different structures in text. As text structure becomes more elaborate, richer commands can be made to edit them.
Working less to capture your thoughts is the
core motivation
for using Emacs.
When text is organized into different structures (character, word, sentence, paragraph,
balanced expression
), different commands can be defined to act on them. Emacs supports the following built-in actions for editing prose:
Marking
Copying
Killing (Cutting)
Transposing
Transforming (upper/lower case, capitalize )
Navigation ( previous, next, forward, backward)
A quick inventory shows no less than 50 commands available to edit text structures given the above. And that is just the tip of the iceberg. Support for pairing braces and quotes, templates, selection based on structure, abbreviation, completion, indentation, and navigation/movement all work in concert to help the writer to work less in achieving their end.
With all this bounty, thereâs a catch. Discovering and knowing all these commands (much less their bindings) has a profoundly steep learning curve. For those few who climb it, my hat-tip to you. For the great mass of others (myself included), they forego using such commands either due to lack of awareness or because they were too cumbersome to recall. Invariably when faced with failing to recall that magic command, one ends up laboriously editing to achieve the desired result, rationalizing that it would be faster than the cost of lookup, disrupting whatever flow state they had at the time.
This is a user interface problem.
My work on
Casual
has been a personal effort to address the usability of accessing so many commands by applying an information architecture to a hierarchy of keyboard-driven menus. Within Casual, there is a set of menus focused on editing which I call
EditKit
whose top level menu is shown below:
From this menu, Iâve aggregated many commands that Iâve encountered (TIL) over my decades of using Emacs. Within this menu tree, Iâve captured commands for editing text structures, registers, and rectangles which have frustrated me in the past due to my failure to recall them.
For a look into what commands are offered in the â(e) Editâºâ menu, take a
deep read of this link
. In particular it incorporates the ability to moving text as described in my earlier post â
Moving Text Elegantly in Emacs
â.
The Emacs Writing Experience and Closing Thoughts
As Emacs was designed to be extensible early on, we now have over
three decades
of collective work in features to support editing different text structures, all with the goal of improved efficiency. Emacs users are fortunate to have access to them as many of these features are not found in other editors. In this regard, Emacs can be seen as an âunfairâ advantage.
The cumulative effect of having access to such a bounty is the net effect of letting the writer devote more time to thinking instead of mechanically wrangling characters on a screen. In using Casual, I have found such access. That said, other users might prefer a different interface. Regardless, the commands doing the work remain the same. If you can use them, you can work
less
to get what you want done.
Isnât that why you wanted to use Emacs in the first place?
Links
Some links to packages and features that Iâve found useful for my Emacs writing experience.

• burnt-resistor认为，近年来日益担忧一种“完美风暴”，即加速主义、种族主义、死亡崇拜的国内恐怖分子会通过黑客攻击、散布虚假信息或操纵无道德的领导人，导致大规模可预防的悲剧。他引用了前UC FBI探员Scott Payne的视频，讲述加速主义者的危险行为，暗示这些极端分子可能会利用技术手段和领导人的无知造成严重后果。

• aspenmayer则关注标题的清晰度问题，指出原标题没有明确州名，可能导致非美国读者 confusion。他修改了标题以减少歧义，并提供了一个存档链接，以帮助读者了解具体事件，即圣保罗因网络攻击受阻，促使国民警卫队介入。

补充讨论：
• burnt-resistor的观点集中在对极端分子利用技术手段造成社会混乱的担忧，带有较强的警示性，并通过引用前执法人员的故事来支持其观点。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于公共技术与政府实际技术差距，以及LLM（大型语言模型）在社交媒体上的应用和操控问题

不同观点：
• [lif] 认为，间谍技术长期以来可能比公众意识到的要先进得多。他通过引用维基百科上关于2012年国家侦察办公室的条目，暗示老旧的间谍技术与当时公众技术水平差距并不大。
• [rasz] 指出，俄罗斯多年来一直在社交媒体上使用LLM机器人，甚至可以在某些情况下引导这些机器人按照自己的指令行动。他还提到，这些机器人有时会因为ChatGPT的信用额度用完而泄露错误信息，并提供了NPR文章和Reddit讨论链接作为例子。
• [FirmwareBurner] 认为，面向大众的AI模型被编程了偏见，以掩盖某些统计现实，从而影响公众的思维和投票行为。同时，政府机构使用的则是无偏见的真实AI模型，而这些模型由同一家公司开发。

• [jdkee] 提供了一个存档链接，但未有进一步的具体讨论或说明，可能意在提供额外背景信息或参考。

争议焦点：
• 公众技术与政府实际技术之间的差距，以及是否存在故意编程的AI偏见以影响公众思维。

data.author: michaelphi
data.article_summary: Piper是一款由AssemblyAI创始工程师开发的AI电话代理，帮助用户自动拨打繁琐的电话，如预约餐厅、取消订阅或与客服沟通。通过Chrome插件，用户可在浏览网页时点击电话号码，输入需求，Piper就会自动拨打电话并处理一切，包括等待和导航菜单。它提供实时更新和通话记录，适用于各种服务预约、账单纠纷和退货等。Piper的智能对话接近真人，用户无需亲自拨打电话，节省时间和精力。该服务可以免费试用，旨在简化那些令人厌烦的电话任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（尤其是LLM）在客户服务电话中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持使用AI进行客户服务**：[zzyzxd] 分享了自己使用AI客服的积极体验，认为LLM可以有效处理初步问题，并将问题快速分类给合适的人解决，提升了服务效率。
• **对边缘案例的担忧**：[jeffwass] 指出AI难以处理复杂的特殊情况，认为AI客服在处理简单查询时可能有用，但在遇到复杂问题时表现不足。
• **对自动化泛滥的忧虑**：[Sanctor] 认为当前的趋势（计算机与计算机通过自然语言交互）是资源的浪费，并质疑未来是否会完全依赖LLM而放弃API。
• **对服务展示和命名的建议**：[runako] 对Piper的展示视频提出改进建议，并指出命名上可能与其他工具产生混淆。
• **对服务安全和隐私的关注**：[gruez] 担心AI在电话中披露身份可能会导致安全问题，因为提供个人信息可能被诈骗者利用。
• **对小企业和个人用户的负面影响**：[stevage] 认为AI客服会让小企业和个人不得不与AI交流，增加了不便。
• **对垄断企业客服的应用潜力**：[drewg123] 认为AI客服在对付像CVS Pharmacy或Comcast这样的垄断企业时有潜力，能有效减少用户等待时间。

补充讨论：
• **技术问题与绕过自动客服的技巧**：[qwertox] 分享了自己通过不回应DTMF音调来绕过自动菜单并快速接通真人的经验。
• **国际可用性及法律限制**：[endigma] 询问了Piper国际电话的可用性，[billconan] 则指出在美国使用AI客服可能违反1991年的法律。
• **用户对AI的抵触**：[qingcharles] 提到人们往往察觉到是AI后就挂断电话，导致使用Piper联系真人时遇到困难。

争议焦点：
• AI在客户服务中的适用范围和处理复杂问题的能力。
• AI客服可能带来的安全和隐私问题。
• 自动化趋势对小企业和个人的影响。
• 使用AI客服是否符合法律规定，尤其是在美国。

总体来看，讨论围绕AI在电话客服中的应用展开，既有对其提升效率的肯定，也有对其处理复杂问题能力、安全隐私及社会影响的担忧。

data.title: Why Are Quiet Spaces Disappearing?
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了公共安静空间（如火车安静车厢、博物馆、图书馆等）逐渐消失的现象及其原因。作者通过个人经历和网友反馈，描述了这些原本应保持安静的场所变得越来越嘈杂，例如安静车厢不再安静，博物馆和图书馆也充满了噪音。这种变化部分归因于疫情后人们忽视了公共场合的礼貌行为，导致安静空间不再受重视。图书馆甚至鼓励社交活动，而非提供安静的阅读和学习环境。文章最后提出疑问：如果图书馆不再是安静的公共空间，还有什么地方可以替代？并暗示这种趋势可能源于人们在疫情后对公共行为规范的遗忘。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：噪音问题及其成因，特别是在公共场所的噪音现象

不同观点：
• [t-3] 认为噪音问题的成因可能与主动降噪耳机（尤其是现代的蓝牙耳机，如AirPods）的普及有关。这些设备让用户可以按需屏蔽外界噪音，导致人们不再关心自己制造的噪音，甚至可能无意中制造更多噪音。此外，他还提到现代的炫耀性消费文化可能也在推动这种现象，人们倾向于使用 loud 和 flashy 的方式来展示自己的地位或存在感。

• [nothercastle] 不同意噪音问题是由降噪耳机或疫情后现象引起的，指出在新冠疫情之前，蓝牙音箱在 hiking trails（远足小径）等公共场所已经存在噪音问题，因此噪音问题并非新现象，也并非由特定设备或疫情引发。

• [robotapertama] 提出文化差异的观点，指出在日本并没有类似的噪音问题，暗示这可能是一种文化现象，不同文化背景下的社会行为规范不同，可能导致不同的噪音接受度和制造情况。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了技术设备（如降噪耳机和蓝牙音箱）与社会行为之间的关系，讨论了这些设备如何影响人们的噪音意识和行为。
• 争议的焦点在于噪音问题的原因：[t-3] 认为是现代技术（降噪耳机）和消费文化的结合，[nothercastle] 则认为这种现象早已存在，与技术无关，而 [robotapertama] 从文化差异的角度提出不同的看法。
• 评论还暗示了噪音问题可能具有地域性和文化差异，并非全球一致的现象。

“Guests are asked to limit conversation and speak in subdued tones.”
“Phone calls are not allowed.”
“All portable electronic devices must be used with headphones.”
“Passengers using headphones must keep the volume low enough so that the audio cannot be heard by other passengers.”
My friend loves the Quiet Car. But there’s just one problem. It isn’t very quiet. Sometimes it’s just as noisy as the rest of the train—or even worse.
“People have no respect for the Quiet Car,” he laments.

This isn’t an isolated situation. All our quiet spaces are getting noisier.
“When did museums stop being quiet spaces?”
complains a Redditor
:
I understand that museums are some of the best educational activities and affordable fun for the whole family. Children are allowed to be excited and express that, but when 200 families are at full volume at once it turns a museum lobby into a wind tunnel of sound. Maybe because I’m not a kid anymore, I notice it more? Was it always this loud?
Some museums even encourage the din. They tell families to bring their children—
and get as noisy as possible
.
But the most obvious place where silence is no longer golden is the library. Not long ago, these sanctuaries were so sacred that librarians became emblems of imposed silence.
Shushing was to a librarian what the Hippocratic oath was for a doctor—or maybe even more sacred. After all, physicians only utter their oath once, while librarians were constantly declaring
sh-sh-sh-sh!
That was a great catchphrase, and served the public well. People go to libraries to study and read—so it really ought to be a quiet place.
I benefited enormously from these quiet spaces during my formative years. I’m certain that I learned more at the library than in the classroom.
Just walking in the door of the Bodleian Library at Oxford was a special experience for me as a student. I felt like I was entering a fortress—where all seekers would be protected from every danger and distraction.
This is the actual door to the main library at Oxford.
Once inside, you had access to a sacred inner sanctum of knowledge and learning. Something like this is even better than the
Batcave
.
Duke Humphrey's Library, the oldest reading room in the Bodleian (
photo by David Iliff
)
Not long ago, even the humblest public library shared in this aura of reverence and sanctity. You didn’t need to be a duke or Oxford don or billionaire Bruce Wayne to enjoy it—it was now provided to everybody at the city’s expense.
So the shushing librarian became a cultural meme and comedy trope—and maybe even served as the unfortunate origin of the annoying Karen stereotypes of the current day. For example, when Bill Murray tries to talk to a librarian’s ghost in
Ghostbusters
, the apparition responds:
Sh-sh-sh-sh!—
before mounting a full-fledged paranormal attack.
That’s great for a laugh, but I now miss those shushing librarians. Libraries are no longer quiet places. They’re as noisy as the pub after a football match.
Books are removed, and replaced with coffee bars and spaces for socializing. In case people don’t get the message, librarians now put up signs
discouraging
quiet study.
Check out this “reading room” at Columbia University—at least that’s what the engraved words on the window proclaim. But an update pasted below tells people that they can expect video conferences and group conversations if they actually plan to read in the room.
The “Reading Room” is no longer for readers.
But this raises an obvious question—if we lose libraries as the last public space for quiet reading and reflection, what can replace it?
Perhaps a few religious sanctuaries remain where quiet can be found. But can you really bring a book to the Christian Science Reading Room? Despite the name, I don’t think that’s allowed.
Why is this happening.
My friend who told me about the Amtrak Quiet Car offers a theory:
This all got worse after the pandemic. People spent months in isolation, and when they returned to public spaces, they had forgotten the basic rules of polite behavior in these communal settings.
They stopped using headphones. They did Zoom meetings on speaker phone. In general, they stopped worrying about intruding on other people’s quiet—and didn’t bother to restrain their behavior or devices.
This rudeness feeds on itself. If I go into a public setting where others are noisy, I feel no need to restrain myself.
Just let it rip!

The mystery over why human brains have shrunk over time
18 May 2024
Share
Save
Jasmin Fox-Skelly
Share
Save
Getty Images/BBC
The brains of modern humans are around 13% smaller than those of Homo sapiens who lived 100,000 years ago.Exactly why is still puzzling researchers.
Traditionally our "big brain" is thought to be what sets our species apart from other animals. Our capacity for thought and innovation allowed us to create the first art, invent the wheel, and even land on the Moon.
Certainly, when compared with other animals of a similar size, our brains are gigantic. The human brain has nearly
quadrupled in size
in the six million years since our species last shared a common ancestor with chimpanzees. However, studies show this trend toward larger brains has reversed in
Homo sapiens
. In our species, average brain sizes have shrunk over the course of the last 100,000 years.
For example in a recent 2023
study
, Ian Tattersall, a paleoanthropologist and curator emeritus with the American Museum of Natural History in New York City, tracked the braincase volumes of ancient hominins through time. He started with the oldest known species, and ended with modern humans.
He found that rapid brain expansion occurred independently in different species of hominins, and at different times across Asia, Europe and Africa. Species whose brains grew over time include
Australopithecus afarensis
,
Homo erectus,
Homo heidelbergensis
, and
Homo neanderthalensis
.
Getty Images
Brain sizes changed as new species of humans, such as Homo neanderthalensis emerged (Credit: Getty Images)
However, the trend for brain enlargement over time was turned on its head with the arrival of modern humans. The skulls of men and women today are on average 12.7% smaller than that of
Homo sapiens
who lived during the last ice age.
"We have very peculiarly shaped skulls, so early humans are very easy to recognise – and the very first ones have extremely large brains," says Tattersall.
Tattersall's finding replicates those of others. For example in 1934, Gerhardt Von Bonin, a German-born scientist affiliated with the University of Chicago at Illinois,
wrote
that "there is a definite indication of a decrease [in the human brain] at least in Europe within the last 10,000 or 20,000 years."
So how can we explain this striking reduction? Tattersall suggests that the shrinkage in brain size began around 100,000 years ago, which corresponds to a period of time in which humans switched from a more intuitive style of thinking to what he terms "symbolic information processing" – or thinking in a more abstract way to better understand your surroundings.
As smaller and better organised brains were able to perform more complex computations, metabolically expensive larger brains simply became unnecessary
"This was the time when humans began producing symbolic artefacts and engravings with meaningful geometric images," says Tattersall.
Tattersall believes that the catalyst that caused this change in thinking style was the spontaneous invention of language. This led to the neural pathways of the brain being reorganised in a more metabolically efficient way, allowing humans to get more "bang for their buck".
In other words, as smaller and better organised brains were able to perform more complex computations, metabolically expensive larger brains simply became unnecessary.
Getty Images
As smaller and better-organised brains handled complex computations, metabolically expensive larger brains became unnecessary (Credit: Getty Images)
"It seems to me that probably our predecessors processed information in a sort of a brute-force way, and intelligence in this context scaled with brain size. So, the bigger your brain, the more you got out of it," says Tattersall.
"But our way of thinking is different. We deconstruct the world around us into a vocabulary of abstract symbols, and reassemble those symbols to ask questions like 'What if?'
"This sort of symbolic thinking must have required a much more complex set of connections inside the brain than was present earlier. My suggestion is that having these extra connections allowed the brain to function in a much more energy-efficient way."
However
other palaeontologists argue
that the fossil record shows that brains began shrinking more recently than Tattersall suggests, meaning the change couldn't be linked to language. The date at which Tattersall puts language acquisition at (100,000 years ago) is also contested.
"I love this theory, I think it's actually brilliant," says cognitive scientist Jeff Morgan Stibel from the Natural History Museum in California.
Stibel believes that a changing climate, and not language, could explain our smaller brains
"But we haven't seen the data to show that there was a decline as far back as 100,000 years ago that didn't result at some point in a reversal where brain size began increasing again. There were declines back then. But then brain size started growing again, so the data doesn't ye

data.title: I designed my own fast game streaming video codec – PyroWave
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了通过网络将游戏画面从一台设备传输到另一台设备的低延迟需求，特别是在本地网络环境下的游戏流媒体场景。为了实现极低延迟，关键步骤包括：从设备A发送控制输入到设备B，设备B渲染帧、编码并通过网络发送，设备A解码并显示图像。每个步骤都会增加延迟，因此需要优化。通常使用H.264、HEVC或AV1等视频编解码器，但这些编解码器往往引入延迟。为了最小化延迟，可以采取以下策略：

1. **去除运动预测**：仅使用帧内编码，提高错误恢复能力和简化编码过程，但比特率会增加。
2. **去除熵编码**：熵编码难以并行化，去除后可以加速编码，但会牺牲压缩效率。
3. **离散小波变换**：作为DCT的替代方案，曾在90年代尝试取代DCT，如今在专业领域有应用。

这些方法虽然增加带宽消耗（可能达到100+ Mbits/s），但在本地网络环境中能有效降低延迟。最终目标是设计一个专注于本地流媒体的低延迟编解码器，即便这意味着牺牲带宽效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视频编解码器的低延迟和高效率选择，特别是在游戏流媒体和本地网络流媒体场景中的应用。

不同观点：
• **Almondsetat** 认为 VC-2 是一种基于小波变换的超低延迟编解码器，具有免版税的优势，并计划开发其CUDA加速版本以提高性能。同时建议人们关注这个编解码器。
• **_kb** 强调了在超低延迟场景中权衡带宽和质量的重要性，并提供了VSF关于其他常见选择的总结链接，适合对该领域感兴趣的人参考。
• **sippeangelo** 提出视频游戏引擎可以与编码器合作以优化编码过程，例如利用游戏引擎中的运动预测缓冲区。然而，专利问题可能阻碍这种创新。
• **keketi** 以讽刺的语气建议使用LLM（大型语言模型）进行视频帧的文本转录和重建，虽然这种方式不实际，但突显了对高压缩比的需求。
• **raphman** 提到了非免费的JPEG-XS标准，该标准也声称具有低延迟特性，并且由于有专利池的存在，可能更适合商业项目。

补充讨论：
• **Thaxll** 分享了VLC创建者正在开发类似的超低延迟流媒体技术，并提供了相关链接和视频资源。
• **Cadwhisker** 指出VC-2使用的算法与HTJ2K（高吞吐量JPEG 2000）相同，并询问了两者之间的差异。
• **freshtake** 认为在本地网络流媒体场景中，可以忽略现代编解码器的许多特性，只需关注带宽和处理延迟，例如微软的DXT编解码器就是一个例子。
• **Fidelix** 对该项目表示赞赏，并期待其被整合到Moonlight等项目中。
• **CharlesW** 建议进行与H.264/AVC（使用零延迟设置）和JPEG XS的基准测试对比，以评估VC-2的性能。
• **kookamamie** 认为NDI（现在由Vizrt拥有）是VC-2的 closest competition，两者针对类似的比特率和延迟范围。
• **monster_truck** 认为如果nvenc表现不如预期，可能是设置问题，llhp预设应该足够。
• **superjan** 强调在某些场景中，低延迟和低复杂度比压缩效率更重要，特别是对于学习视频编解码器工作原理的人来说。
• **nairoz** 建议为特定游戏设计定制化的视频编码器，利用对重要区域的先验知识进行更详细的编码。
• **maxglute** 感慨远程桌面流媒体技术的发展，并表达了对Windows Phone操作系统未能成功的遗憾。

争议焦点：
• 不同编解码器在超低延迟场景中的性能对比，特别是VC-2与其他标准如JPEG XS和H.264/AVC的优劣。
• 游戏引擎与编码器合作的可能性和专利对创新的阻碍。

总结：讨论围绕视频编解码器的选择与优化展开，重点在于如何在不同场景中实现超低延迟和高效编码，并涉及具体编解码器的技术细节和性能比较。

44714914.article_content:
Streaming gameplay from one machine to another over a network is a reasonably popular use case these days. These use cases demand very, very low latency. Every millisecond counts here. We need to:
Send controller input from machine A to B over network
B renders a frame on the GPU
B encodes the frame into a bitstream
B sends the result over a network to A
A decodes the bitstream
A displays image on screen
Dopamine is released in target brain
Every step in this chain adds latency and we want to minimize this as much as possible. The go-to solution here is GPU accelerated video compression using whatever codec you have available, usually H.264, HEVC or if you’re really fancy, AV1. Ideally, we want all of this to complete in roughly ~20 ms.
To make this use case work well, we have to strangle the codecs quite a bit. Modern video codecs love latency since it allows tricks like flexible rate control and B-frames. That is what allows these codecs to operate at ridiculous compression ratios, but we have to throw away most of these tricks now. Since the codec cannot add latency, and we’re working on a fixed bit-rate budget (the ethernet cable or WiFi antenna), we’re left with:
Hard-capped constant bit rate
There is no buffer that can soak up variable bit rate
Infinite GOP P-frames or intra-refresh
Either choice deals with packet loss differently
When game streaming, the expectation is that we have a lot of bandwidth available. Streaming locally on a LAN in particular, bandwidth is basically free. Gigabit ethernet is ancient technology and hundreds of megabits over WiFi is no problem either. This shifts priorities a little bit for me at least.
Back in my student days, I designed a very simple low-complexity video codec for my master thesis, and after fiddling with Vulkan video and PyroFling for a while, that old itch was scratched again.
I wanted to see what would happen if I designed a codec with laser focus on local streaming with the absolute lowest possible latency, what could go wrong?
Throwing out motion prediction – intra-only
This is the grug-brained approach to video, but it’s not as silly as it sounds. Bit-rates explode of course, but we gain:
Excellent error resilience
Even on local WiFi streaming to a handheld device, this does matter quite a lot, at least in my experience
Simplicity
Duh
Consistent quality
With CBR, video quality is heavily dependent on how good of a job motion estimation can do
Intra-only has use cases in digital cinema (motion JPEG2000) and more professionally oriented applications where these concerns are likely more important than squeezing bandwidth. We’re now working at 100+ Mbits/s instead of ~10-20 Mbit/s, so streaming over the internet is no longer feasible outside of peer-to-peer with fiber links. For reference, raw 1080p60 with 420 chroma subsampling is in the range of 1.5 Gbit/s, and it only gets worse from there.
Throwing out entropy coding
Entropy coding is an absolute nightmare for parallelization, which means encoding solely on the GPU with compute shaders becomes an extremely painful affair. Let’s just throw that out and see how far we get. Gotta go fast!
There are codecs in this domain too, but it’s getting very specialized at this point. In the professional broadcasting space, there are codecs designed to squeeze more video through existing infrastructure with “zero” lag and minimal hardware cost. My master thesis was about this, for example. A more consumer oriented example is VESA display stream compression (I’m not sure if it does entropy coding, but the compression ratios are small enough I doubt it). There isn’t much readily available software in this domain, it’s generally all implemented in tiny ASICs. If FFmpeg doesn’t support it, it doesn’t exist for mere mortals.
Discrete Wavelet Transforms
While modern codecs are all block-based Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) + a million hacks on top to make it good, there is an alternative that tried its best in the 90s to replace DCTs, but kinda failed in the end.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UGXeRx0Tic4
is a nice video explaining some of the lore. DWT-based compression has a niche today, but only in intra video compression. It’s a shame, because it’s quite elegant.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_wavelet_transform
A graphics programmer will be familiar with this structure immediately, because this is just good old mip-maps with spice. Effectively, we downsample images, and also compute the “error” between the high-res picture and low-res picture. With signal processing lenses on, we can say it’s a critically sampled filter-bank. After processing N pixels, we obtain N / 2 low-pass and N / 2 high-pass pixels. The filters designed to do this are very particular (I really don’t know or care how they were made), but it’s basically just a basic convolution kernel, nothing too wild. The number of levels can vary but I chose 5 levels of decomposition.
Once the image is filtered into different bands, the values are quant
44714914.article_summary:
本文讨论了通过网络将游戏画面从一台设备传输到另一台设备的低延迟需求，特别是在本地网络环境下的游戏流媒体场景。为了实现极低延迟，关键步骤包括：从设备A发送控制输入到设备B，设备B渲染帧、编码并通过网络发送，设备A解码并显示图像。每个步骤都会增加延迟，因此需要优化。通常使用H.264、HEVC或AV1等视频编解码器，但这些编解码器往往引入延迟。为了最小化延迟，可以采取以下策略：

1. **去除运动预测**：仅使用帧内编码，提高错误恢复能力和简化编码过程，但比特率会增加。
2. **去除熵编码**：熵编码难以并行化，去除后可以加速编码，但会牺牲压缩效率。
3. **离散小波变换**：作为DCT的替代方案，曾在90年代尝试取代DCT，如今在专业领域有应用。

这些方法虽然增加带宽消耗（可能达到100+ Mbits/s），但在本地网络环境中能有效降低延迟。最终目标是设计一个专注于本地流媒体的低延迟编解码器，即便这意味着牺牲带宽效率。

data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
Armin Ronacher在这篇文章中讨论了从Async/Await转向虚拟线程的思考。他回顾了Async/Await为Python带来的好处，尤其是让更多人接触并发编程，但也指出其复杂的内在机制和“着色函数”的问题。相比之下，线程虽然概念更简单，但其API设计不佳。随着自由线程的出现，Async/Await的部分优势变得不再明显，导致开发者需要同时应对Async生态和线程系统。

Ronacher提出，可以考虑全面拥抱线程，尤其是虚拟线程，来简化并发编程。他还强调了结构化并发（如任务组）的重要性，它可以明确任务间的父子关系和信息流动。然而，Python中结构化并发的实现仍不完善，特别是在取消任务时的健壮性问题。例如，使用aiofiles库可能导致死锁问题。

最终，作者建议重新设计线程API，利用虚拟线程解决性能问题，并保持结构化并发的优势。这需要运行时直接处理异步I/O的挑战，以确保阻塞操作不会影响并发执行。
