Skip to content
Tuning Up
What’s Not to Like?
On similes, good and bad
By
Max Byrd
|
July 24, 2025
locket479/Flickr
Similes! I have hundreds of them on three-by-five notecards, highbrow and lowbrow, copied from newspapers, comic strips, sonnets, billboards, and fortune cookies. My desk overflows with them. They run down to the floor, trail across the room into the hallway. I have similes the way other houses have ants.
Why? To start, for the sheer laugh-out-loud pleasure of them. “His smile was as stiff as a frozen fish,” writes Raymond Chandler. “He vanished abruptly, like an eel going into the mud,” writes P. G. Wodehouse, the undoubted master of the form. Or Kingsley Amis’s probably first-hand description of a hangover: “He lay sprawled, too wicked to move, spewed up like a broken spider-crab on the tarry shingle of the morning.”
From time to time, I’ve tried to organize my collection, though mostly the task is, as the cliché nicely puts it, like herding cats. Still, a few categories come to mind. The Really Bad Simile, for instance. Examples of this pop up like blisters in contemporary “literary” fiction. Here is a woman eating a crème brûlée: “She crashed the spoon through the sugar like a boy falling through ice on a lake.” (Authors’ names omitted, per the Mercy Rule.) Or: “A slick of beer shaped like the Baltic Sea spilled on the table.” Sometimes they follow a verb like tin cans on a string: “The restraining pins tinkled to the floor like metal rain, hunks of hair tumbling across her face in feral waves.” Or sometimes they just make the page itself cringe and curl up at the corners: “Charlie’s heart rippled like a cloth spread across a wide table.”
Writing about sex can drive a writer to similes of unparalleled badness. Someone has borrowed my copy of
Lady Chatterley’s Lover,
but these more recent examples might do, from
The Literary Review’
s “Bad Sex in Fiction Award”: “Katsuro’s penis and testicles became one single mound that rolled around beneath the grip of her hand. Miyuki felt as though she was manipulating a small monkey that was curling up its paws.” Or this loving, if somewhat chiropractic moment: “her long neck, her swan’s neck … coiling like a serpent, like a serpent, coiling down on him.” Or finally (my eyes are closed as I type): “Her vaginal ratchet moved in concertina-like waves, slowly chugging my organ as a boa constrictor swallows its prey.”
Strange if not terrible similes can turn up anywhere. The 17th-century poet Abraham Cowley ungallantly compares his lover’s stubborn heart to a grenade that, as she enters a room, “will tear and blow up all within.” Famously but weirdly, T. S. Eliot’s unmedical Prufrock sees the evening “spread out against the sky / Like a patient etherized upon a table.” In the least romantic simile ever worked into a love poem, John Donne likens himself and his lover to a geometer’s “stiff twin compasses”: “Thy soul, the fixed foot, makes no show / To move, but doth, if the other do.” And he takes another stanza to say that the fixed compass leans toward the far one, “And grows erect, as that comes home.” This is the style of writing that Dr. Johnson called, somewhat scornfully, “metaphysical poetry”: “The most heterogeneous ideas are yoked together by violence.” (You might say the same thing about Wodehouse—man, eel in the mud—but he is being funny, not witty.)
Donne’s simile belongs to another category as well, the epic or Homeric simile. Every reader of the
Iliad
knows something like this picture of an attacking army as a wildfire:
“As when the obliterating fire comes down on the timbered forest / and the roll of the wind carries it everywhere,” and so the Achaean host drives ahead for another five lines. Modern prose writers can also unscroll a simile at surprising length. John Updike dives right in: “The sea, slightly distended by my higher perspective, seems a misty old gentleman stretched at his ease in an immense armchair which has for arms the arms of this bay and for an antimacassar the freshly laundered sky. Sailboats float on his surface like idle and unrelated benevolent thoughts.” And one would not like to have been the beefy Duke of Bedford when Edmund Burke imagined how revolutionary mobs might regard him: “Like the print of the poor ox that we see in the shop windows at Charing Cross, alive as he is, and thinking no harm in the world, he is divided into rumps, and sirloins, and briskets, and into all sorts of pieces for roasting, boiling, and stewing.”
Strange if not terrible similes can turn up anywhere. The 17th-century poet Abraham Cowley ungallantly compares his lover’s stubborn heart to a grenade that, as she enters a room, “will tear and blow up all within.”
It takes a dramatic mind to carry a comparison through so logically and so far. The Homeric simile evokes a world far larger than a single flash of thought, however clever. Its length creates a scene in our minds, even a drama where contraries come alive: an army driving into batt

data.article_summary:
本文讨论了数组和表作为函数的概念，并探讨了多维数组和表的结构扩展。文章首先指出，数组是将一组数字映射到同质值的函数，与关联数组和结构体不同。传统数组在一维上操作，而表（如Nushell和Pandas中的）结合了数组和结构体的特性，允许通过字符串键和索引访问数据。

接着，文章详细分析了多维数组，特别是在APL类语言中的应用，说明这些数组可以看作是函数的嵌套，且每个深度的数组具有相同长度。通过函数的柯里化，二维数组可以表示为接受行并返回列函数的函数，这允许进行矩阵转置等操作。

文章还讨论了如何将这一概念扩展到任意维度，并解释了如何通过函数变换重新排列数组轴。最后，文章简要提及了像素结构的表示，进一步说明数组和函数的紧密联系。总的来说，文章提供了一种统一的视角来理解数组和表，并预示了可能的新的变体。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数组与表（Arrays and Tables）在不同技术背景下的实现与应用

不同观点：
• **D4M的优势**：teleforce认为D4M（Dynamic Distributed Dimensional Data Model）通过结合电子表格、表、数据库和图形的概念，基于关联数组数学，提供了一种清新且数学上严谨的选择，尤其是在面对将所有功能都加到PostgreSQL或者整合不同系统的情况下。D4M避免了过度复杂化，类似于SQL的关系数据库概念，但基于新的数学基础。
  
• **多维数组的语言支持不足**：Animats指出，现代编程语言在多维数组支持上存在不足。例如，FORTRAN早就有多维数组，但C、Go和Rust等语言没有直接支持。多维数组的切片问题使得设计变得更加复杂，尤其是在需要支持多轴切片时。讨论最终陷入了细节争论，没有任何实际进展。

• **对标题和内容的批评**：zahlman认为要求写满2000字是无意义的，甚至标题过滤机制也是一个误导功能。如果只是“数组和表”作为标题会更好，带有字数要求的标题通常意味着低质量的投稿。

• **XSLT/XPath的例子**：mvc提到XSLT/XPath提供了一种多轴访问数据结构的方式，这可能对数组和表的多维操作有参考价值。

• **历史背景与FORTRAN的索引机制**：nyrikki提到通过去除类型限制，可以更好地理解FORTRAN的多维数组支持。IBM 704计算机的索引寄存器和位运算结合，为FORTRAN的多维数组提供了基础，这种概念与现代BI工具（如Tableau）的实现有一定的历史联系。

• **代数形状与数组结构**：mpweiher提供了一篇关于通过代数形状构建数组的论文，讨论了如何从代数角度理解数组结构，进一步探讨了数组的多维性和复杂性。

• **数组索引的价值**：galaxyLogic质疑使用非整数索引数组的意义。他认为，通过定义整数值的命名常量可以达到同样的效果，并提出整数索引已经足够。

• **数组索引的灵活性与性能问题**：kccqzy认为大多数编程语言在数组索引上的限制（如必须使用整数）导致程序员不得不使用更通用的哈希表，从而牺牲性能。他以Haskell为例，说明了如何通过更灵活的索引机制提高编程的表达能力。同时，kccqzy还探讨了数组的长度问题和类型签名，特别是对无限集合和代数操作的同构性进行了深入分析。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多种技术，包括Lua的表（tables）、PostgreSQL的广泛应用、XSLT/XPath的多轴访问、FORTRAN的历史索引机制以及Haskell的灵活数组索引，展示了在数组和表的实现上有多种不同的思路和历史演变。
• 关于多维数组和切片操作的复杂性，特别是在现代语言中的支持不足，也成为了讨论的一个焦点，说明这一问题在实际应用中具有普遍性和挑战性。
• 代数角度的数组结构分析和数组索引的灵活性问题，揭示了在数组设计中存在的一些深层次的数学和性能考量。

2000 words about arrays and tables
THEY'RE JUST FUNCTIONS
I'm way too discombobulated from getting next month's release of
Logic for Programmers
ready, so I'm pulling a idea from the slush pile. Basically I wanted to come up with a mental model of arrays as a concept that explained APL-style multidimensional arrays and tables but also why there weren't multitables.
So, arrays. In all languages they are basically the same: they map a sequence of numbers (I'll use
1..N
)
1
to homogeneous values (values of a single type). This is in contrast to the other two foundational types, associative arrays (which map an arbitrary type to homogeneous values) and structs (which map a fixed set of keys to
heterogeneous
values). Arrays appear in PLs earlier than the other two, possibly because they have the simplest implementation and the most obvious application to scientific computing. The OG FORTRAN had arrays.
I'm interested in two structural extensions to arrays. The first, found in languages like nushell and frameworks like Pandas, is the
table
. Tables have string keys like a struct
and
indexes like an array. Each row is a struct, so you can get "all values in this column" or "all values for this row". They're heavily used in databases and data science.
The other extension is the
N-dimensional array
, mostly seen in APLs like Dyalog and J. Think of this like arrays-of-arrays(-of-arrays), except all arrays at the same depth have the same length. So
[[1,2,3],[4]]
is not a 2D array, but
[[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]
is. This means that N-arrays can be queried on any axis.

So, I've had some ideas on a conceptual model of arrays that explains all of these variations and possibly predicts new variations. I wrote up my notes and did the bare minimum of editing and polishing. Somehow it ended up being 2000 words.
1-dimensional arrays
A one-dimensional array is a function over
1..N
for some N.
To be clear this is
math
functions, not programming functions. Programming functions take values of a type and perform computations on them. Math functions take values of a fixed set and return values of another set. So the array
[a, b, c, d]
can be represented by the function
(1 -> a ++ 2 -> b ++ 3 -> c ++ 4 -> d)
. Let's write the set of all four element character arrays as
1..4 -> char
.
1..4
is the function's
domain
.
The set of all character arrays is the empty array + the functions with domain
1..1
+ the functions with domain
1..2
+ ... Let's call this set
Array[Char]
. Our compilers can enforce that a type belongs to
Array[Char]
, but some operations care about the more specific type, like matrix multiplication. This is either checked with the runtime type or, in exotic enough languages, with static dependent types.
(This is actually how TLA+ does things: the basic collection types are functions and sets, and a function with domain 1..N is a sequence.)
2-dimensional arrays
Now take the 3x4 matrix

There are two equally valid ways to represent the array function:
A function that takes a row and a column and returns the value at that index, so it would look like
f(r: 1..3, c: 1..4) -> Int
.
A function that takes a row and returns that column as an array, aka another function:
f(r: 1..3) -> g(c: 1..4) -> Int
.
2
Man, (2) looks a lot like
currying
! In Haskell, functions can only have one parameter. If you write
(+) 6 10
,
(+) 6
first returns a
new
function
f y = y + 6
, and then applies
f 10
to get 16. So
(+)
has the type signature
Int -> Int -> Int
: it's a function that takes an
Int
and returns a function of type
Int -> Int
.
3
Similarly, our 2D array can be represented as an array function that returns array functions: it has type
1..3 -> 1..4 -> Int
, meaning it takes a row index and returns
1..4 -> Int
, aka a single array.
(This differs from conventional array-of-arrays because it forces all of the subarrays to have the same domain, aka the same length. If we wanted to permit ragged arrays, we would instead have the type
1..3 -> Array[Int]
.)
Why is this useful? A couple of reasons. First of all, we can apply function transformations to arrays, like "
combinators
". For example, we can flip any function of type
a -> b -> c
into a function of type
b -> a -> c
. So given a function that takes rows and returns columns, we can produce one that takes columns and returns rows. That's just a matrix transposition!
Second, we can extend this to any number of dimensions: a three-dimensional array is one with type
1..M -> 1..N -> 1..O -> V
. We can still use function transformations to rearrange the array along any ordering of axes.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Frigade产品概念及其落地页的技术和用户体验问题

不同观点：
• **网站性能问题**：
  - [superasn] 和 [moomoo11] 提到网站加载过重，导致浏览器卡顿甚至系统资源被耗尽。他们认为一个更简单的页面会更好。
  - [saberience] 也批评了网站的设计，特别是不流畅的滚动体验和过多的动态效果，认为这是当前许多初创公司网站的通病。

• **产品功能和应用场景**：
  - [flippy_flops] 对Frigade的概念表示赞赏，但提到对AI解决方案往往不够成熟感到疲劳，希望看到更多具体应用场景的展示，如在Survey Monkey上的应用。
  - [twoodfin] 建议将用户体验反馈回馈给产品开发者，认为这样可以为产品经理提供宝贵的洞察。

• **技术实现问题**：
  - [nico] 和 [lyime] 对通过不同角色邀请agent@frigade.ai的机制表示兴趣，但[nico]提出了使用相同邮箱创建多个角色的技术问题。
  - [skeeter2020] 进一步质疑了如果用户不使用邮箱或邮箱不作为用户上下文时，邀请机制如何工作。

• **隐私和安全问题**：
  - [anyg] 对产品的实用性和应用范围表示认可，但提出了客户对信息泄露的担忧，特别是工作流被泄露给竞争对手的风险。他们也建议开发浏览器扩展以扩大产品的使用范围。

• **运行环境问题**：
  - [lawlessone] 询问产品是否本地运行，显示出对产品技术架构的关注。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到网站的用户体验问题，尤其是性能和设计上的缺陷，这可能是Frigade需要尽快解决的关键问题。
- 功能和应用场景的具体展示成为用户关注的重点，特别是如何在实际环境中应用并提供反馈。
- 技术实现细节如邀请机制和运行环境也引发了讨论，显示出用户对产品技术细节的关注。
- 隐私和安全问题被提及，表明用户对数据保护的重视程度。

data.title: Ultra-Rapid Vision in Birds
data.author: downboots
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过行为实验研究了三种小型鸣禽（蓝山雀、领雀和斑姬鹟）的视觉时间敏锐度。研究发现，这些鸟类能够分辨高达145赫兹的光暗交替周期，远超基于其体型和代谢率的预测，并且比其他脊椎动物及人类的最高分辨频率高出约50赫兹。这种快速视觉能力可能源于自然选择的压力，有助于它们在飞行中精准探测和追踪快速移动的物体。研究表明，快速视觉可能是许多生态相似的鸟类共有的特征，而不仅限于猛禽的锐利视觉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：鸟类是否能够通过眼睛运动或其他快速运动来感知高于闪烁融合频率的闪烁光，以及它们对闪烁光的反应速度是否比人类快。

不同观点：
• modeless认为，即使闪烁频率高于人类视觉的闪烁融合阈值，鸟类仍可能通过使用眼睛运动或其他快速运动来区分闪烁光。具体来说，modeless指出，恒定光源在运动中会产生平滑的模糊，而闪烁光则会产生多个清晰的图像。然而，该评论也提到，目前似乎没有方法验证鸟类是否通过运动来区分闪烁光。

• yrcyrc支持modeless的观点，并补充了一个相关的观察，提到有说法称鸟类反应速度比人类快13倍，这在鸟群飞行中尤其有用，因为它们需要快速处理大量视觉信息。这暗示鸟类可能确实能够感知高于人类阈值的闪烁光。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否能验证鸟类通过运动或其他机制感知闪烁光。modeless质疑当前研究方法的局限性，而yrcyrc提供了一个可能的解释，即鸟类快速反应能力可能使它们在某些情况下能够感知到人类无法感知的闪烁。

• 两个评论都提到了鸟类感知能力的潜在差异，尤其是与人类视觉系统的对比，强调了鸟类在快速运动和反应方面的独特优势。

Abstract
Flying animals need to accurately detect, identify and track fast-moving objects and these behavioral requirements are likely to strongly select for abilities to resolve visual detail in time. However, evidence of highly elevated temporal acuity relative to non-flying animals has so far been confined to insects while it has been missing in birds. With behavioral experiments on three wild passerine species, blue tits, collared and pied flycatchers, we demonstrate temporal acuities of vision far exceeding predictions based on the sizes and metabolic rates of these birds. This implies a history of strong natural selection on temporal resolution. These birds can resolve alternating light-dark cycles at up to 145 Hz (average: 129, 127 and 137, respectively), which is ca. 50 Hz over the highest frequency shown in any other vertebrate. We argue that rapid vision should confer a selective advantage in many bird species that are ecologically similar to the three species examined in our study. Thus, rapid vision may be a more typical avian trait than the famously sharp vision found in birds of prey.

44702478.article_summary: 这篇文章通过行为实验研究了三种小型鸣禽（蓝山雀、领雀和斑姬鹟）的视觉时间敏锐度。研究发现，这些鸟类能够分辨高达145赫兹的光暗交替周期，远超基于其体型和代谢率的预测，并且比其他脊椎动物及人类的最高分辨频率高出约50赫兹。这种快速视觉能力可能源于自然选择的压力，有助于它们在飞行中精准探测和追踪快速移动的物体。研究表明，快速视觉可能是许多生态相似的鸟类共有的特征，而不仅限于猛禽的锐利视觉。
44702478.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：鸟类是否能够通过眼睛运动或其他快速运动来感知高于闪烁融合频率的闪烁光，以及它们对闪烁光的反应速度是否比人类快。

不同观点：
• modeless认为，即使闪烁频率高于人类视觉的闪烁融合阈值，鸟类仍可能通过使用眼睛运动或其他快速运动来区分闪烁光。具体来说，modeless指出，恒定光源在运动中会产生平滑的模糊，而闪烁光则会产生多个清晰的图像。然而，该评论也提到，目前似乎没有方法验证鸟类是否通过运动来区分闪烁光。

• yrcyrc支持modeless的观点，并补充了一个相关的观察，提到有说法称鸟类反应速度比人类快13倍，这在鸟群飞行中尤其有用，因为它们需要快速处理大量视觉信息。这暗示鸟类可能确实能够感知高于人类阈值的闪烁光。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否能验证鸟类通过运动或其他机制感知闪烁光。modeless质疑当前研究方法的局限性，而yrcyrc提供了一个可能的解释，即鸟类快速反应能力可能使它们在某些情况下能够感知到人类无法感知的闪烁。

• 两个评论都提到了鸟类感知能力的潜在差异，尤其是与人类视觉系统的对比，强调了鸟类在快速运动和反应方面的独特优势。

data.title: Hexatetrahedral Rails
data.author: julik
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了软件开发中的六边形架构（Hexagonal Architecture）在Rails应用中的实践及其面临的挑战。作者指出，约十年前受领域驱动设计（DDD）和Alastair Cockburn的六边形架构启发，许多Rails项目采用了这种架构风格，但如今这些项目在升级和维护时遇到了复杂性问题。作者戏称这些项目为“hexatetrahedral Rails applications”，因为它们常常引入了超出预期好处的复杂性，甚至变成了不必要的“ complicationments”。

六边形架构的初衷是通过模块化和小接口组合实现解耦，但在Rails中实施时，往往导致不必要的间接层和维护负担。作者质疑这种解耦的必要性，尤其当应用的主要交付方式是Web时。除非应用需要嵌入到其他程序中，否则过度解耦可能弊大于利。作者建议从过去的实践中提取有价值的经验，而非盲目追随时尚。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rails中的数据操作、仓库模式（Repositories）的应用及其合理性、与框架解耦的必要性

不同观点：
• [pqdbr] 认为文章中关于 `user.log_entries` 在 Rails 7+ 中行为的说法不正确。根据其测试，`user.log_entries` 会如预期返回一个 `LogEntry` 实例，而不是文章所说的会返回空数组直到重新加载。
• [0x457] 认为仓库模式有其合理性。如果直接使用 ActiveRecord，那么无法责怪初级开发者在每次请求时对表进行全表扫描。同时，不理解为什么要替换 ActiveRecord 来创建仓库，而不是在其基础上构建。
• [static_void] 表示庆幸文章是讽刺和批评，因为只是出于猎奇心理点击进来。将其比喻为软件架构中的“看车祸现场”。
• [yakshaving_jgt] 支持与框架解耦的观点，并引用 Gary Bernhardt 的 Destroy All Software 视频系列作为支持。认为解耦、自定义持久层函数、通过自动化测试驱动设计都是好主意，并应避免昂贵的集成测试。
• [TOGoS] 对使用 `UsersRepository.find_all_with_email(...)` 的方式感到不解，认为如果要加载对象，应该从一个特定的仓库加载，而不是从一个类的仓库加载。同时指出，当应用需要从多个数据源获取数据时，数据与特定数据源的紧密耦合会造成混乱。这也是其不使用 Rails 的原因。
• [ryandv] 提供了一个历史背景链接，指向一篇在上次广泛讨论中标题具有挑衅性的文章，为讨论提供了更多的背景信息。
• [aaroninsf] 提供了一个关于类比的链接，为不熟悉文中类比的读者提供参考。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了 Rails 框架中的数据操作细节（如 `user.log_entries` 的行为）以及仓库模式的实际应用价值。
• 讨论了与框架解耦的必要性及其带来的好处，特别是在多数据源情况下。
• 引用了外部资源和历史背景信息，为讨论提供了更多的上下文和深度。

争议焦点：
• Rails 中数据操作的预期行为，特别是 `user.log_entries` 在不同版本中的表现。
• 仓库模式的应用是否合理，特别是在使用 ActiveRecord 的情况下。
• 与框架解耦的必要性和实现方式，特别是对于多数据源的应用场景。

44701001.article_content:
Software is a creative endeavor and a craft. And like any creative endeavor and any craft, it is subject to fashions. About a decade ago, one of those fashions was
Hexagonal Rails
largely inspired by the DDD book, but also by the original Hexagonal Architecture work by Dr. Cockburn.
Some of these applications are now up for their Rails upgrade and an “oil change,” and it’s interesting to see them in the wild and how they get perceived through the lens of the years that have gone by since then. I call them “hexatetrahedral Rails applications” - in jest, of course - because they often end up presenting complexities that go beyond the intended benefits, sometimes becoming what I’d describe as
complications
or even
complicationments.
And while I appreciate the good intentions behind this approach, I’ve found myself questioning whether the benefits outweigh the costs in most cases. So I felt that - at the very least - I want to suss out why it is valuable, but also - figure out how I define/detect those apps in the wild, and how to understand their
raison d’être
well. Not to be snarky - but to look for the nuggets of wisdom in there which can be useful for us, today.
Why the vitriol?
I use this term from time to time because I’ve observed teams struggling with the maintenance and evolution of applications architected this way. While most “adult” Rails codebases (anywhere from 7 to 18 years of age) tend to be messy, that mess usually is within the confines of the
knowable
and well-discovered Rails builtins - ActiveRecord, ERB, controllers, helpers, the works.
Hexatetrahedral apps, in contrast, present a different paradigm which is usually (not always) supplemented by a large amount of non-default tooling. That tooling also needs updating. It needs to be understood. It is often coming from a single person who might have either abandoned it, or decided to redo it nearly from scratch. The burden of maintaining those “divergent” dependencies is much higher than “just updating the Rails app.”
And all of that also comes with a lot of dogma, usually:
No, you shall not do a
User.where
directly, you have to do a
UsersRepository.find_all_with_email(...)
.
That setup often adds indirections that don’t necessarily improve the expressiveness of the codebase, while making changes more complex - because, for every change, the engineer needs to decide whether they will be dropping this “repository” or “domain design” approach and just hit the ActiveRecord subclasses directly - or keep up the approach of going through “the published pathways.”
The Original Premise
It is actually very instructive to try and understand the hexagonal architecture proposition – the original one. Alastair Cockburn, the author of the architecture, actually recently did a video presentation that is
worth a watch
– if you have touched a hexatetrahedral Rails application recently you will realize that this is not what the architecture implies.
The original premise is actually quite sound, and shares similarities with other well-regarded layering propositions such as “functional core, imperative shell” and is based on composition of modules over small interfaces. But to have the luxuries of that composition it is hardly necessary to subscribe to the entire bill of materials thought customary for a “Hexagonal Rails” setup.
Why It Kind Of Fails
And the arguments for doing a “hexagonal architecture” inside Rails quickly get thin. “Decouple from Rails”? Your app is a Rails app. Why would you want to “decouple” from Rails if the main delivery vehicle of your app is… the web and Rails? Ok, I did do one app that had even a modicum of success and that had CLI and web frontends, whereby in both the “meat” of the application was being exercised fully - that was
tracksperanto.
But other use cases are quite thin in the wild. A GUI version of your app? If you already have a Ruby runtime in place and you already need most of the dependencies - you can run a script that wraps a Rails Executor around most key mutating actions and you are good to go.
And that’s even mostly ignoring the fact that the prevalent majority of native GUI toolkit bindings for Ruby are abysmally bad and not getting better, except for calling Java UI libraries from jRuby. CLI for a point-of-sales terminal or something similar? You can let it talk to your application over what’s called a “driving adapter” in the terminology of Dr. Cockburn, but you don’t need to “decouple from Rails.” Most of the conversations I’ve had with people about this kind of boiled down to a circular argument, namely: “we need to decouple from Rails to be less coupled to Rails.”
Why
the said decoupling was so essential - I rarely could decipher.
Now, it is a very valid desire to have this decoupling if your deliverable is, in itself, a
library-like
thing that you want to make embeddable in other applications. But if that’s the goal - there are less rigid architectures which allow you the same. Make it a duo of two files (mod

data.article_summary: 这篇文章提到的是一个名为"gtrsnipe"的代码库，由用户"scottvr"创建并公开分享。目前，该项目有12个星标（Star），但还没有被其他用户复刻（Fork）。文章还指出，要更改通知设置，用户必须先登录自己的账户。文章内容简短，主要涉及项目的关注情况和基本的互动操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Github上一个音乐映射工具（gtrsnipe）的功能、应用及局限性

不同观点：
• **关注指法和和弦形状**：[omoikane] 对工具根据指伸距离评分表示关注，但指出工具没有考虑和弦形状问题，尤其是避免大横按和弦的需求，并建议加入对变调夹的支持。

• **工具转换应用**：[jarmitage] 提出该工具是否能将MIDI转换为http://strudel.cc的小型符号表示法，并提到之前的一个相关项目（midi_to_tidalcycles），暗示了对该工具扩展应用的兴趣。

• **工具的可靠性与重复段处理**：[robbomacrae] 对工具在处理乐谱重复段方面的能力表示关注，并提到自己在博士研究中类似的工具，强调了在处理乐谱相似性方面的挑战。

• **工具的局限性**：[nartho] 指出该工具仅限于6弦吉他和3种调弦方式，认为这限制了其在更广泛音乐类型中的应用。

• **支持与兴趣**：[jmkr] 对工具表示赞赏，特别是对ABC符号的支持，并表示有兴趣将其用于和弦图制作。

补充讨论：
• **其他类似工具**：[westurner] 提到其他类似工具如tayuya、Kord，并讨论了这些工具的功能和潜在应用，如LilyPond输出和文本界面创建。同时，还提到了与音效处理相关的工具和库，如pedalboard，暗示了对工具集成的可能性探讨。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于工具的功能局限性（如支持的弦数和调弦方式）以及在处理复杂乐谱（如重复段和特定和弦形状）方面的能力。这些争议反映出用户对工具扩展性和灵活性的期望。

• 主要争议在于工具的功能局限性（如支持的弦数和调弦方式）以及在处理复杂乐谱（如重复段和特定和弦形状）方面的能力。这些争议反映出用户对工具扩展性和灵活性的期望。

data.author: Brajeshwar

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube对未成年人账户的禁令及其影响

不同观点：
• WantonQuantum指出，该禁令仅针对账户持有，并不禁止16岁以下人群观看YouTube视频，因此影响有限。
• forgotoldacc认为，过去人们呼吁保护未成年人免受不良内容影响，而现在政府实施这些法律后，人们却感到困惑和愤怒，因为需要提交身份验证，这可能会导致更严重的隐私问题。
• simpaticoder建议，YouTube可以推出一个专门的教育平台，如education.youtube.com，以过滤内容，从而保留教育性内容，减少不适当内容的暴露。
• spicyusername认为，对10-12岁以下的儿童实施全面禁令是可以理解的，但对于年龄较大的儿童，全面禁止可能过于严厉，且执行上存在困难。
• m101提出，YouTube或许会推出没有YouTube Shorts的版本，因为Shorts可能使政府有理由进行投诉。
• seydor担心，这样的禁令会激化青少年对成年人的敌意，可能导致不良的社会后果。
• non-认为，青少年有能力绕过内容禁令，这样的措施只会促使他们更早接触到VPN等工具。
• SilverElfin质疑，为什么像澳大利亚、英国、欧盟等国家突然变得支持审查，这与他们作为自由民主国家的形象不符。
• like_any_other指出，应利用家长控制软件而非扩大国家监控，但政府在公众压力下选择了这一措施。
• 9rx讨论了YouTube作为视频分享平台与社交媒体的区别，认为两者在实际使用中已变得难以区分。
• asyx强调，YouTube对其职业生涯有重要帮助，尤其在学习方面，禁令将剥夺青少年获取丰富学习资源的途径。
• Jalad分享了个人经验，认为YouTube在教育方面非常有价值，但承认当前的人工智能和有毒内容环境与过去不同。
• ccppurcell反驳认为，YouTube上存在大量不当内容，且容易接触到，因此需要严格管理。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于如何平衡保护未成年人免受不良内容影响与保留教育性内容之间的关系。
• 另一个讨论点是执行此类禁令的可行性和潜在后果，包括隐私问题和对青少年心理的影响。
• 有人质疑这些措施是否会有效，或是否会导致更严重的问题，如青少年绕过禁令和隐私泄露。
• 对政府和科技公司在处理这些问题上的角色和责任存在不同看法。

data.title: Show HN: A high-altitude low-power flight computer for high-altitude balloons
data.author: mpkendall
data.article_summary: Tiny4FSK是一个旨在用于高空气球（HAB）的超小型高空追踪系统，目前处于研发和测试阶段。该项目使用1节AA电池供电，可持续工作10-17小时，采用4FSK调制和Horus Binary v2系统。主要硬件包括SAMD21G18A微控制器、Si4063传输模块、ATGM336H GPS模块、BME280环境传感器、TPS61200升压转换器和MCP1700降压转换器。代码采用模块化设计，支持扩展和自定义配置。天线系统使用70cm业余无线电频段（420-450 MHz），需要FCC颁发的业余无线电许可证，并配备优化的四分之一波长单极天线，以实现高效信号传输。项目文件和代码可在GitHub上获取，供爱好者和研究者使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高空气球（HAB）项目的技术实现与挑战

不同观点：
• [支持与兴趣] @normaldotcom 表示对HAB项目的发展很感兴趣，提到自己曾开发过APRS跟踪器和WSPR版本，并分享了相关项目链接。他鼓励项目团队继续努力。
• [个人经验与挑战] @dylan604 分享了自己过去尝试气球发射和自制飞行计算机的经验，提到在处理传感器数据和内存限制时遇到困难，最终使用了Arduino Mega。他还指出由于缺乏无线电操作许可，他们的跟踪方式很原始，并提醒其他人记得在气球上附上联系信息。
• [商业机会] @guywithahat 提到Sceye公司正在招聘并从事相关工作，但工作地点要求居住在沙漠地区。
• [技术设想与限制] @paulgerhardt 提到一个朋友经常放飞气球，气球经过中东或朝鲜等敏感地区，他设想通过远程指令控制轻量相机，但由于带宽和负载限制（必须在100克以内，带宽约30字节/分钟），实现起来有难度。他还提出有趣的想法，即在气球返回友好地区时投放相机内存卡。
• [技术改进建议] @Catbert59 对项目表现出兴趣，并提出了一些技术改进建议，包括使用2.4GHz LoRa进行高率遥测和利用433MHz进行低率遥测，并提到使用STMicroelectronics的STM32U系列芯片和ePeas的能量收集器。

补充讨论：

Tiny4FSK - The Lightweight Horus Binary Tracker Built for HABs
WORK IN PROGRESS
- Please do not rely on this as your only tracking system. Tiny4FSK is still in the R&D phase of development and testing.
NEW
- Incorporated new Rev. 4 PCB files and code (12/21/24).
STATE
- Rev. 4 is fully working! Currently testing.
What is the Tiny4FSK project?
Tiny4FSK aims to be an ultra-tiny high-altitude tracking system. It runs on 1 AA battery that lasts for 10-17 hours (a few seconds between position updates, can run longer if there's a longer delay). It runs on 4FSK (4-frequency shift keying), which means that it separates tones into 4 separate frequencies. Upon this, it uses the
Horus Binary v2
system, which is a relatively modern system popularly used with
RS41ng
.
What are High-Altitude Balloons?
High altitude balloons (HABs) allow space science enthusiasts to launch their own payloads to near-space (30km) at a cost of hundreds of dollars instead of millions of dollars.  This can be done for atmospheric research, breathtaking imagery, and scientific experimentation. While demanding meticulous planning, safety adherence, and technical skill in electronics and mechanics, this hobby rewards makers with a chance to get hands on with projects like electronic data loggers, camera systems, wireless communications, and more.
Parts and Materials
This codebase is meant to work with the Tiny4FSK PCB, also available on this GitHub repository. Key components include:
Microcontroller
-
SAMD21G18A
. A modern Cortex-M0+ microcontroller by Microchip.
TX Module
-
Si4063
. A transceiver from Silicon Labs, similar to the Si4032 on RS41 radiosondes.
GPS RX Module
-
ATGM336H
. A cheap, high-performance GPS module from ZHONGKEWEI.
Environmental Sensor
-
BME280
. A proven sensor from Bosch for measuring temperature, pressure, and humidity.
Boost Converter
-
TPS61200
. Boosts 1.5V battery level to 3.3V for the rest of the board from Texas Instruments.
LDO Step-Down
-
MCP1700
. A step-down converter from Microchip.
This list is not exhaustive. Additional components and passives are detailed in the schematic files.
The Codebase
This code is modular and separated into several different files for easy expansion. These files are listed below:
Tiny4FSK.ino
- Main Arduino file with control flow.
config.h
- Configuration file for user parameters.
crc_calc.cpp and crc_calc.h
- CRC16 generator files for parity bits.
horus_l2.cpp and horus_l2.h
- Horus layer 2 file, Golay error correction algorithm.
voltage.cpp and voltage.h
- Voltage detection using ADC values.
si4063.cpp and si4063.h
- Si4063 driver files for radio transmission.
4fsk_mod.cpp and 4fsk_mod.h
- 4FSK modulation functions.
delay_timer.cpp and delay_timer.h
- Low-level delay functions based on timers.
utils.cpp and utils.h
- A collection of utility functions.
Step by Step Setup Guide
Setting up the PCB
Carefully
snap off the USB breakout board from the board.
Solder on the female 1x4 header row onto the underside of the USB breakout. Solder on the 1x4 male header row to the corresponding adjecent pins (labeled VSS, GND, D-, and D+).
3. To program the board, attach the USB breakout board as shown in the photo.  Once the board is programmed, the USB breakout board can be removed for flight.
Antenna System
This system relies on the 70cm amateur radio band (420-450 MHz in the US), and requires an amateur radio license, issued by the FCC, to operate. A pre-cut braided copper
monopole
is included, optimized to transmit on this frequency. The included antenna is a quarter-wave monopole, meaning that the antenna is just a quarter of the wavelength of the signal, and yet it maintains a good SWR (quantification of how much signal is reflected back into the transmitter). There is a pad that supports a quarter-wave monopole, but also provides grounding pads for a coax connector if alternate antennas wish to be used.
Why does this work?
A 1/4 wave monopole antenna works by using a quarter of the wavelength of the signal, which creates a resonant frequency that efficiently radiates radio waves. The ground plane acts as a reflector, effectively doubling the antenna's length and

data.title: Reuters used Gemini Pro to collect and analyze prison temperature data
data.author: gaws
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国部分州立监狱囚犯的生活条件，特别是在高温环境下缺乏空调设施的人道性问题。

不同观点：
• **观点一**（人道主义立场）：[kylecazar] 认为，将囚犯关在高温、没有空调的牢房中是不人道的。尤其在德州等高温地区，夏季气温极高，缺乏基本的生活条件如空调是不可接受的。虽然不要求达到像斯堪的纳维亚国家那样的高标准，但至少应该保证基本的人道条件。该观点引用了路透社的调查数据，指出在29个州中，近50%的州立监狱住房单元部分或完全没有空调，其中德州的情况最为严重，58个设施中有51个缺乏空调。

• **可能的反对方观点**（资源限制或惩罚立场）：虽然未在评论中直接出现，但可以推测出一种可能的反对方观点，即监狱系统的资源有限，无法为所有设施配备空调；或者认为囚犯因其犯罪行为失去了某些权利，包括享受舒适生活条件的权利。因此，即使条件较为艰苦，也可以被视为对他们的一种惩罚或威慑。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：评论中提到的主要争议在于如何界定“人道条件”的底线。一方认为即使在监狱中，囚犯的基本生活条件也应得到保障，特别是在极端气候条件下如德州的高温。另一方可能认为，囚犯的生活条件不需要达到一般社会的标准，艰苦的环境反而是刑罚的一部分。

• **数据支持**：[kylecazar] 引用了路透社的调查和德州刑事司法部门的数据，增强了对监狱设施中缺乏空调这一问题的关切，表明这并非个别现象，而是广泛存在于多个州，尤其是德州。

• **道德与现实的平衡**：讨论中隐含了对道德标准与现实资源限制的权衡问题。即使不要求达到北欧国家的高福利标准，基本的居住条件如空调是否应成为普遍标准，仍是一个值得进一步讨论的议题。

• **数据支持**：[kylecazar] 引用了路透社的调查和德州刑事司法部门的数据，增强了对监狱设施中缺乏空调这一问题的关切，表明这并非个别现象，而是广泛存在于多个州，尤其是德州。

• **道德与现实的平衡**：讨论中隐含了对道德标准与现实资源限制的权衡问题。即使不要求达到北欧国家的高福利标准，基本的居住条件如空调是否应成为普遍标准，仍是一个值得进一步讨论的议题。

data.title: The case for memes as a new form of comics
data.author: ProAm
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了互联网对漫画职业的影响，特别是网络 meme 作为一种新型数字漫画的兴起。美国俄亥俄州立大学英语教授 Michelle Ann Abate 认为，meme，尤其是图像宏（image macros），在认知和创作方式上与单格漫画有相似之处。她指出，虽然漫画通常由艺术家同时创作图像和文字，而 meme 则是对已有图像进行改编，但这种做法类似于音乐中的采样，最终仍是一种原创艺术。Abate 还提到，《纽约客》杂志的漫画标题比赛本质上是一种 meme 生成器，而 meme 的在线特性也影响了其格式，例如多格 meme 通常垂直排列以适应手机阅读。总体而言，meme 代表了漫画 genre 的新演变阶段，视觉与文字元素共同创造幽默。

It's undeniable that the rise of the Internet had a profound impact on cartooning as a profession, giving cartoonists both new tools and a new publishing and/or distribution medium. Online culture also spawned the emergence of viral memes in the late 1990s. Michelle Ann Abate, an English professor at The Ohio State University, argues in
a paper
published in INKS: The Journal of the Comics Studies Society, that memes—specifically, image macros—represent a new type of digital comic, right down to the cognitive and creative ways in which they operate.
"One of my areas of specialty has been graphic novels and comics," Abate told Ars. "I've published multiple books on various aspects of comics history and various titles: everything from Charles Schulz's
Peanuts
to
The Far Side
, to
Little Lulu
to
Ziggy
to
The Family Circus
. So I've been working on comics as part of the genres and texts and time periods that I look at for many years now."
Her most recent book is 2024's
Singular Sensations: A Cultural History of One-Panel Comics in the United States
, which Abate was researching when the COVID-19 pandemic hit in 2020. "I was reading a lot of single panel comics and sharing them with friends during the pandemic, and memes were something we were always sharing, too," Abate said. "It occurred to me one day that there isn't a whole lot of difference between the single panel comics I'm sharing and the memes. In terms of how they function, how they operate, the connection of the verbal and the visual, there's more continuity than there is difference."
So Abate decided to approach the question more systematically. Evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins coined the word "meme" in his 1976 popular science book,
The Selfish Gene
, well before the advent of the Internet age. For Dawkins, it described a "unit of cultural transmission, or a unit of information": ideas, catchphrases, catchy tunes, fashions, even arch building.
Credit:
Jennifer Ouellette via imgflp
In a 21st century context, "meme" refers to a piece of online content that spikes in popularity and gets passed from user to user, i.e., going viral. These can be single images remixed with tailored text, such as "
Distracted Boyfriend
," "
This Is Fine
," or "
Batman Slapping Robin
." Or they can feature multiple panels, like "
American Chopper
." Furthermore, "Memes can also be a gesture, they can be an activity, they can be a video like the
Wednesday
dance or the ice bucket challenge," said Abate. "It's become such a part of our lexicon that it's hard to imagine a world without memes at this point."
For Abate, Internet memes are clearly related to sequential art like comics, representing a new stage of evolution in the genre. In both cases, the visual and verbal elements work in tandem to produce the humor.
Granted, comic artists usually create both the image and the text, whereas memes adapt preexisting visuals with new text. Some might consider this poaching, but Abate points out that cartoonists like Charles Schulz have long used stencil templates (a static prefabricated element) to replicate images, a practice that is also used effectively in, say,
Dinosaur Comics
. And meme humor depends on people connecting the image to its origin rather than obscuring it. She compares the practice to sampling in music; the end result is still an original piece of art.
In fact, The New Yorker's hugely popular cartoon caption contest—in which the magazine prints a single-panel drawing with no speech balloons or dialogue boxes and asks readers to supply their own verbal jokes—is basically a meme generator. "It's seen more as a highbrow thing, crowdsourcing everybody's wit," said Abate. "But [the magazine supplies] the template image and then everybody puts in their own text or captions. They're making memes. If they only published the winner, folks would be disappointed because the fun is seeing all the clever, funny things that people come up with."
Memes both mirror and modify the comic genre. For instance, the online nature of memes can affect formatting. If there are multiple panels, those panels are usually arranged vertically rather than horizontally since memes are typically read by scrolling down one's phone—like the "American Chopper" meme:
Credit:
Jennifer Ouellette via imgflip
Per Abate, this has the added advantage of forcing the reader to pause briefly to consider the argument and counter-argument, emphasizing that it's an actual debate rather than two men simply yelling at one another. "If the panels were arranged horizontally and the guys were side by side in each other's face, installments of 'American Chopper' would come across very differently," she said.
A pad with infinite sheets
Scott McCloud is widely considered the leading theorist when it comes to the art of comics, and his hugely influential 2000 book,
Reinventing

data.title: Study mode
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）作为学习工具的优缺点及其实际效果

不同观点：
• 支持观点1：LLM作为学习伙伴非常有价值，可以提出“简单”的问题而不必担心尴尬。通过逐步引导学习材料，能够有效帮助自学者。这种工具提供了随时可用的学习助手，极大提升了自学的效率和体验。（jacobedawson, czhu12）
• 支持观点2：LLM可以帮助加速学习中的搜索和理解过程，特别是在解析公式和提供背景信息方面非常有用。通过LLM验证理解和解析符号，可以有效避免误解和时间浪费。（roadside_picnic）
• 反对观点1：有人担心LLM可能让学习变得过于简单或表面化，影响深度学习。过度依赖LLM可能会导致学习者缺乏自主思考能力，形成对AI的依赖。（poemxo）
• 反对观点2：LLM的错误和局限性可能对学习者产生误导，尽管它会承认错误，但学习者仍需保持警惕，验证信息来源。（wodenokoto, anupshinde）
• 中立观点1：LLM的学习模式本质上只是系统提示的变化，并没有真正的技术突破，对于已经知道如何请求帮助的用户来说，可能没有太大新意。（naet, adamkochanowicz）
• 中立观点2：有人提出，LLM的学习模式需要更好的用户界面来提升交互体验，比如将问题和答案更紧密地关联，以便于复习和跟踪学习进度。（x187463）

补充讨论：
• 实验需求：有观点建议通过随机对照实验研究LLM学习模式对学生的实际效果，评估其是否能带来有意义的提升，以及在允许学生犯错和指导复习之间的平衡。（jryio）
• 商业担忧：有评论担心平台提供商可能通过内置功能吞噬自定义工具的市场，影响相关创业公司的生存。（Workaccount2, varenc）
• 伦理问题：有评论质疑LLM开发过程中专家贡献的补偿问题，暗示可能存在不公平的商业行为。（megamix）

争议焦点：LLM是否真正提升了学习效果，或者只是让学习变得过于依赖技术而缺乏深度思考。同时，LLM的错误和局限性如何影响学习者的知识构建过程。

data.title: Raw milk outbreak from 2023 reported
data.author: sea-gold
data.article_summary: 2023年10月，加州圣地亚哥县卫生官员警告称，与生（未灭菌）牛奶相关的沙门氏菌疫情暴发，导致至少9人患病，其中3名儿童住院。随后病例增至12例，生牛奶及生奶油被召回。橙县也报告了7例病例。尽管疫情持续至2024年3月，最终报告显示共有5个州的171人感染，其中120人为儿童，22人住院，无死亡病例。然而，加州公共卫生部门（CDPH）未及时广泛发布疫情信息，引发批评。CDPH事后仅通过社交媒体和地方卫生部门的通报进行公共警示，未解释为何未发布详细新闻稿。疫情规模和影响引发了对公共卫生响应透明度的质疑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生牛奶（未经过巴氏杀菌的牛奶）是否值得尝试，其风险与口感评价如何。

不同观点：
• **Philipkglass的观点**：他曾经尝试过生牛奶，但并没有感受到与普通牛奶在味道上的显著差异，和他预期的“ culinary delight（美食享受）”不同。他提到，相比之下，新鲜橙汁比经过巴氏杀菌的橙汁味道明显更好，但生牛奶却没有类似的显著差异。他认为一些人愿意为生牛奶支付更多并承担风险，可能是因为心理预期或市场炒作。

• **Alifatisk的观点**：Alifatisk对生牛奶的尝试持怀疑态度，认为饮用生牛奶存在很高的风险，并质疑这种行为是否有任何实际的好处。他隐含的立场是，风险可能大于潜在的好处，暗示不值得为了未明确的益处去冒险。

补充讨论：
• **风险与收益的争议**：评论中Alifatisk提出了关于饮用生牛奶风险的担忧，这与Philipkglass对口感和体验的描述形成对比。Philipkglass虽然承认风险，但似乎更关注味道和体验，而Alifatisk则关注风险与收益的平衡问题。

• **市场和消费者心理**：Philipkglass提到人们愿意为生牛奶支付更多，暗示市场需求和消费者心理可能推动了生牛奶的流行，尽管实际口感差异可能并不大。这表明消费者在追求某种“稀缺性”或“冒险”体验，而非仅仅是味道。

• **安全与警告**：Philipkglass提到他购买生牛奶的商店附带了很多警告标志，说明市场上对生牛奶的销售有一定的监管和警示措施。这进一步强化了Alifatisk对风险的关注。

争议焦点：生牛奶是否值得尝试，主要围绕其风险性与潜在的口感或健康益处之间的权衡。

On October 20, 2023, health officials in the County of San Diego, California, put out
a press release
warning of a
Salmonella
outbreak linked to raw (unpasteurized) milk. Such an outbreak is not particularly surprising; the reason the vast majority of milk is pasteurized (heated briefly to kill germs) is because milk can easily pick up nasty pathogens in the farmyard that can cause severe illnesses, particularly in children. It's the reason public health officials have long and strongly warned against consuming raw milk.
At the time of the press release, officials in San Diego County had identified nine residents who had been sickened in the outbreak. Of those nine, three were children, and all three children had been hospitalized.
On October 25, the county put out
a second press release
, reporting that the local case count had risen to 12, and the suspected culprit—
raw milk and raw cream from Raw Farm LLC
—had been recalled. The same day, Orange County's health department put out its own
press release
, reporting seven cases among its residents, including one in a 1-year-old infant.
Both counties noted that the California Department of Public Health (CDPH), which had posted the recall notice, was working on the outbreak, too. But it doesn't appear that CDPH ever followed up with its own press release about the outbreak. The CDPH did write social media posts related to the outbreak:
One on October 26, 2023,
announced the recall;
a second on November 30, 2023,
noted "a recent outbreak" of
Salmonella
cases from raw milk
but linked to general information about the risks of raw milk; and
a third on December 7, 2023,
linked to general information again with no mention of the outbreak.
But that seems to be the extent of the information at the time. For anyone paying attention, it might have seemed like the end of the story. But according to the final outbreak investigation report—
produced by CDPH and local health officials
—the outbreak actually ran from September 2023 to March 2024, spanned five states, and sickened at least 171 people. That report was released last week, on July 24, 2025.
Shocking outbreak
The report was published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, a journal run by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The report describes the outbreak as "one of the largest foodborne outbreaks linked to raw milk in recent US history." It also said that the state and local health department had issued "extensive public messaging regarding this outbreak."
According to the final data, of the 171 people, 120 (70 percent) were children and teens, including 67 (39 percent) who were under the age of 5. At least 22 people were hospitalized, nearly all of them (82 percent) were children and teens. Fortunately, there were no deaths.
"I was just candidly shocked that there was an outbreak of 170 plus people because it had not been reported—at all," Bill Marler, a personal injury lawyer specializing in food poisoning outbreaks, told Ars Technica in an interview. With the large number of cases, the high percentage of kids, and cases in multiple states, "it's shocking that they never publicized it," he said. "I mean, what's the point?"
Ars Technica reached out to CDPH seeking answers about why there wasn't more messaging and information about the outbreak during and soon after the investigation. At the time this story was published, several business days had passed and the department had told Ars in a follow-up email that it was still working on a response. Shortly after publication, CDPH provided a written statement, but it did not answer any specific questions, including why CDPH did not release its own press release about the state-wide outbreak or make case counts public during the investigation.
"CDPH takes its charge to protect public health seriously and works closely with all partners when a foodborne illness outbreak is identified," the statement reads. It then referenced only the social media posts and the press releases from San Diego County and Orange County mentioned previously in this story as examples of its public messaging.
“This is pissing me off”
Marler, who represents around two dozen of the 171 people sickened in the outbreak, was one of the first people to get the full picture of the outbreak from California officials. In July of 2024, he obtained an interim report of the investigation from state health officials. At that point, they had
documented at least 165 of the cases
. And in December 2024, he got access to
a preliminary report of the full investigation dated October 15, 2024
, which identified the final 171 cases and appears to contain much of the data published in the MMWR, which has
had its publication rate slowed amid the second Trump administration
.
Getting that information from California officials was not easy, Marler told Ar

data.title: Evidence for hepatitis C virus involvement in bipolar disorder and schizophrenia
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了病毒感染与精神疾病（如精神分裂症（SCZ）和双相情感障碍（BPD））之间的关联，特别是通过研究脉络丛（CP）中的病毒RNA。研究使用来自Stanley Medical Research Institute的脑组织样本，对84例SCZ、73例BPD、23例重度抑郁症（MDD）和76例对照组进行了RNA测序。结果发现，SCZ和BPD患者的CP中更可能含有病毒序列，尤其是丙型肝炎病毒（HCV）。进一步分析显示，SCZ和BPD人群中的慢性HCV患病率显著高于MDD和对照组。尽管HCV未在 hippocampus 中发现，但其在CP中的存在与宿主转录变化相关，可能涉及先天免疫反应。这表明HCV感染可能与精神疾病的病理有关，而不仅是由静脉注射等行为引起。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HCV（丙型肝炎病毒）与精神疾病（如精神分裂症和双相情感障碍）之间的关联及其因果关系

不同观点：
• [_alternator_] 认为该研究揭示了HCV与精神疾病（如精神分裂症和双相情感障碍）之间的关联是真实的，但质疑HCV是否是这些疾病的因果因素。虽然HCV在脑部（脉络丛）中出现并可能引发局部免疫反应，但要得出“HCV导致精神分裂症和双相情感障碍”的结论仍存在较大跳跃。

• [hungmung] 提到治疗HCV的新药物可能引发躁狂发作，但目前尚不确定这种现象的具体原因。可能是药物本身导致，也可能是生活突然改变引发的反应，或者是由于身体不再需要对抗慢性感染而导致能量过剩，使人无法适应。

补充讨论：
• [_alternator_] 强调了研究中的机制性证据有限，目前仅知道HCV会出现在脑部并引发免疫反应，但这不足以证明HCV是精神疾病的原因。
• [hungmung] 提出了治疗HCV的药物可能带来的精神健康副作用，这表明在治疗HCV时需要考虑其对精神健康的潜在影响。

争议焦点：HCV是否是精神分裂症和双相情感障碍的因果因素，以及治疗HCV的药物对精神健康的影响机制。这两个问题目前都缺乏足够的证据支持明确的结论。

44737247.article_content:
Association of viral RNAs in the choroid plexus with bipolar disorder and schizophrenia and evidence for the hepatitis C virus involvement in neuropathology
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Bipolar disorder
Schizophrenia
Abstract
Many epidemiological studies have shown an association between infectious agents, particularly viruses, and psychiatric disorders including schizophrenia. However, evidence of a viral infection in the brain that associates with schizophrenia (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BPD), and major depression (MDD) has not been found. A potential reason for this discrepancy may be that viruses are more likely to infect the neuroepithelium than neural tissue. To test this hypothesis, we used viral sequence enrichment technology and performed RNA sequencing in postmortem choroid plexus (CP) isolated from 84 SCZ, 73 BPD, 23 MDD cases and 76 unaffected controls (CNT) from the Stanley Medical Research Institute brain collection. This approach enabled us to identify the presence of 13 viral species in the CP of 46 subjects. We discovered that CP samples collected from subjects with SCZ and BPD are more likely to contain viral sequences. In terms of individual viruses, the Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) was the only viral species that reached the threshold of statistical significance for an association with SCZ and BPD. Therefore, we focused on HCV to characterize the association between psychiatric disorders and viruses. Analysis of the TriNetX electronic health record database with data on 285 million patients revealed that the prevalence of chronic HCV was 3.6 and 3.9 percent in the SCZ and BPD populations respectively. The prevalence of chronic HCV in these populations was almost double that observed for MDD (1.8%) and approximately 7-fold higher than the control population (0.5%). These findings confirm previous studies that report higher HCV prevalence in SCZ and BPD and suggest that HCV infection may be associated with disease pathology rather than behaviors such as intravenous drug injection, since these behaviors are present in all three disorders. We analyzed hippocampus RNA sequencing data from the subjects identified to be HCV positive via sequence capture. We found that although the virus was absent in this tissue, HCV RNA in the CP was associated with consistent host transcriptional changes in the hippocampus that were potentially related to the innate immune response. Our results are consistent with previous studies and provide clues regarding the contribution of viruses to the pathology of psychiatric disorders.

data.title: Show HN: Print the daily weather forecast on a thermal receipt printer
data.author: chr15m
data.article_summary: 该项目展示了如何使用ESC/POS协议在热敏收据打印机上打印每日天气预报。主要功能包括：通过脚本获取天气数据并打印，支持自定义GPS坐标和时区。项目依赖Python 3、Pillow库和ImageMagick工具。使用时需安装依赖，并通过命令行或环境变量输入坐标和时区信息。若未提供，默认使用伦敦的坐标。可以通过设置Cron任务实现每日自动打印。项目文件包括脚本、图标和使用说明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：热敏纸的安全性

不同观点：
• 观点一：一些热敏纸不安全，特别是含有双酚A（BPA）或双酚S（BPS）的纸张。Orphea引用了明尼苏达州政府的文章，指出这些化学物质可能对健康有危害。
   
• 观点二：并非所有热敏纸都不安全。有观点可能认为，只有特定含有BPA或BPS的纸张才存在健康风险，而市场上也有不含这些化学物质的替代品。

补充讨论：
• 热敏纸的化学成分：讨论中提到了BPA和BPS，这些化学物质常用于热敏纸的制造，以帮助显色，但它们被认为可能对人体健康有影响。
   
• 政府监管：有人可能会提到政府或相关机构对热敏纸中这些化学物质的监管和限制，例如明尼苏达州的文章，说明这个问题已经引起了一定程度的关注。

• 争议焦点：热敏纸中的化学物质是否对人体有害，以及是否应该全面禁止或替换这些化学物质。同时，消费者如何辨别安全的热敏纸也是一个讨论点。

• 健康风险意识：Orphea的评论提醒读者关注热敏纸的潜在风险，表明消费者需要提高警惕并获取相关信息以保护自身健康。

Thermal Receipt Weather Printer
Prints a daily weather forecast on an ESC/POS thermal printer, such as the "Bisofice Mini BT thermal receipt printer".
Dependencies
|
Setup
|
Usage
|
Cron
Dependencies
Python 3
Pillow
: The Python imaging library.
ImageMagick
: For converting SVG icons to a printable format.
Setup
Install dependencies:
On Debian/Ubuntu:
sudo apt-get update
&&
sudo apt-get install imagemagick python3-pil
On other systems, install
ImageMagick
via your package manager and
Pillow
via pip:
pip install Pillow
Get the weather icons:
Run the script with the
--download-icons
flag to download only the necessary icon files:
./printweather.py --download-icons
Or
git clone https://github.com/erikflowers/weather-icons
Or
download the zip
.
Usage
Run the script, redirecting the output to your printer device (e.g.,
/dev/usb/lp0
or
/dev/ttyUSB0
).
The script can be run from any directory by providing its full path:
/path/to/print-weather/printweather.py
>
/dev/usb/lp0
Supplying Coordinates
You can provide GPS coordinates and timezone via command-line arguments or environment variables. If none are provided, the script defaults to London, UK.
The order of command-line arguments is:
LATITUDE LONGITUDE TIMEZONE
As command-line arguments:
#
Example for London
./printweather.py 51.5072 -0.1276
"
Europe/London
"
>
/dev/usb/lp0
As environment variables:
LATITUDE=51.5072 LONGITUDE=-0.1276 TIMEZONE=
"
Europe/London
"
./printweather.py
>
/dev/usb/lp0
Scheduling with Cron
To run the script automatically at 5am every day in the system's timezone, edit the crontab with
crontab -e
and add the following line.
Use environment variables to configure the location and timezone.
0 5 * * * LATITUDE=51.5072 LONGITUDE=-0.1276 TIMEZONE="Europe/London" /path/to/print-weather/printweather.py > /dev/usb/lp0
Note: Replace
/path/to/print-weather/
with the actual path to the project directory.

data.title: No traffic deaths in Helsinki for a year
data.author: DaveZale
data.article_summary: 赫尔辛基实现了一个重要里程碑，整整一年未发生交通死亡事故。这一成就归功于长期规划、基础设施改造、降低限速以及加强交通执法。目前，超过一半的街道限速为30公里/小时，学校周边限速也已调低。街道设计优化、步行和骑行设施的扩展进一步提升了安全性。交通事故数量从1980年代的每年近1000起减少到277起。电动滑板车管理仍是挑战，但通过调整停车规则和限速等措施已有所改善。赫尔辛基的交通安全战略持续至2026年，目标是保护行人、儿童和骑行者，并以欧盟2050年消除交通死亡为长远目标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：赫尔辛基市街道限速调整及其影响

不同观点：
• **反对限速降低的观点**：SilverElfin认为，赫尔辛基将大部分街道的限速从50 km/h降低到30 km/h，影响了生活质量，因为这会使出行更加痛苦，浪费人们的时间。他们指出，虽然低限速可能减少交通事故死亡，但并不能让出行变得高效或令人满意。他们主张通过发展汽车安全技术来实现减少伤害，而不是单纯依靠降低限速。

• **对安全措施的隐私担忧**：SilverElfin进一步指出，城市官员与警方合作的增加，以及更多自动化测速执法手段的使用，实际上是一种以“安全”为借口的广泛监控。这引发了对隐私和监控过度扩张的担忧。

补充讨论：
• **交通安全的不同策略**：SilverElfin认为，城市的目标应该是实现快速出行和轻松驾驶，同时减少伤害，而不是仅仅通过降低限速来追求零交通事故死亡。这涉及到对交通管理策略的广泛讨论，包括技术进步在交通安全中的角色。

• **执法手段的争议**：自动化测速执法手段的增加被视为对个人隐私的潜在威胁，这表明在实施安全措施的同时，如何平衡公共安全与个人权利成为讨论的焦点。

争议焦点：限速降低对交通效率和生活质量的影响，以及通过自动化执法手段加强安全监管是否构成对隐私的侵犯。

Helsinki has completed
an entire year without a single traffic-related fatality, according to city and police officials. The last recorded death occurred in early July 2024 in the Kontula district.
Authorities described the milestone as exceptional and credited long-term planning, targeted infrastructure changes, and lower speed limits.
“A lot of factors contributed to this, but speed limits are one of the most important,” said
Roni Utriainen
, traffic engineer with the city’s Urban Environment Division.
More than half of Helsinki’s streets now have speed limits of 30 km/h. Fifty years ago, the majority were limited to 50 km/h. In a move to further reduce risk, the city lowered limits around schools to 30 km/h earlier this year. The new restrictions take effect at the start of the school term.
Alongside speed control, design has played a key role. Street layouts, intersections, and pedestrian crossings have been redesigned to prioritise safety. Cycling and walking infrastructure has been expanded in recent years, helping to separate vulnerable road users from motor traffic.
Utriainen also highlighted improvements in traffic enforcement. Cooperation between city officials and police has increased, with more automated speed enforcement and targeted patrols.
“Public transport in Helsinki is excellent, which reduces car use, and with it, the number of serious accidents,” he said.
Vehicle safety standards have also advanced, contributing to improved outcomes in the event of collisions.
The improvement is not limited to fatalities. In the past 12 months, Helsinki recorded 277 accidents resulting in injury. This compares to nearly 1,000 such incidents annually during the late 1980s, when the city often saw up to 30 deaths per year.
Helsinki’s current traffic safety strategy runs from 2022 to 2026 and includes special measures to protect pedestrians, children, and cyclists. Planning has been supported by better data collection, including digital monitoring of traffic flows and incident reporting.
Utriainen said the city’s efforts are cumulative and span decades. “The direction has been positive for years,” he said. Helsinki also recorded zero pedestrian fatalities in 2019.
Electric scooters remain a challenge, though the city has responded by adjusting parking rules, restricting speed in certain areas, and improving signage.
“They became popular around five years ago, somewhat unexpectedly. But since then, many solutions have been put in place,” Utriainen said.
He credited all road users, motorists, cyclists, and pedestrians, for contributing to the result through their behaviour and awareness.
The European Union aims to eliminate all traffic fatalities by 2050, an initiative known as Vision Zero. Utriainen said the target serves as a practical framework for decision-making.
“For us, it’s more about how the goal guides our everyday actions. We aim to assess all our decisions based on their long-term impact,” he said.

• **对安全措施的隐私担忧**：SilverElfin进一步指出，城市官员与警方合作的增加，以及更多自动化测速执法手段的使用，实际上是一种以“安全”为借口的广泛监控。这引发了对隐私和监控过度扩张的担忧。

补充讨论：
• **交通安全的不同策略**：SilverElfin认为，城市的目标应该是实现快速出行和轻松驾驶，同时减少伤害，而不是仅仅通过降低限速来追求零交通事故死亡。这涉及到对交通管理策略的广泛讨论，包括技术进步在交通安全中的角色。

• **执法手段的争议**：自动化测速执法手段的增加被视为对个人隐私的潜在威胁，这表明在实施安全措施的同时，如何平衡公共安全与个人权利成为讨论的焦点。

争议焦点：限速降低对交通效率和生活质量的影响，以及通过自动化执法手段加强安全监管是否构成对隐私的侵犯。

data.title: Ferrari were SO impressed by the Xiaomi SU7, they bought one
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: 文章报道称，小米推出的SU7 Ultra电动车以其强劲的性能和加速表现引起了汽车行业的广泛关注，甚至吸引了超级跑车品牌法拉利的兴趣。据中国博主透露，法拉利购买了一辆SU7 Ultra，用于对其 upcoming电动车型平台的研发和 benchmarking（对标分析）。图片显示，这辆SU7 Ultra驶出了法拉利位于意大利马拉内罗的工厂。此外，还有消息称法拉利代表去年访问了小米总部，讨论联合开发下一代高性能电动机。SU7 Ultra拥有1,548马力，0-60英里加速不到2秒，最高时速超过200英里，售价却低于特斯拉Model S Plaid和保时捷Taycan Turbo GT，发布后迅速售罄。这一事件可能标志着汽车创新的领先地位正从西方转向东方。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对小米产品及市场表现的评价

不同观点：
• [Guid_NewGuid] 对小米公司的广泛产品线表示惊讶，提到在巴拿马机场看到小米店铺出售从手机到家用电器等多种产品，并指出小米的股票大幅上涨。他对小米的印象从"廉价手机"转变为一个拥有多样产品的公司。

• [Sohcahtoa82] 对小米的SU7电动车表示兴奋，认为它展示了竞争者在电动车性能上的潜力。他提到对高价低性能的电动车感到失望，而小米SU7的出现表明他所期望的平价高性能电动车是有可能实现的。

• [thedrbrian] 认为汽车制造商之间互相购买和研究彼此的汽车是很常见的行为，并指出中国公司经常借鉴其他汽车的设计风格，暗示小米可能也不例外。

• [constantcrying] 认为小米的SU7除了价格低廉外，没有其他令人印象深刻的地方。如果小米能够在保持价格低廉的同时维持可持续的利润率，那么欧美汽车行业将面临严重威胁。他质疑高价高性能汽车制造商的生存空间。

补充讨论：
• [PaulHoule] 提供了一个链接，可能包含对相关话题的进一步讨论或信息，但没有详细阐述自己的观点。

争议焦点：
• 小米的SU7电动车是否真的具备市场竞争力，尤其是在性能和价格上的优势是否能持续。
• 小米是否依赖于借鉴其他厂商的设计，这对它的创新能力有何影响。
• 欧美汽车制造商在面对像小米这样的竞争对手时，是否能够维持其高价高性能的市场定位。

Report: Ferrari were SO impressed by the Xiaomi SU7, they bought one
Jo Borrás
| Jul 29 2025 - 6:47 pm PT
18 Comments
With its
tire-blistering acceleration
and
record-setting performance
, the Xiaomi SU7 Ultra has been getting attention throughout the auto industry, impressing everyone who’s seen it. That “everyone” now seems to include the OG supercar brand, itself.
CarNewsChina
posted pictures from a Weibo user that reportedly show a Xiaomi SU7 Ultra exiting the storied Ferrari factory in Maranello, Italy. According to a Chinese blogger going by 西米露在博洛尼亚 (which seems to translate to “Sago Dessert in Bologna”), the prancing horse brand is actively benchmarking the Chinese hypercar for its own upcoming EV.
The SU7 Ultra was definitely coming from inside Ferrari’s facility. After verification, we learned this specific vehicle was officially purchased by Ferrari for testing, and the development of their next-generation electric platform.
西米露在博洛尼亚
Yet another Chinese auto blogger,
苏黎世贝勒爷
, claims that Ferrari representatives visited Xiaomi headquarters last year,
allegedly to discuss the joint development of next-generation high-performance EV motors
.
The Xiaomi SU7 Ultra made its debut last year
, promising 1,548 hp, sub 2.0-second 0-60 mph times, and a top speed well over 200 mph – all at a price lower than a Tesla Model S Plaid or
Porsche Taycan Turbo GT
. The car sold out almost immediately after it was unveiled, racking up some 50,000 orders almost overnight.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The new electric benchmark
Xiaomi SU7 Ultra at Fiorano; via Weibo user Piniluoshan.
In the automotive world, “
benchmarking
” is a process in which car companies systematically tear down each others’ competitive products to compare everything from sound insulation, vehicle ride and handling, component materials, and even manufacturing methods against their own or against other industry leaders. The goal is to evaluate performance, cost, quality, and other key metrics, effectively figuring out “where they stand” in the market.
If Ferrari really
did
buy an SU7 to benchmark it against their own upcoming electric supercar, it’s more than just a curiosity –
it could mean that the highest tiers of automotive innovation have shifted from West to East
. Maybe forever.

data.title: Show HN: I built an AI that turns any book into a text adventure game
data.author: rcrKnight
data.article_summary: KathaaVerse是一个互动文本 fiction 平台，用户可以将书籍转化为互动冒险体验。平台提供多种类型的故事，包括奇幻与魔法、科幻、当代小说以及反乌托邦与惊悚类别。经典作品如《爱丽丝梦游仙境》、《哈利波特与魔法石》、《魔戒》、《沙丘》和《1984》等都被收录其中，用户可以根据自己喜好选择并引导情节发展。每个故事都提供“开始”选项，让用户沉浸于不同的虚构世界中，体验个性化的冒险旅程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成叙事文本的质量、用户与AI在叙事中的互动、技术实现的挑战与建议、以及AI生成内容的价值问题。

不同观点：
• **AI在生成逻辑叙事方面的不足**：[why_at] 提到AI在生成像《霍比特人》这样的故事时，出现了重复角色和缺乏逻辑性的问题，表明AI在保持连贯叙事方面的不足。

• **用户主导叙事与AI被动回应的矛盾**：[kmnc] 认为AI往往只是被动回应，用户主导了叙事方向，导致故事变得可预测、浅薄且重复，质疑这种模式下的创意性。

• **AI生成内容的情感缺失**：[jaysonelliot] 指出AI生成的内容缺乏人类作者的情感和深度，认为即使在不知道内容由AI生成的情况下，仍能感受到内容的空虚和不满足，尤其是与人类创作的文本冒险游戏相比。

• **技术优化建议**：[spdustin] 提供了关于如何通过结构化选择和引导AI生成更具互动性和连贯性的故事的技术建议，强调了通过指令和随机性（RNG）的结合来改善叙事体验。

• **对AI生成故事的趣味性认可**：[fifticon] 和 [oooyay] 等用户对AI生成故事的趣味性和潜力表示认可，尽管他们遇到了技术问题，如速率限制，但仍对整体体验持积极态度。

• **AI生成内容的价值质疑**：[HellDunkel] 从艺术交流的角度质疑AI生成内容的价值，认为AI生成内容缺乏与人类沟通的深度和意义。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现中的问题**：[bArray]、[mNovak] 和 [superkacper4] 提到了在实际使用中遇到的技术问题，如速率限制错误、故事显示不全、以及黑暗模式崩溃等。

• **多选择题模式的建议**：[sjw987] 提出了一种基于现有书籍内容生成多选择题的替代方案，认为这样可以避免AI生成故事时偏离原著，同时也能用于学习和研究。

• **经典文学作品的潜在应用**：[abrookewood] 和 [BaudouinVH] 讨论了AI生成内容在经典文学作品中的潜在应用，如《卡夫卡的审判》或《城堡》，提出了对预计算路径和存储结果的建议以优化体验。

争议焦点：
• **AI生成内容的创意性与被动性之间的平衡**：用户对于AI在叙事中应扮演的角色存在分歧，一部分用户希望AI能更主动引导故事，另一部分用户则认为AI只是被动响应，缺乏创意性。
• **AI生成内容的价值和意义**：部分用户质疑AI生成内容是否具有与人类创作内容相同的艺术和交流价值，这一问题在讨论中引发了对AI生成内容未来发展的深思。

data.article_summary: Enovix公司开发了一种采用硅负极的新型电池AI-1，其能量密度比当前主流智能手机电池高出约20%。这一突破有望大幅提升智能手机的电池续航能力。硅材料的应用使得电池可以在相同体积下储存更多能量，为消费电子产品带来显著的性能提升。这一技术进步对于智能手机及其他便携设备具有重要意义。文章由IEEE Spectrum的撰稿编辑Charles Q. Choi撰写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple Vision Pro电池技术的未来发展及其市场潜力

不同观点：
• kridsdale3认为，通过改进电池技术，未来的Apple Vision Pro电池包可以缩小至现有尺寸的1/3（可能不需要使用腰包），或者在现有功耗水平下续航时间延长3倍。他还提到，传闻下一代Vision Pro将采用M4级别的芯片，进一步降低功耗。因此，kridsdale3预测，经过1到2次迭代，Apple可能会推出一款更具大众市场吸引力的产品。

• malchow则关注电池技术的具体材料改进，指出新电池技术使用100%活性硅材料作为阳极，而非仅在石墨中掺杂5%的硅。他还分享了一个展示生产过程的预览视频链接，对技术的先进性表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• kridsdale3的观点更侧重于Apple Vision Pro整体产品的市场潜力和用户体验的改进，特别是重量、热量和续航时间等方面。
• malchow的观点则聚焦于电池技术本身的创新，特别是材料科学方面的突破，如100%活性硅材料在阳极中的应用。
• 争议的焦点可能在于技术的实际应用和市场化时间。kridsdale3更乐观地预计短期内可以看到改进产品，而malchow则关注技术的实际生产和实现。
• malchow提供的视频链接为讨论增添了技术细节和可视化信息，使讨论更加具体和生动。

总结来看，评论主要围绕Apple Vision Pro电池技术的未来发展，讨论了电池体积和续航时间的改进潜力，以及新材料和生产工艺的创新。同时，也对技术实现和市场化的前景存在一定乐观但有区别的预期。

data.title: YouTube will identify and restrict minors' accounts with AI
data.author: conor-
data.article_summary: YouTube将从下个月开始使用人工智能技术通过账户年龄和活动来识别美国未成年用户，并自动对其账户实施限制，如屏蔽年龄限制内容、减少个性化广告、推送休息提醒以及限制敏感话题的视频推荐。此外，上传视频或留言时会自动出现隐私提醒。若系统判断错误，用户可通过上传政府ID、自拍或输入信用卡验证年龄。此举是YouTube加强未成年人网络安全的一部分，并将在其他国家逐步推广。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在HTTP协议中引入内容分级系统的可行性与影响

不同观点：
• [支持观点 - atonse]  
   支持在HTTP协议中引入内容分级系统，认为可以通过HTTP头部字段（如X-Minimum-Recommended-Age或X-Contains-Content-Themes）标示页面内容，例如是否包含暴力、裸体等。这种方法可以保护隐私，并允许父母通过浏览器设置控制孩子可以访问的内容。同时，提到YouTube已经要求创作者指定观众群体，认为这种方式可以更精细地控制内容访问，而不必完全屏蔽平台。

• [反对观点 - RamblingCTO]  
   认为这种内容分级系统有些“反乌托邦”色彩，尤其在YouTube已经因其内容审核问题备受批评的情况下。同时，RamblingCTO对YouTube的垄断地位表示不满，认为这种系统可能反而巩固YouTube的统治地位，而不是带来真正的改变。他表达了对去中心化平台（如Peertube）的期望，但认为这些替代平台目前还不够好。

补充讨论：
• [争议焦点]  
   争议的焦点在于内容分级系统的潜在效果。支持者认为它有助于更精细地控制内容访问，保护隐私，同时方便家长管理孩子浏览的内容。而反对者则担心这种系统可能被大平台利用，进一步巩固其垄断地位，并且对内容审核问题带来新的挑战。

• [技术实现的简单性与现实复杂性]  
   atonse认为技术上只需添加几个HTTP头部字段，实现简单，且已有类似做法（如YouTube的观众指定功能）。但RamblingCTO则隐含指出，内容分级涉及的不只是技术问题，还有更广泛的社会和政治影响，尤其是平台垄断和内容审核方面。

• [对替代平台的期望]  
   RamblingCTO提到去中心化平台（如Peertube），显示出对当前大平台的不满，并希望有更好的替代品。然而，他也承认这些替代平台目前还不够成熟。这引出了一个额外讨论点：如何在大平台垄断的现状下寻找和支持替代方案。

YouTube will identify and restrict minors’ accounts with AI
Next month, YouTube will use an account’s age and activity to determine if it belongs to someone under 18.
Next month, YouTube will use an account’s age and activity to determine if it belongs to someone under 18.
by
Emma Roth
Close
Emma Roth
News Writer

Follow

Emma Roth
Jul 29, 2025, 5:48 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: Alex Castro / The Verge
Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
YouTube will soon begin using AI-powered age estimation technology to figure out which users are under the age of 18.
Starting August 13th
, YouTube will detect underage users in the US based on their activity and the age of their account, allowing the platform to automatically apply restrictions.
These accounts will get the same protections YouTube already offers to users who identify themselves as under 18, including a block on age-restricted videos, non-personalized ads,
“take a break” notifications
, and a
limit on repeated video recommendations
about sensitive topics, such as body image. The platform will also automatically turn on reminders about privacy when users upload a video or leave a comment.
Google first announced plans to use
machine learning to power age estimation
earlier this year, which aligns with a global crackdown on child safety online. Last week, the
UK’s online age verification rules
went into effect, requiring users to verify their ages on sites with porn or content deemed “harmful.” Several states have passed laws
blocking minors from accessing porn sites
, while efforts to age-gate social media platforms have largely
fallen flat
. The European Union is also testing
an age verification prototype
that it will eventually link with digital IDs.
Related
The UK is slogging through an online age-gate apocalypse
Reddit and Discord’s UK age verification can be defeated by Death Stranding’s photo mode
YouTube will notify users if it determines they are under 18, but if the platform gets it wrong, users can verify their age by uploading a government ID, taking a selfie, or entering a credit card. The platform notes that some creators may “experience a shift in their audience categorized as teens,” potentially resulting in less ad revenue, since minors aren’t shown personalized ads.
“Over the next few weeks, we’ll begin to roll out machine learning to a small set of users in the US to estimate their age, so that teens are treated as teens and adults as adults,” James Beser, YouTube’s director of product management,
writes in a post explaining the change
. Beser adds that YouTube will “closely monitor” the update before rolling it out to other countries.

data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [starkparker的观点] 认为该视频非常恐怖，令人不适。他怀疑这个视频是一个实际产品的宣传，而不是恐怖电影的病毒式营销。他对于这是真实产品宣传的可能性感到震惊。

data.title: My 2.5 year old laptop can write Space Invaders in JavaScript now (GLM-4.5 Air)
data.author: simonw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Simon Willison在2025年7月29日发布的一篇博客，讲述了在一台2.5年历史的笔记本电脑上使用GLM-4.5 Air模型和MLX库编写JavaScript版本的《太空入侵者》游戏。GLM-4.5模型由中国的Z.ai发布，具备较高的编码能力。尽管模型体积庞大（1060亿参数，205.78GB），但经过量化压缩，可以在64GB内存的MacBook Pro M2上运行。作者展示了如何配置和运行该模型，并成功生成了可运行的游戏代码。作者还提到，与两年前相比，本地运行的高质量编码模型性能显著提升，显示了2025年模型在个人设备上的快速发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在本地硬件上运行的能力及其应用价值

不同观点：
• [NitpickLawyer] 认为，开源模型的质量和发布速度已经超越了他的预期。他从历史角度对比了GPT-J等早期模型与当前的GLM 4.5 Air、Mistral 3.2 Small等模型，指出这些新模型的能力显著提升，且在本地运行成为可能，这是两年前无法想象的。
• [bob1029] 强调现有硬件的能力被低估，批评了“ bitter lesson ”和“ efficient compute frontier ”等观点，认为这些理论可能误导了研究方向。他指出当前模型的效率低下，但通过降低权重精度仍能实现惊人的结果。
• [righthand] 对LLM的实际应用价值提出质疑，认为许多人使用LLM来增强演示文稿而非实现实际功能。他举例说明同事使用LLM生成复杂但无实际效用的解决方案。
• [alankarmisra] 认可LLM在本地运行的里程碑意义，但质疑其在特定领域（如Space Invaders）的实际价值，认为从GitHub等平台获取现有实现可能更有效。
• [lxgr] 提出一个科幻式的问题，探讨今日消费级硬件是否能运行未来的超级智能或代理，并引导讨论这种情景的可能性。
• [captainregex] 质疑本地AI的最大用户群体及其应用场景，认为当前使用本地AI更多是因为技术可行性而非实际需求。

补充讨论：
• [simonw] 和 [ddtaylor] 分享了实际测试结果，展示了新模型在本地运行的情况，并提供了相关链接和截图。

44723316.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
My 2.5 year old laptop can write Space Invaders in JavaScript now, using GLM-4.5 Air and MLX
29th July 2025
I wrote about the new
GLM-4.5
model family yesterday—new open weight (MIT licensed) models from
Z.ai
in China which their benchmarks claim score highly in coding even against models such as Claude Sonnet 4.
The models are pretty big—the smaller GLM-4.5 Air model is still 106 billion total parameters, which
is 205.78GB
on Hugging Face.
Ivan Fioravanti
built
this
44GB 3bit quantized version for MLX
, specifically sized so people with 64GB machines could have a chance of running it. I tried it out... and it works
extremely well
.
I fed it the following prompt:
Write an HTML and JavaScript page implementing space invaders
And it churned away for a while and produced
the following
:
Clearly this isn’t a particularly novel example, but I still think it’s noteworthy that a model running on my 2.5 year old laptop (a 64GB MacBook Pro M2) is able to produce code like this—especially code that worked first time with no further edits needed.
How I ran the model
I had to run it using the current
main
branch of the
mlx-lm
library (to ensure I had
this commit
adding
glm4_moe
support). I ran that using
uv
like this:
uv run \
--with
'
https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/archive/489e63376b963ac02b3b7223f778dbecc164716b.zip
'
\
python
Then in that Python interpreter I used the standard recipe for running MLX models:
from
mlx_lm
import
load
,
generate
model
,
tokenizer
=
load
(
"mlx-community/GLM-4.5-Air-3bit"
)
That downloaded 44GB of model weights to my
~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--mlx-community--GLM-4.5-Air-3bit
folder.
Then:
prompt
=
"Write an HTML and JavaScript page implementing space invaders"
messages
=
[{
"role"
:
"user"
,
"content"
:
prompt
}]
prompt
=
tokenizer
.
apply_chat_template
(
messages
,
add_generation_prompt
=
True
)
response
=
generate
(
model
,
tokenizer
,
prompt
=
prompt
,
verbose
=
True
,
max_tokens
=
8192
)
The response started like this:
<think>
The user wants me to create a Space Invaders game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. I need to create a complete, functional game with the following features:
Player spaceship that can move left/right and shoot
Enemy invaders that move in formation and shoot back
Score tracking
Lives/health system
Game over conditions [...]
Followed by the HTML and this debugging output:
Prompt: 14 tokens, 14.095 tokens-per-sec
Generation: 4193 tokens, 25.564 tokens-per-sec
Peak memory: 47.687 GB
You can see
the full transcript here
, or view
the source on GitHub
, or
try it out in your browser
.
A pelican for good measure
I ran
my pelican benchmark
against the full sized models
yesterday
, but I couldn’t resist trying it against this smaller 3bit model. Here’s what I got for
"Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle"
:
Here’s the
transcript for that
.
In both cases the model used around 48GB of RAM at peak, leaving me with just 16GB for everything else—I had to quit quite a few apps in order to get the model to run but the speed was pretty good once it got going.
Local coding models are really good now
It’s interesting how almost every model released in 2025 has specifically targeting coding. That focus has clearly been paying off: these coding models are getting
really good
now.
Two years ago when I
first tried LLaMA
I never
dreamed
that the same laptop I was using then would one day be able to run models with capabilities as strong as what I’m seeing from GLM 4.5 Air—and Mistral 3.2 Small, and Gemma 3, and Qwen 3, and a host of other high quality models that have emerged over the past six months.

44736238.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Something that has become undeniable this month is that the best available open weight models now come from the Chinese AI labs.
I continue to have a lot of love for Mistral, Gemma and Llama but my feeling is that Qwen, Moonshot and Z.ai have positively
smoked them
over the course of July.
Here's what came out this month, with links to my notes on each one:
Moonshot
Kimi-K2-Instruct
- 11th July, 1 trillion parameters
Qwen
Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507
- 21st July, 235 billion
Qwen
Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct
- 22nd July, 480 billion
Qwen
Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507
- 25th July, 235 billion
Z.ai
GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.5 Air
- 28th July, 355 and 106 billion
Qwen
Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507
- 29th July, 30 billion
Qwen
Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507
- 30th July, 30 billion
Notably absent from this list is DeepSeek, but that's only because their last model release was
DeepSeek-R1-0528
back in April.
The only janky license among them is Kimi K2, which uses a non-OSI-compliant modified MIT. Qwen's models are all Apache 2 and Z.ai's are MIT.
The larger Chinese models all offer their own APIs and are increasingly available from other providers.  I've been able to run versions of the Qwen 30B and GLM-4.5 Air 106B models on my own laptop.
I can't help but wonder if part of the reason for the delay in release of OpenAI's open weights model comes from a desire to be notably better than this truly impressive lineup of Chinese models.

In 2023, after the State of JS and State of CSS surveys had already been going on for a few years, we realized something was missing: what about the technology that brings it all together?
After all, HTML now goes beyond tags and attributes, encompassing APIs for dynamic updates, rich embeds, performance hints, templating & components, and more.
The first State of HTML, led by web superstar
Lea Verou
broke all previous records for a new survey with 21,000 respondents, and introduced new UI paradigms that improved all future surveys.
This year, with Lea back at the helm, we added ✨35 new features✨, and introduced two new sections:
Graphics & Multimedia
and
Performance
.
What's more, survey results will be taken in consideration by browser vendors when deciding on their roadmaps, so participating can help shape the future of the web!
Are you ready? Get, set, go!
Loading...
FAQ
How long will answering the survey take?
Depending on how many questions you answer (all questions can be skipped), filling out the survey should take around 10-15 minutes.
Who should take this survey?
This is an open survey for anybody who makes websites or web apps, whether regularly or occasionally, as part of their job, as a student, or just for fun!
What are the survey's goals?
The survey's goals are to measure awareness of new HTML features and browser APIs, and help developers keep track of how their usage is evolving.
How will this data be used?
All data collected will be released openly for any developer or company to consult. Browser vendors also
use this data
to prioritize focus areas and inform their roadmaps.
When will the results be released?
The survey will run from July 15 to August 15, 2025, and the survey results will be released around September 15, 2025.
Who runs this survey?
This survey is run by
Devographics
together with a collective of contributors, translators, and volunteers.
How was this survey designed?
This survey was designed as the results of an
open design process
involving browser vendors and the web development community.

data.title: Tony Hoare on record handling. (1966) [pdf]
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hoare的观点在其实践性和历史背景下的适用性

不同观点：
• FrankWilhoit部分认同Hoare的观点，认为Hoare的许多看法是正确的，但指出其中许多在Hoare所处时代的机器上是不切实际的，主要是由于资源不足。
• 有人认为即使后来资源不再成为限制因素，Hoare的原则也未被重新审视和应用，主要原因是这些原则的实施会要求对运行中的系统进行破坏性的更改。

补充讨论：
• Hoare的观点虽有前瞻性，但在其提出时缺乏实际操作性，导致在技术条件成熟后也未被广泛采纳。
• 讨论中提到技术和资源限制对理论和实践之间差距的影响，表明即使有价值的理论也可能因其实施成本过高而被搁置。
• 争议的焦点在于Hoare的原则是否应在资源充足的现代被重新评估和应用，以及实施这些原则是否仍然过于 disruptive（具有破坏性）。

不同观点：
• **时尚与美学优先**：设计师为了保持女性服装的“女性化”轮廓，避免加入口袋，担心口袋会影响服装的外观和线条。这种设计选择反映了时尚界对女性身材美学的传统标准和偏见。[1][3][5]

• **历史性别角色**：从17世纪开始，男性服装普遍有了口袋，而女性服装则往往没有。这是因为社会普遍认为女性不需要携带物品，特别是金钱和钥匙等，这些由男性负责管理。这种设计反映了历史上的性别不平等和性别角色分工。[2][4][5]

• **社会控制论**：有证据显示，在某些历史时期（如法国大革命期间），女性被禁止使用口袋，以限制她们携带或隐藏物品的能力，这反映了当时社会对女性独立性和流动性的控制意图。[5][6]

• **经济因素与配饰产业**：有人认为，限制女性服装口袋的设计是为了推动女性购买手袋和钱包，从而维持配饰市场的需求。一些品牌通过销售手袋获得的利润高于在服装中加入口袋的成本，这种商业策略已延续多年。[5]

• **成本节约**：加入功能性口袋可能会增加材料和生产时间，因此一些品牌选择使用较小或假口袋来节省成本。不过，这仅是问题的一部分，更深层次的原因与历史传统和社会观念有关。[5]

补充讨论：
• **传统的延续**：尽管在现代社会中女性的地位和角色发生了变化，但女性服装的口袋设计仍然落后于男性服装，许多专家认为这是过时的设计习惯和性别化的时尚思维的延续。[4][5]

争议焦点：
• **性别不平等的反映**：评论中对女性服装缺乏口袋的现象是否反映了深层次的性别歧视和社会对女性独立性的限制存在争议。部分观点认为现代时尚设计应更注重实用性和平等，而非延续历史上的性别偏见。[1][2][5][6]

• **时尚与功能的平衡**：时尚界在设计女性服装时，是否应更多考虑功能性（如增加实用口袋）而不是仅仅追求美学效果，这也是一个讨论的焦点。[3][5]

What starts with a P and ends with an S that every single woman dreams about? POCKETS!
Real world pocket CTA in store!
We pulled data from Semrush to make this point: people want pockets!  It took us a few minutes to do this data-dive that reveals an enormous, untapped market. Across just four main clothing categories, there is a combined total of over
257,300 monthly searches
for items with pockets. This staggering volume confirms that pockets are not a minor detail but a primary, non-negotiable purchasing criterion for hundreds of thousands of shoppers.
Key Finding: Market Demand Exceeds a Quarter of a Million Monthly Searches
Pockets Breakdown by Clothing Category
Checking Semrush quickly, we can see that shorts, dresses, skirts and women's pants are sought with pockets. The demand is not evenly distributed. "Shorts" are the clear leader, accounting for over half of the total search volume. There’s a caveat: this specific query is gender-neutral. Men also want shorts with pockets. They want shorts with pockets with such an intensity that they represent almost 50% of the shorts category we looked at.
This is likely driven by athletic and lifestyle needs, as evidenced by top keywords. We have some running shorts, biking shorts, gym shorts, running shorts, you name it! Disclaimer: we did some back of the napkin data analysis. We’re not paid for this, we just want pockets! However, if you are curious like us (and want pockets), check out this table breaking down the top monthly searches for each category:
Clothing Category
Total Monthly Search Volume
Top Commercial Keywords
Shorts
143,800
biker shorts with pockets (1.9K), running shorts with phone pocket (1.9K), bike shorts with pockets (1.6K)
Dresses
75,300
dress with pockets (1.9K), dresses with pockets (1.9K), black dress with pockets (720)
Skirts
24,500
skirts with pockets (1.0K), skirt with pockets (720), maxi skirt with pockets (590)
Pants
13,700
women's cargo pants with pockets (590), women's pants with pockets (480), women's yoga pants with pockets (480)
The Strategic Implications of Pockets
The data reveals more than just volume; it exposes user intent, frustration, and a clear path to higher conversions if you help customers find clothing items with pockets.
High Commercial Intent
: Shoppers use specific, long-tail keywords like
running shorts with phone pocket
and
biker shorts with pockets
. This shows they are actively looking for a solution to a specific need and are ready to buy.
Active User Frustration
: Search queries for pants include questions like
why do women's pants not have pockets
. This is a direct signal from the market that a core need is being consistently ignored, creating an opportunity for any brand that listens.
DIY Intent Proves It's a "Must-Have"
: For dresses and skirts, users are searching for instructions on
how to add pockets to a dress
(260 monthly searches). When customers are willing to perform alterations themselves, it proves the feature is a necessity, not just a preference.
Clear SEO & UX Mandate
: This data provides an undeniable business case. Creating dedicated filters, categories, and landing pages for clothing "with pockets" is the most direct way to capture this high-intent traffic, improve the user experience, and increase sales.
We really, really, really want pockets. It bears repeating.
Build the "Pockets" Filter Now
Given the high search volume for women's clothing with pockets, particularly in categories like shorts and dresses, online clothing brands should implement a pocket filter in their women's section. This filter would cater to the substantial number of shoppers actively seeking garments with pockets, as evidenced by specific search terms like "running shorts with phone pocket" and "dress with pockets." Implementing such a filter would significantly improve user experience, streamline the shopping process for customers with this specific need, and likely increase conversion rates by directly addressing a key purchasing criterion.
We advise you to create landing pages or category pages for men’s shorts with pockets.

data.title: Examining mushrooms under microscopes helps engineers design stronger materials
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了通过研究蘑菇的微观结构来启发设计更坚固的材料。重点研究了白色纽扣蘑菇和舞茸这两种可食用蘑菇的菌丝网络。研究发现，菌丝（hyphae）的排列方式对其宏观强度有重要影响。白色纽扣蘑菇的菌丝较薄且交错排列，弹性约为18兆帕，类似于天然橡胶。而舞茸具有两种菌丝，其中较厚的骨骼菌丝平行排列，使其硬度达到560兆帕，接近高密度聚乙烯的硬度。计算机模型进一步证明，改变菌丝的角度可以调控材料的强度，而不需要改变其化学成分。这种研究有助于开发环保的强韧材料。
